title: The Welfare State Matrix: An Architectural Diagnosis of the German Welfare State

detail.title: The Welfare State Matrix: An Architectural Diagnosis of the German Welfare State

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is himself active, as Managing Director of KyberMedis GmbH (Berlin), in the field of municipal care architecture, in particular in the planning and support of medical care centres and primary-care centres in municipal sponsorship. The architectural diagnosis developed in this paper thus touches a field of application in which the author is at the same time operationally active as a consultant. The analytical argument of the paper is conceived independently of this; it takes no side for any specific form of sponsorship and makes the conflict of interest expressly transparent here for reasons of scholarly transparency.

detail.abstract:
Over the past three decades, the German welfare state has undergone more reforms than in the five decades before — and in the process has not stabilised but destabilised. This paper advances the thesis that the structural cause of recurrent reform crises lies not primarily in demography, scarcity of funding or a shortage of skilled personnel, but in the systematic conflation of four welfare-state logics: Insurance (collective, contribution-based), Social Assistance (individual, tax-based), Public Provision (collective, tax-based, territorially anchored) and Market (individual, premium-based).

The Welfare State Matrix develops an analytical diagnostic model — not an empirical causal model. Methodologically it follows the construction of ideal types in the Weberian sense (Weber, 1922) and makes visible where the effect of welfare-state reform is systematically absorbed by structural logic breaks. The analysis shows that exemplary fields of reform — the contribution-based health-insurance cover of recipients of Germany’s means-tested minimum income support system (Bürgergeld), the capacity funding of hospitals, the interface between statutory and private health insurance, and the structures of primary care — display a consistent pathology: at each of these points incompatible logics meet without the conflation having been resolved in architectural terms. In the case of the primary-care centre this pathology appears in especially concentrated form — here all four logics converge at the level of a single care institution. Reform efforts fail less because of an absence of political will than because of this unresolved structural conflation.

International reference systems show that architectural clarification is not only practically feasible but leads to structurally more stable and demonstrably more capable care systems: the Netherlands, with the separation — established since 2006 — of the Zorgverzekeringswet, the Wet langdurige zorg and the Wet maatschappelijke ondersteuning, whose reformed system held leading positions in international performance comparisons for years; and the Swedish system, with its regional tax funding. The paper proposes a Welfare State Architecture Act on the model of regulatory framework legislation, a parallel restructuring of the Social Code (Sozialgesetzbuch) along the four logics, and a step-by-step clarification strategy directed at the most costly logic breaks. The Welfare State Matrix makes this architectural clarification possible; it is not itself a reform programme but supplies the hitherto unstated precondition for the success of any such programme.

reference: Santos MA, Morales-Arilla J, Cornielles ZP. From Collective Punishment to Constraints on Authority: Rethinking the Impact of US Sanctions on Venezuela. Cambridge University Press; 2026.
title: From Collective Punishment to Constraints on Authority: Rethinking the Impacts of US Sanctions on Venezuela
affiliations: Instituto Tecnologico y de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey - Escuela de Gobierno y Transformación Pública, Tecnológico de Monterrey and Harvard University

detail.title: From Collective Punishment to Constraints on Authority: Rethinking the Impacts of US Sanctions on Venezuela

publicationDetails.detailsText: Santos MA, Morales-Arilla J, Cornielles ZP. From Collective Punishment to Constraints on Authority: Rethinking the Impact of US Sanctions on Venezuela. Cambridge University Press; 2026.

detail.abstract: This Element critically examines the claim that United States economic sanctions on Venezuela constituted “collective punishment” of the Venezuelan population, contributing significantly to the country’s economic collapse and humanitarian crisis. Through comprehensive analysis of economic, developmental, and welfare indicators from 2013 to 2023, it demonstrates that the bulk of Venezuela’s economic devastation – including 52 percent of GDP losses and 98 percent of import declines – largely occurred before financial sanctions were imposed in August 2017. Key welfare indicators such as infant mortality, undernourishment, and life expectancy had deteriorated substantially by 2017 and subsequently stabilized or improved following sanctions implementation, contradicting narratives that attribute Venezuela’s collapse primarily to external economic pressure. The Element provides a timeline of Venezuelan economic and political events around sanctions and a critical review of the literature on their economic effects.

title: Online Multi-Slice Task Allocation in Multi-UAV Networks
affiliations: Wuhan University, City University of Hong Kong (CityU), affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Wuhan University

detail.title: Online Multi-Slice Task Allocation in Multi-UAV Networks
detail.abstract: UAV network slicing enables flexible, task-oriented resource allocation. However, most current deployments lack true slicing support and face scalability and coordination challenges. Existing methods fail to jointly handle multi-type tasks, UAV deadlines, and hierarchical bandwidth quotas, leading to suboptimal welfare in dynamic environments. We study QoS-aware resource allocation in multi-UAV networks, with the objective of maximizing social welfare. We present a holistic mechanism called Advanced Dynamic Slicing and Task Allocation that supports per-task cross-slice orchestration and per-UAV multi-slice service under per-UAV capacity, coverage, and deadline constraints; we design an online primal–dual algorithm with a dual subroutine that prices multi-slice demands and applies a unit-cost heuristic (travel cost amortized by multi-slice bandwidth requirement) to select feasible UAVs; and we reformulate the integer program to capture travel constraints, bidding prices, and slice-level quotas, using complementary-slackness guidance for real-time task acceptance and resource allocation. In contrast to existing online primal–dual or auction-based UAV schedulers, the proposed mechanism explicitly combines (i) per-UAV concurrent multi-slice service, (ii) per-task cross-slice composition, and (iii) travel-cost-aware deadline constraints in a single optimization and algorithmic framework. Our duality analysis establishes a one-to-one correspondence between dual solutions and primal allocations, ensuring feasible online decisions. Empirical studies verify consistent performance gains, achieving about 10\% higher social welfare than other allocation baselines. We also discuss modeling assumptions, economic interpretation, and limitations, providing a clearer positioning of the proposed mechanism relative to prior work and outlining directions for further empirical validation.

title: Exploiting Structural Properties of the Allocation Subproblem in Emergency Logistics Center Location: A Dominance-Preserving Decoder and Heuristic-Priority Discrete PSO
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Beijing Union University

detail.title: Exploiting Structural Properties of the Allocation Subproblem in Emergency Logistics Center Location: A Dominance-Preserving Decoder and Heuristic-Priority Discrete PSO
detail.abstract: Urban flood disasters create urgent location–allocation decisions for emergency logistics systems, where facility opening, split demand service, heterogeneous vehicle assignment, and time-critical delivery must be coordinated under disrupted road conditions. Existing studies mainly accelerate such problems by tuning metaheuristic search operators, while the structural parameters of the embedded allocation problem are rarely used to guide solution evaluation.This paper develops a scenario-based mixed-integer programming model for flood emergency logistics center location–allocation and proposes a problem-structure-driven decoder embedded in a discrete particle swarm optimization framework (H-SDPSO). The model minimizes expected total cost, including facility construction, trip-based transportation, and overtime penalties, while explicitly incorporating split service, heterogeneous fleet capacity, a hard response horizon, and a soft regular-working-time budget.Methodologically, two decoder-level priority rules are derived from model parameters: (i) a proximity-based center-scanning rule, locally justified under monotone road-impedance conditions, and (ii) a dynamic saving-score vehicle-assignment rule, supported by an exchange argument showing dominance preservation for vehicle-type assignment.A case study using official Zhengzhou statistical data shows that H-SDPSO attains relative gaps of 4.03% (F1) and 0.81% (F2) against exact CPLEX solutions under the 28-disaster-point setting. Sensitivity analysis further shows that when affected points increase from 23 to 56 and the speed coefficient decreases from 1.2 to 0.6, total cost rises from 11.05 million to 43.63 million CNY. The results indicate that balanced fleet structures and stable high-frequency candidate centers improve flood-response preparedness, and that model-level decoder design can complement conventional search-level metaheuristic improvement.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Household Risky Financial Market Participation: Evidence from China's Frontier Regions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Guangxi University

detail.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Household Risky Financial Market Participation: Evidence from China's Frontier Regions
detail.abstract: This study explores the impact of generative artificial intelligence (AI) on household participation in risky financial markets. Using micro-level data from the 2025 Frontier Economics Database Household Survey, we find that generative AI significantly increases both the probability of participating in risky financial markets and the proportion of risky financial assets held. Mechanism analysis reveals that generative AI influences participation primarily by alleviating information and borrowing constraints. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the impact of generative AI is more pronounced for households with lower human and physical capital, as well as those residing in regions characterized by either high cultural diversity or border proximity. Furthermore, generative AI and digital inclusive finance exhibit a complementary relationship, working synergistically to improve household financial decision-making. These findings enrich the existing literature on the role of Generative AI in household asset allocation decisions.

title: A Biological Basis For Experiential Utility: Relief and Comfort

detail.title: A Biological Basis For Experiential Utility: Relief and Comfort
detail.abstract: This paper develops a biological interpretation of experiential utility by decomposing experiential value into relief-oriented and comfort-oriented components. Standard economic models typically represent utility as a unified scalar function in which increases in consumption or wealth generate positive utility through a common mechanism. In contrast, the present framework argues that the alleviation of deprivation and the acquisition of positive comfort may arise through partially distinct motivational and organismic processes. The paper integrates evidence from behavioral economics, psychology, stress physiology, and affective neuroscience suggesting that organisms respond asymmetrically to negative and positive experiential states. Deprivation reduction, threat attenuation, and stress relief often exhibit greater salience, urgency, and behavioral dominance than equivalent increases in comfort or pleasure. Building on this asymmetry, the paper proposes that relief utility arises primarily through the reduction of deprivation, instability, pain, stress, and organismic dysregulation, while comfort utility arises primarily through positive enhancement, experiential ease, satiation, and enrichment. The framework provides a compositional interpretation of diminishing marginal utility, arguing that the flattening of marginal utility may partly reflect a shift from highly salient relief-oriented utility generation toward lower-salience comfort-oriented utility generation as material deprivation declines. The paper also examines implications for scarcity, poverty, well-being, consumption behavior, and subjective welfare measurement. The paper also contributes to a broader compositional theory of utility in which utility is interpreted as arising from multiple distinct underlying mechanisms rather than from a single homogeneous process. At a wider level, the paper contributes to a growing interdisciplinary literature integrating economics with psychology and biology while preserving the analytical structure of economic utility theory. The central contribution of the paper is to provide a biologically grounded framework for interpreting experiential utility as internally compositional rather than homogeneous.

title: Goal-Based Wealth Management Beyond Accumulation: Ruin Avoidance and Tie-Breaking on U.S. Data
affiliations: AMGSM-IAE Aix-en-Provence, Aix Marseille University, CERGAM

detail.title: Goal-Based Wealth Management Beyond Accumulation: Ruin Avoidance and Tie-Breaking on U.S. Data
detail.abstract: We extend the static multiperiod Goal-BasedWealth Management (GBWM)algorithm of Das et al. (2018), as implemented by Simonato (2025) on U.S.accumulation data, to the full retirement life cycle by incorporating a 25-yeardecumulation phase with periodic withdrawals and a ruin boundary. Usingnon-parametric bootstrap simulations on U.S. real return data (S&P 500with dividends reinvested, 10-year Treasury bond, 3-month T-bill, 1962-2025), we compare three tie-breaking rules (min_risk, intermediate, andmax_return) across four life-cycle scenarios indexed by the withdrawal-to-contribution ratio ω = Wd/A ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5}. Our findings are threefold. First,within this static implementation, GBWM achieves ruin rates of 0.1-5.9%against 0.4-23.6% (TDF) and 0.8-19.2% (MV) across all scenarios, regard-less of the tie-breaking rule. Second, the tie-breaking rule is quasi-immaterialfor ruin rates but decisive for terminal wealth: max_return delivers meanterminal wealth 5.9× to 9.8× higher than min_risk at identical ruin rates,with the ratio monotonically increasing as ω declines. Third, a two-regimemechanism explains this divergence: during accumulation the solvency cri-terion retains discriminating power, while at retirement ties expand to up to15 tied portfolios with return spreads reaching 6.9%, transferring effectivecontrol to the tie-breaking rule throughout the 25-year decumulation phase.

title: Persistence and innovation in the momentum signal
affiliations: Sungkyunkwan University

detail.title: Persistence and innovation in the momentum signal
detail.abstract: By separating the momentum indicator into a predictable persistent component and a forecast-error innovation, we examine how each component contributes to the momentum premium. The persistent component absorbs most of the momentum profit, challenging a pure transitory-mispricing interpretation of momentum. The innovation component earns a smaller positive premium, concentrated among non-extreme momentum stocks but reversed at the extremes.​

title: Imagining biodiversity-respectful food system futures
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Imagining biodiversity-respectful food system futures
detail.abstract: Future imaginaries shape societal pathways by framing what kinds of change is considered desirable, feasible, and legitimate. When collectively shared, such narratives can reinforce dominant trajectories or open space for transformative change. In food systems, imaginaries are particularly salient given the urgent need to halt biodiversity decline alongside persistent disagreements over how this should be achieved. This study examines the imaginaries underpinning land sparing and land sharing as contrasting land use strategies for promoting biodiversity within food systems. Although increasingly presented as complementary, their paradigmatic and ontological foundations remain poorly understood. Drawing on a series of futures workshops with key stakeholders of the Finnish food system, this study explores how sparing and sharing imaginaries are articulated, what elements they comprise, and which underlying ontologies shape them. The analysis reveals that while the imaginaries share certain surface-level goals, they diverge markedly in their assumptions about food system’s institutional structures and human–nature relations. The sparing imaginary largely reinforces existing food system structures and relies on top-down control, whereas the sharing imaginary challenges prevailing institutional arrangements and emphasises collective, bottom-up agency. By making these underlying orientations visible, the study helps explain why food system transformation often remains incremental despite widespread recognition of the biodiversity crisis. The findings contribute to research on food system futures by demonstrating how imaginaries can function as a bridging concept between future visions and deeper paradigmatic foundations, and by providing analytical orientation for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners navigating competing pathways towards biodiversity-respectful food systems.

reference: Banking and Finance Law Review, Volume 40, No. 3, Pp. 517-523; 2024
title: Book review: Digital Assets and the Law: Fiat Money in the Era of Digital Currency
affiliations: University of Glasgow - School of Law

detail.title: Book review: Digital Assets and the Law: Fiat Money in the Era of Digital Currency

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banking and Finance Law Review, Volume 40, No. 3, Pp. 517-523; 2024

detail.abstract: In the wake of the unprecedented challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, a group of scholars from the Blockchains and Artificial intelligence for Business, Economics and Law (BABEL) research team within the Department of Economics and Management (DiSEI) at the University of Florence embarked on a research journey that culminated in the creation of "Digital Assets and the Law: Fiat Money in the Era of Digital Currency." The genesis of this work lies in webinars held in December 2020 and November of the same year, exploring the roles of fiat currencies and digital assets. The subsequent research project, led by the co-editors Filippo Zatti and Rosa Giovanna Barresi, bringing together diverse scholars and perspectives, underscores the transdisciplinary nature of the book. Such a broad range of authors and expertise that contributed to this joint venture, facilitated by the extensive network of the Digital Euro Association (DEA), adds credibility to the collaborative effort. The book delves into the intricate landscape of digital currencies, with a particular focus on the digital euro, while analyzing similar ventures all around the world. This evolution in the ecosystem of currencies and payments has been labelled as a "liberalization" and compared to the introduction of competition in China's economic model in terms of a breakthrough novelty for the global banking and financial system for the years to come.

title: Bridging Renewable Intermittency and Steady State Demand: Optimizing Capacity Configuration for Scalable Green Ammonia
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhejiang University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Bridging Renewable Intermittency and Steady State Demand: Optimizing Capacity Configuration for Scalable Green Ammonia
detail.abstract: Green ammonia (NH3), an essential base chemical with vast demand and a promising carbon-free energy carrier and fuel, demands an urgent transition towards low-carbon production via renewable electrification. However, the inherent intermittency and fluctuation of renewable power conflict with the steady-state operation required by conventional NH3 synthesis. This mismatch represents a critical barrier to its techno-economic viability and large-scale industrialization. Herein, we propose an optimal capacity configuration strategy that integrates multi-stage smoothing of renewable power fluctuations with flexible regulation of the NH3 synthesis process. Based on a 3000 t yr-1 demonstration project designed in Inner Mongolia as the model, the variations of energy and mass flows reveal the specific electricity consumption increasing from 10.95 kWh kg NH3-1 at high load to 19.38 kWh kg NH3-1 at low load. By optimizing the capacity configuration of key system modules, a minimum levelized cost of 3561 RMB t NH3-1 was achieved. Compared to the conventional coal-based NH3 route, flexible green NH3 system can save 1.57 tce t NH3-1 and reduce 4.35 tCO2e t NH3-1. With future improvements in carbon tax policies and technological advances, the cost of green NH3 is projected to decrease by an additional 697 RMB t NH3-1 and 1007 RMB t NH3-1, respectively, validating its promising prospects for large-scale commercialization.

title: Score Clipping in Classical Music Competitions: Structural Pathologies and Evidence From Chopin 2025
affiliations: Skidmore College, University of Miami Frost School of Music and Merope

detail.title: Score Clipping in Classical Music Competitions: Structural Pathologies and Evidence From Chopin 2025
detail.abstract: The CMEAN method clips individual juror scores to a band around each contestant's cross-juror arithmetic mean. This paper identifies three structural failures of this rule. First, CMEAN channels strategic behaviour towards the endpoints of the scale at the point of reporting. Second, under ordinary differences in scale use, it can reverse expressed juror preferences or even change the winner. Third, as a score-by-score correction rule, it can miss distributed profile-level manipulation while compressing sincere isolated differentiation. Using data from the 19th International Chopin Piano Competition (2025), we find that CMEAN altered juror-specific rankings in 60.7% of cases in Stage 1 and 67.2% in Stage 2, and reversed 1,856 strict pairwise preferences across the competition. Monte Carlo simulations calibrated to the Chopin score matrix show systematic costs in honest panels, little benefit under weak manipulation, and usefulness only when manipulation is already blunt and visible. The concern motivating correction in high-stakes panel evaluation is legitimate; candidate-wise mean-centred clipping is a fragile, parameter-sensitive response.

title: Re-Keying the Synaptic Replication Crisis: A Local Credit Assignment Framework for Deterministic Neuromodulation

detail.title: Re-Keying the Synaptic Replication Crisis: A Local Credit Assignment Framework for Deterministic Neuromodulation
detail.abstract:
The development of neurotechnologies and psychiatric treatments is systematically bottlenecked by a fundamental limitation: deep-brain stimulation (DBS), closed-loop neuromodulation, and brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) approximate brain states instead of calculating exact boundary constraints. This mirrors the pharmaceutical replication crisis—a $28 billion problem where irreproducibility stems from method contamination, not physics. We identify the synaptic replication crisis: the inability to reliably map synthetic interfaces or stimulation parameters to organic neural pathways across subjects, sessions, and devices.

​The root cause is the same 40-year backpropagation bottleneck that has limited deep learning—the Weight Transport Problem, Update Locking, and Vanishing/Exploding Gradients now manifest in biological neural networks. This work does not claim to present new empirical neurophysiological datasets or propose alternative mechanisms of synaptic plasticity. Rather, it introduces the Local Credit Assignment Framework (LCAF), a computational metrology infrastructure adapted for deterministic neuromodulation, whose three axes map directly to known biological credit assignment mechanisms:

  1. ​Neuromodulatory broadcast signals as approximate teaching signals,

  1. ​Dendritic compartment error computation as local loss architecture, and

  1. ​Predictive coding circuits as non-sequential credit assignment.

​The framework proves that neurological network refinement can occur deterministically in real-time without massive computational overhead. Adversarial feedback simulation (8 iterations to fixed point) demonstrates convergence across neurochemical pathways. Falsifiable predictions include: LCAF-compliant neuromodulation achieves >90\% replication success across subjects versus the current <30\% benchmark.

title: DeepMPRA: A novel deep learning framework for global microplastics risk assessment in lacustrine ecosystems
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Chengdu Institute of Biology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Chengdu Institute of Biology, Jishou University, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Chengdu Institute of Biology, Tsinghua University, University of Zagreb, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Jishou University and Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Chengdu Institute of Biology

detail.title: DeepMPRA: A novel deep learning framework for global microplastics risk assessment in lacustrine ecosystems
detail.abstract: Lakes are critical freshwater resources threatened by microplastic (MP) pollution globally. Current ecological risk assessment for microplastics relies on linear index systems that require arbitrary background values and assume additive effects among plastic properties, potentially missing the nonlinear interactions that influence real-world hazard. Using a global lake dataset (283 lakes across 23 countries), we developed DeepMPRA, a deep learning framework that learns risk thresholds directly from data without predefined background values. DeepMPRA integrates generative data augmentation, an autoencoder for nonlinear feature extraction, and unsupervised clustering to define risk as deviation from a learned low-risk reference. Conventional methods and DeepMPRA produced discordant classifications for 57% of samples: classical approaches overestimated risk for very low abundance samples (classifying them as moderate risk) and underestimated risk for samples with high-risk combinations of abundance, small particle size, and hazardous polymers (classifying them as low risk). DeepMPRA identifies abundance, particle size, and polymer type as the primary risk determinants. Globally, pronounced spatial heterogeneity emerged: Spain, Indonesia, and Turkey showed the highest MP abundances, while Russia and Mongolia maintained the lowest levels. Moreover, the framework uncovers karst lakes as unexpected high-risk hotspots (very high to extremely high risk), a vulnerability linked to groundwater-dominated recharge, polyethylene terephthalate dominance, and elevated proportions of fibers and sub-millimeter particles. Explainable machine learning highlights cropland, seawater, and wetland as the most sensitive land-use drivers, with univariate sensitivity analysis validating their influence. DeepMPRA offers a threshold-free, nonlinear paradigm for microplastic risk assessment applicable across aquatic ecosystems.

reference: Islamic Finance News Volume 22 Issue 12, on 26 March 2025
title: The UAE's Quiet Masterstroke: Turning Islamic Finance From a Niche Into a Global Force
affiliations: Maalexi Inc.

detail.title: The UAE's Quiet Masterstroke: Turning Islamic Finance From a Niche Into a Global Force
detail.abstract:
This article examines the structural transformation of Islamic finance from an ethical niche into a globally competitive asset class, with particular focus on the United Arab Emirates as its most consequential architect. Drawing on data from the ICD-LSEG Islamic Finance Development Report 2024, Fitch Ratings, S&P Global, the Central Bank of the UAE, and the Global Islamic Fintech Report 2024/25, we identify three interlocking mechanisms through which the UAE has built and sustained its leadership position: the construction of a deep, diversified institutional ecosystem; the development of a world-leading Sukuk market — notably in ESG-linked instruments — underpinned by coherent regulatory incentives; and the emergence of a mature Islamic fintech infrastructure addressing long-standing gaps in Shariah-compliant finance delivery.


Our central argument is that the UAE's success is not the product of cultural or religious factors alone, but of a deliberate strategic reframing: from Islamic finance as an obligation to Islamic finance as a competitive asset. This reframing expressed in regulatory architecture, capital market design, and fintech ecosystem building, has attracted capital and participants well beyond the traditional Islamic finance community. The article identifies two material gaps that remain: below-peer Financial Performance and Sustainability scores in the IFDI, which constrain the sector's appeal to the most demanding international capital. We conclude that the direction of travel is unambiguous, and that the case for engaging with Islamic finance instruments, on financial merit alone, is now sufficiently evidenced to demand serious consideration from institutional investors, financial institutions, and policymakers globally.

title: How Earning Fixes Everything Paper 7 of 10: The Demand-Side Paradox Series
affiliations: Humanix

detail.title: How Earning Fixes Everything Paper 7 of 10: The Demand-Side Paradox Series

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Founder and CEO of Humanix, an economic architecture proposed as one response to the issues raised in this paper series.

detail.abstract: Paper 7 of the Demand-Side Paradox series. Argues that income distribution is an economic efficiency question, not just an equity one. The marginal propensity to consume differential between US wealth quintiles is 14.5 to 1; the GiveDirectly Kenya randomized controlled trial documented a 2.5x multiplier; productivity has outpaced typical compensation by 2.7 to 1 over 40 years; labor share sits at a 78-year low. Together these point to one conclusion: the AI economy fails when concentrated income destroys the demand base every firm depends on. Only re-earning within the AI value chain breaks the feedback loop.

title: A Public-Data Framework for Monitoring Corporate Credit-Line Utilization: Evidence from U.S. Banking Data and Loan Officer Surveys

detail.title: A Public-Data Framework for Monitoring Corporate Credit-Line Utilization: Evidence from U.S. Banking Data and Loan Officer Surveys

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. The views expressed in this paper are solely those of the author and do not represent any employer, institution, or organization. The analysis uses publicly available data and independently prepared code. No confidential, proprietary, or employer-specific data are used.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it uses only publicly available aggregate financial, banking, macroeconomic, and survey data. The study does not involve human subjects, patients, private individual-level data, or personally identifiable information.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a public-data framework for monitoring and forecasting corporate credit-line utilization in the U.S. banking system. Because bank-internal utilization measures are generally proprietary, the paper constructs a reproducible aggregate utilization proxy using public data, defined as commercial and industrial loans divided by the sum of commercial and industrial loans and unused loan commitments. The proxy is interpreted as a public drawn-share measure of aggregate committed corporate credit exposure, making it relevant for credit exposure monitoring, drawdown-risk analysis, and stress testing. The empirical analysis combines this utilization proxy with macro-financial variables and the Federal Reserve's Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices. The main specification models quarterly changes in utilization as a function of lagged utilization changes and lagged C&I loan demand reported by loan officers. Using quarterly data beginning in 1997 and an out-of-sample evaluation period beginning in 2017, the parsimonious AR(1) plus SLOOS demand model achieves an out-of-sample utilization-level MAE of 0.0038 and RMSE of 0.0063. Adding lagged SLOOS C&I loan demand materially improves forecast accuracy relative to an autoregressive benchmark, while broader macro-financial controls, including credit spreads, industrial production, and lending standards, provide limited additional improvement. Forecast-loss comparisons indicate that the main model significantly reduces absolute forecast errors relative to both the no-change and AR(1) benchmarks. The model captures the broad post-2021 decline in utilization but underpredicts the acute COVID liquidity spike, with COVID-window MAE approximately 3.6 times the full out-of-sample MAE. These findings suggest that public loan officer survey information contains meaningful predictive content for corporate credit-line utilization, while also highlighting model risk associated with acute stress-period forecasting.

title: Demand Forecasting for Low-Volume, High-Variability Medical SKUs in Small Independent Healthcare Practices: A Methodological Framework

detail.title: Demand Forecasting for Low-Volume, High-Variability Medical SKUs in Small Independent Healthcare Practices: A Methodological Framework
detail.abstract: Forecasting demand for low-volume, high-variability medical SKUs in small independent healthcare practices is methodologically distinct from hospital-scale or large-retail demand forecasting. At the practice-SKU level, histories are short and sparse, consumption patterns are intermittent, and structural breaks are common as clinical protocols evolve, suppliers substitute, and national shortages propagate to the point of care. This paper develops a forecasting methodology framework tailored to that setting. The framework combines classical statistical forecasting with machine-learning approaches and treats regime shifts as first-class objects through drift detection, model-refresh triggers, and conservative fallbacks during transitions. Operational signals are integrated as exogenous covariates, and forecasts are produced as full predictive distributions rather than point estimates. The methodology has been validated through production deployment across U.S. independent practices spanning medical aesthetic, wellness, weight-management, and dermatology-adjacent settings; empirical observations indicate stable accuracy, reduced manual ordering effort, and lower waste and stockout frequency. The contribution is a forecasting framework adapted to the operational and statistical realities of the small-practice setting.

title: Green Bonds and Environmental Outcomes: Inferential Conditions for Interpreting Cross-Country Evidence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Green Bonds and Environmental Outcomes: Inferential Conditions for Interpreting Cross-Country Evidence
detail.abstract: This paper asks how much can be learned from cross-country comparisons between green-bond issuance and environmental outcomes. The main problem is that issuer countries are not evenly distributed, so the effective estimating sample is narrower than the global panel suggests. The study uses a 2017-2023 panel covering 217 economies and 1,519 country-year observations before outcome and moderator restrictions. In the FAOSTAT-main benchmark, 83 of the 141 countries with moderator coverage issue green bonds at least once. Issuance is concentrated among richer economies: 97.2% of countries in the top GDP quartile issue at least once, compared with 45.7% outside that group. This imbalance matters because it determines which observations identify the fixed-effects estimates. The clearest composite-index pattern appears in the Water Quality Index. The air and forest indices do not show the same relationship. The water result is also support-constrained. It is estimated from 162 observations, 30 countries, and four issuer-HighDep countries. The result is best read as a benchmark-specific water-domain association, not as causal evidence that green bonds improve environmental outcomes.

title: Rethinking the Wealth Distribution Function of Work in the Age of AI: Toward a Population-Based Risk-Commitment Standard

detail.title: Rethinking the Wealth Distribution Function of Work in the Age of AI: Toward a Population-Based Risk-Commitment Standard

declarations.declarationOfInterest: nil
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: nil

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence and automation are expanding society's capacity to create wealth while undermining work's traditional function of distributing that wealth. If capital monopolizes the gains, the market's purchasing power base will erode. This paper diagnoses this decoupling of creation from distribution and critiques existing responses-Universal Basic Income (UBI) and Modern Monetary Theory (MMT)-for their respective shortcomings. Building on the author's prior work, the paper proposes a population-based risk-commitment standard that shares UBI's distributional insight while adding a monetary anchor and a voluntary risk upgrade mechanism. The anchor of money shifts from labor to survival risk. The mechanism has two layers: basic risk self-retention (individuals receive currency and bear the consequences of their spending) and excess risk socialization (a social risk pool covers catastrophic losses). Individuals may voluntarily upgrade their risk exposure-accepting a higher deductible for higher monthly issuance. The mechanism operates through three channels: (1) initiative as risk-taking, (2) market preservation through distributed purchasing power, and (3) evolutionary dynamism through market selection. The COVID-19 pandemic provided a natural experiment in direct monetary distribution. In 2020-2021, dozens of governments issued cash transfers to households when work temporarily collapsed. While inflation rose significantly in 2021-2022, driven primarily by supply-side factors, it did not escalate into hyperinflation, and the transfers were credited with preventing a deeper recession. This demonstrates that direct monetary distribution is feasible and can be sustainable under crisis conditions. The paper examines Taiwan's Long-Term Care 2.0 program as a working prototype of demand-side anchoring and concludes with policy recommendations for a phased transition. The risk-commitment standard is, in effect, UBI with a risk-reward mechanism and a dual-anchor-a version of basic income designed for an age where initiative, not labor, is the scarce resource.

title: Pain and Gain: The Opioid Crisis and Financial Adviser Misconduct
affiliations: University of South Carolina, Darla Moore School of Business, University of South Carolina - Darla Moore School of Business, Washington State University and University of South Carolina

detail.title: Pain and Gain: The Opioid Crisis and Financial Adviser Misconduct
detail.abstract: We document how the opioid crisis reshapes professional conduct in a domain far removed from public health: financial adviser misconduct. Using transaction-level prescription opioid distribution data merged with adviser misconduct records from 2006 to 2019, we find that a one-standard-deviation increase in county-level per capita oxycodone distribution raises the probability of misconduct by 6 percent relative to the sample mean. The staggered adoption of Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs provides a supply-side shock that reduces misconduct accordingly. The evidence is consistent with a social-norm erosion mechanism: opioid exposure predicts lower local social capital and more first-time violations by previously unblemished advisers.

title: The World Trade Organization: Twenty-Five Structural Failures That Mathematics Exposes. SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 and TRADE-73.5 as a Complete Replacement for the Nominal Trade Paradigm

detail.title: The World Trade Organization: Twenty-Five Structural Failures That Mathematics Exposes. SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 and TRADE-73.5 as a Complete Replacement for the Nominal Trade Paradigm
detail.abstract: This article performs a systematic legal and mathematical audit of the World Trade Organization framework, identifying twenty-five specific structural failures embedded directly in the founding documents of the WTO-the Marrakesh Agreement Establishing the WTO (1994), the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT 1994), the Dispute Settlement Understanding (DSU), the Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures (SCM), the Agreement on Agriculture, the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS), the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), and the Anti-Dumping Agreement. Each failure is identified by the exact document and article. For each structural failure, the corresponding mechanism in SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.8 and its TRADE-73.5 module is shown to provide a mathematically complete and legally superior solution. The conclusion is unambiguous: the WTO failures are not accidental gaps. They are load-bearing elements of a system designed to codify the trade dominance of its founding powers. Only a mathematically deterministic replacement resolves the problem at its architectural root.

title: A Joint Level-Change Classification of a Macro Fear Score: Conditional Return Distributions in U.S. Equities

detail.title: A Joint Level-Change Classification of a Macro Fear Score: Conditional Return Distributions in U.S. Equities
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a two-dimensional classification of macroeconomic stress states and examines the conditional distribution of U.S. equity returns across the resulting joint regimes. The first axis is the level of a macro fear score p bottom , constructed as the linear average of 3-year rolling percentile ranks across four macro series (VIX, 10-year Treasury the dot-com sub-sample as a structurally distinct configuration, separating it from the GFC and COVID-19 sub-samples on the dimension of episode duration relative to the 756-day rolling-window construction of p bottom. The results are framed as descriptive statistics of conditional return distributions, not as forecasts of future returns. We do not claim that the documented regularities will persist beyond the 2026 cutoff , nor that the threshold parameters chosen here are theoretically optimal.

title: No-Arbitrage Shape Restrictions for Zero and Swap Par Yield Curves
affiliations: Fudan University

detail.title: No-Arbitrage Shape Restrictions for Zero and Swap Par Yield Curves
detail.abstract: The yield curve is one of the central objects in fixed-income markets, summarizing borrowing costs and investment returns across maturities. While the economic interpretation of upward-sloping, flat, and inverted curves has been studied extensively, less attention has been paid to a simple structural question: why are observed zero and par yield curves often concave over a substantial maturity range? This paper gives a no-arbitrage explanation based on stylized but economically meaningful curve-shift assumptions. For zero-coupon bonds, a convex zero curve permits a zero-cost butterfly portfolio, long the short and long maturities and short the intermediate maturity, whose value is non-negative under parallel shifts and strictly positive under a non-degeneracy condition. The same argument extends to proportional nonparallel shifts after replacing maturity by the appropriate shiftweighted maturity. For par curves, represented first by annual par swap rates and then by the corresponding market-annuity formulation, the proof is more involved because par rates and discount factors are linked by a nonlinear bootstrap relation. We show that, under parallel par-rate shifts, an increasing par curve plotted against its annuity factor must be concave; otherwise a static par-swap butterfly generates an arbitrage under the assumed shift mechanism. The paper therefore unifies the zero-curve and par-curve versions of the same trading idea: curve convexity is incompatible with no arbitrage when the dominant curve movement is a level shift.

title: Quantity and Quality: A Standard Reporting Framework for Energy Systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Quantity and Quality: A Standard Reporting Framework for Energy Systems
detail.abstract: Energy systems are conventionally reported using scalar energy quantities (joules, kilowatthours, megawatt-hours, quads, barrels-of-oil-equivalent, etc.) or power rates (watts, kilowatts, megawatts). This rst-law convention is simple and universally adopted, yet it systematically conceals the second-law distinction between energy quantity and accessible work potential. Classical exergy analysis restores this distinction, but reference-state dependence, carrier-specic terminology, and cumbersome formulations have prevented it from becoming a routine operational reporting layer in multi-carrier energy systems. This paper introduces a standard two-number reporting framework that closes the gap. Every reported energy quantitywhether primary consumption, delivered electricity, fuel inventory, storage asset, or owing streamis reported as quantity plus Exergy Factor: accumulated energy quantity: (E, f X) power rate: (P, f X) where f X = X A /E = ẊA /P is the accessible exergy per unit energy (or per unit power) evaluated at a declared reporting boundary. The framework denes the carrier-level intensive variable as the exergy voltage, ∆Φ (C) A = dX A /dC, which yields the universal exergy-ow law

title: SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.9: Empirical Validation of a Theoretical Model for Currency Valuation Based on Real Assets and Its Quantum-Physical Foundations, and Why SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.9 Does Not Contradict Nobel Laureates' Theories in Economics and Finance but Complements and Extends Them

detail.title: SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.9: Empirical Validation of a Theoretical Model for Currency Valuation Based on Real Assets and Its Quantum-Physical Foundations, and Why SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.9 Does Not Contradict Nobel Laureates' Theories in Economics and Finance but Complements and Extends Them
detail.abstract: This paper presents a conceptual and empirical verification of the SVWORLD Standard 73.5 v1.9 (CVR73)-a new architecture for assessing the stability of sovereign currencies. Unlike traditional approaches that evaluate only nominal indicators (GDP and debt), this model measures the real resource endowment of economies. The article explains the principles of cleaning national balance sheets from hidden debts and physical depreciation of infrastructure. Based on historical data from 1990-2025, it is proven that the model is capable of predicting major financial crises one to one-and-a-half years before their onset. The deep connection between the behavior of modern financial systems and the laws of quantum physics and thermodynamics is also revealed. For the first time, key economic theories of Nobel laureates are unified and mathematically reconciled within a single model, and a Sovereign Digital Asset (SDA) is proposed as a universal unit of measurement.

title: Bidirectional Spatiotemporal State Space Modeling for Short- and Long-Term Vessel Trajectory Prediction
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Bidirectional Spatiotemporal State Space Modeling for Short- and Long-Term Vessel Trajectory Prediction
detail.abstract: Accurate vessel trajectory prediction is critical for maritime safety, traffic management, and autonomous navigation in complex waters. However, vessel movements are highly nonlinear, dynamically variable, and characterized by long-range spatiotemporal dependencies, which limit the performance of existing methods in both short- and long-term prediction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes BMAG, a vessel trajectory prediction framework that integrates Bidirectional Mamba2, Attention, and GRU. Built on AIS data, BMAG employs an end-to-end encoder-decoder architecture with an input embedding layer, a bidirectional Mamba2 encoder, and an autoregressive GRU decoder with multi-head cross attention. The encoder captures bidirectional spatiotemporal interactions from historical trajectories and fuses contextual information through a learnable weighting mechanism, while the decoder selectively exploits relevant historical states to improve prediction accuracy and stability. Experiments on 2024 AIS datasets from Tampa Bay and the Port of New York show that BMAG consistently outperforms advanced baselines, reducing ADE and FDE by up to 23.5% and 14.6% for 20-min prediction, and by 31.5% and 28.7% for 60-min prediction, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness and robustness of BMAG for multi-horizon vessel trajectory prediction in complex maritime environments.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF MONETARY POLICY IN CONTROLLINGINFLATION IN GHANA:EVIDENCE FROM THE INFLATION TARGETING FRAMEWORK
affiliations: University of Professional Studies, University of Professional Studies and University of Professional Studies

detail.title: EFFECTIVENESS OF MONETARY POLICY IN CONTROLLINGINFLATION IN GHANA:EVIDENCE FROM THE INFLATION TARGETING FRAMEWORK
detail.abstract: This study investigates how effectively monetary policy has managed inflation in Ghana since the country adopted its Inflation Targeting (IT) framework. The motivation behind this work is straightforward: despite nearly two decades of policy interventions by the Bank of Ghana, inflation has remained high and difficult to tame. To get to the bottom of this puzzle, the study draws on annual time-series data spanning 2002 to 2025 and applies the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model, a method well-suited for capturing both short-run dynamics and long-run relationships between variables.The variables under examination include Ghana’s inflation rate, monetary policy rate, exchange rate, broad money supply, and private-sector credit growth. The analysis is grounded in two influential bodies of thought: Monetarist Theory, which traces inflationary pressure directly to money supply growth, and the Keynesian Transmission Mechanism, which describes how policy rate adjustments ripple through the economy to affect prices.The findings paint a nuanced picture. Monetary policy does exert a meaningful influence on inflation; tighter policy reduces price pressures over time, but its effectiveness is noticeably constrained by exchange-rate pass-through and persistent money supply expansion. In other words, the Bank of Ghana’s policy signals are being partially drowned out by structural and external forces. Based on these findings, the study calls for stronger coordination between monetary and fiscal authorities, more robust exchange-rate management, and policy frameworks that build public trust in the central bank’s commitment to price stability.

title: Analysis of Demand and Supply in the Healthcare Sector in Oman between 2020-2024: The Role of Government Intervention and System Efficiency
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Analysis of Demand and Supply in the Healthcare Sector in Oman between 2020-2024: The Role of Government Intervention and System Efficiency
detail.abstract: This study estimated the demand, supply, government interventions, health systems performance, and assessment of the Omani health system between 2020 and 2024. The data for the study were obtained from the NCSI Health Statistics 2025 Report, Oman Vision 2040 Report 2024/2025, World Bank Open Data, and WHO Global Health Expenditure Database between 2020 and 2024. Market structure, demand and supply, qualitative price elasticity analysis, and government intervention are some of the tools applied to analyze the microeconomic aspects of the pharmaceutical industry. The analysis reveals that the healthcare market in Oman is a dominant firm oligopoly where the MOH employs about 70% of all physicians in Oman (NCSI, 2025). There is excess demand, and price elasticity has been estimated at relatively low levels of −0.2 (Manning et al. 1987; Aron-Dine et al. 2013). Thus, healthcare is a necessity good. National health expenditure rose by 14% and capital expenditure tenfold (NCSI, 2025), with overcrowding increasing as evidenced by rising occupancy rates, and a 331% increase in referrals abroad from 2020 to 2024 (390 in 2020, 1682 in 2024). It ranks third (after Qatar and the United Arab Emirates) on a variety of health indicators, compared to other GCC states, and spends a higher percentage of its GDP on health. The report recommended options with trade-off to develop a sustainable health system aligned with Oman Vision 2040 aspirations.

title: Sequential Verification of Large Language Model Outputs: An Operations Research Framework Combining Pandora Optimal Search, CUSUM Quickest Change Detection, and Contextual Bandits

detail.title: Sequential Verification of Large Language Model Outputs: An Operations Research Framework Combining Pandora Optimal Search, CUSUM Quickest Change Detection, and Contextual Bandits
detail.abstract: We propose SEVER (SEquential VERification), a three-layer operations research framework for hallucination detection in large language models (LLMs). Existing detection methods such as semantic entropy (Farquhar et al., 2024) and SelfCheckGPT (Manakul, Liusie, & Gales, 2023) operate as static classifiers on completed responses, ignoring three structural features of the verification problem: (i) verifiers vary materially in cost and informativeness; (ii) hallucinations frequently emerge mid-response as semantic drift rather than uniformly across tokens; and (iii) the appropriate verifier mix depends on query context. SEVER addresses each in turn. Layer 1 applies Weitzman's (1979) Pandora rule to order verification instruments by reservation value, computing optimal stopping policies under heterogeneous compute, latency, and monetary costs. Layer 2 applies the CUSUM quickest-change-detection procedure of Page (1954) to a token-level grounding signal, localising within-response drift with asymptotically optimal detection delay. Layer 3 maintains a contextual Thompson-sampling posterior over verifier effectiveness, enabling per-query-class policy adaptation with logarithmic regret guarantees (Agrawal & Goyal, 2012). We derive sufficient conditions under which the composite decision rule attains prescribed type-I and type-II error rates while minimising expected verification cost. The framework is closed-form for Layer 1, recursive for Layer 2, and Bayesian-incremental for Layer 3, making it deployable as a thin orchestration wrapper around existing LLM serving infrastructure. We outline an empirical evaluation protocol over established benchmarks (TruthfulQA, FActScore, WikiBio-GPT3, HaluEval) and discuss applications in regulated finance (CCD II, FCA Consumer Duty, PRA SS1/23) and defence (UK Dstl, UK AISI) where cost-aware verification is operationally critical. SEVER complements rather than competes with the underlying detectors: any semantic-entropy, SelfCheckGPT, NLI-grounding, retrieval, or LLM-asjudge method becomes a 'box' in the Pandora pool. The contribution is the policy that orchestrates them.

title: Effects of Street Trees on PM2.5 and PM10 Pollution in Summer Hangzhou: A Mobile Monitoring Study with LiDAR and Environmental Sensors​
affiliations: Zhejiang A&F University, Zhejiang A&F University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhejiang A&F University, Zhejiang A&F University, Zhejiang A&F University and Zhejiang Agriculture and Forestry University

detail.title: Effects of Street Trees on PM2.5 and PM10 Pollution in Summer Hangzhou: A Mobile Monitoring Study with LiDAR and Environmental Sensors​
detail.abstract: With rapid urbanization, street trees have become an important part of urban greening. To investigate the effects of street trees on PM2.5 and PM10 pollution in summer in Hangzhou, 29 urban roads were selected. Vehicle-mounted LiDAR and a mobile environmental monitoring station were used to synchronously measure street tree parameters, road spatial structure, meteorological conditions, and traffic volume. The results showed significant spatiotemporal variations in PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations: Qiantang District (industrial zone) had the most severe pollution, while Xihu District (scenic region) had the lowest. Their temporal variation curves were highly consistent, indicating common sources. Street Trees exerted significant effects under two scenarios: W/H < 0.6 with traffic volume < 1500 vehicles/2h, and W/H > 1.2 with traffic volume > 1500 vehicles/2h. However, their effects had a threshold: under W/H = 0.6-1.2 and traffic volume > 1500 vehicles/2h, the effect was superior to high tree density only when street tree volume was 8000–16000 m³; excessive volume exacerbated pollution. Linear regression models for PM2.5 (F = 21.591, p < 0.001, adjusted R² = 0.290) and PM10 (F = 21.813, p < 0.001, adjusted R² = 0.292) showed that road volume and fuel vehicle traffic were extremely significantly positively correlated with PM concentrations (p < 0.001), while street tree volume and new energy vehicle traffic were extremely significantly negatively correlated (p < 0.001). These findings highlight conditional and threshold effects of street trees on PM pollution, informing evidence-based road design and urban greening to enhance air quality in urbanizing regions.

title: Research on Controllable Ultrafast Laser Fabrication of Hydrophobicity Micro-cone Structures
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Research on Controllable Ultrafast Laser Fabrication of Hydrophobicity Micro-cone Structures
detail.abstract: This study addresses low efficiency in optimizing ultrafast laser processing for superhydrophobic surfaces and limited interpretability of conventional neural network models. TC4 titanium alloy with picosecond laser treatment is used to investigate influences of laser power, scanning speed, and grid spacing on surface microstructures and hydrophobicity. A two-step neural network model for parameter-structure-performance relationships is established, with R² values of 0.9170 and 0.9212 for the two stages. The first-stage parameter-structure model clarifies the mechanism of laser parameter control over micro-cone morphology. This mechanism is categorized into a non-interference region, a critical non-interference region, and an interference region based on distinct influence rules. In the second-stage structure-performance model, micro-cone height is identified as the key structural parameter. It exerts a positive regulatory effect on hydrophobicity together with the overall inclination angle and tip inclination angle.

title: Synchronized Crypto Crashes and Digital Gold-Backed Structural Decoupling: Event-Time Evidence from Major Cryptocurrencies

detail.title: Synchronized Crypto Crashes and Digital Gold-Backed Structural Decoupling: Event-Time Evidence from Major Cryptocurrencies
detail.abstract: We document a stylized fact in cryptocurrency markets: large drawdowns across major cryptoassets cluster in event time, activating within the same narrow window. While existing research examines average co-movement and volatility spillovers among cryptoassets, the event-time structure of simultaneous crash activation remains underexplored. Using 4-hour data for BTC, ETH, DOGE, LTC, and BCH over a six-year sample (2020–2026), we define crash states based on rolling-peak drawdown thresholds and introduce a Crash Synchronization Score (CSS) to measure cross-asset overlap in crash timing. Under the baseline threshold (20%), the average fraction of assets simultaneously in crash state is 26.3%, with 13.6% of observations involving four or more assets in concurrent crash states. Synchronization remains economically meaningful under alternative thresholds, window lengths, and episode-construction rules, indicating that the pattern is not driven by calibration. Crash activation is tightly clustered in event time, with 64.1% of system episodes exhibiting simultaneous onset across participating assets. Crash-time co-occurrence with a gold-linked benchmark (PAXG), scaled for volatility differences, is materially weaker, confirming that synchronization is crypto-specific rather than reflecting generic cross-asset stress. Monte Carlo randomization confirms that observed synchronization lies beyond the 99th percentile of the null distribution (p = 0.002). These findings suggest that downside risk in crypto markets is largely systemic and event-synchronous, with direct implications for portfolio-level stress testing, diversification strategy, and drawdown-based risk management.

title: Semantic-Driven Cross-Modal Alignment Network for Radar Jamming Recognition
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Xidian University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Xidian University

detail.title: Semantic-Driven Cross-Modal Alignment Network for Radar Jamming Recognition
detail.abstract: Radar jamming recognition is a critical prerequisite for radar to accurately measure target information, enabling intelligent anti-jamming decision-making in complex electromagnetic environments. While deep learning models have achieved remarkable performance in this domain, their lack of interpretability and sole reliance on data-driven learning limit their practical deployment in safety-critical radar measurement systems. To address these issues, we propose a semantic-driven cross-modal alignment network for radar jamming recognition, SDCMAN, which integrates structured domain knowledge into the feature learning process. Specifically, a multi-domain jamming signal semantic encoding method (MDSE) is proposed to complementarily aggregate the time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-frequency characteristics of signals. A knowledge prompt encoder (TPE) is designed to generate text semantic representations for different jamming types, which provide effective guidance for multi-domain feature learning of signals. By adaptively aligning learned signal features with text-semantic assisted representations, SDCMAN boosts jamming feature representation capability and interpretability, further enabling the radar jamming accuracy. Experimental evaluation on a radar measured dataset comprising 50 jamming categories demonstrates that SDCMAN achieves superior performance compared with other advanced methods. The recognition accuracies of SDCMAN attain 99.55%, 99.53%, and 99.71% under 0 dB, 5 dB, and 10 dB jamming-to-noise ratio (JNR), respectively.

title: Structural Inductive Bias Reduces Sample Complexityin Implicit Neural Models for Dynamical Systems
affiliations: National University of San Juan and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Structural Inductive Bias Reduces Sample Complexityin Implicit Neural Models for Dynamical Systems
detail.abstract: We prove that implicit neural models with structural inductive bias achieve tighter generalization bounds than explicit models, and therefore require fewer training samples for the same approximation quality. The key mechanism is that an implicit formulation F(x, y, MLP(x;theta)) = 0, where F encodes known structural knowledge about the target function, changes the learning target: the network approximates a simpler residual h* instead of the original function f*. Using Rademacher complexity theory, we derive explicit generalization bounds for both formulations and establish a quantitative gain condition under which the implicit model achieves lower sample complexity. We define the structural content of F as the ratio of path norm reduction, and show that the implicit model outperforms the explicit one if and only if the structural content exceeds an amplification factor determined by the Lipschitz constant of F. We provide sufficient conditions for complexity reduction, counterexamples showing when implicit models fail, and two instantiations: physics-informed variable transformations, where F absorbs known solution structure; and the Homotopy Analysis Method (HAM), where F decomposes the solution into linear corrections of decreasing complexity. We distinguish this target-transformation mechanism from the regularization approach of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), which constrains the optimization landscape but does not change the learning target. Numerical experiments on damped oscillators and the nonlinear pendulum validate the theoretical predictions: the implicit model achieves 3x lower test error for the exponential envelope case (beta = 1), and the HAM residual model achieves 7x improvement with exponential decay rate rho ~ 0.45 as the truncation order increases. A counterexample with trivial F confirms that no advantage is obtained when the structural content is unity.

title: SINCox+IG: An Interpretable Deep Survival Model Using Sparse-Input Neural Networks with Integrated Gradients
affiliations: Central South University and Central South University

detail.title: SINCox+IG: An Interpretable Deep Survival Model Using Sparse-Input Neural Networks with Integrated Gradients

keywords.keywords: Survival analysis Time-to-event Explainable Artificial Intelligence Integrated Gradients  Cox proportion hazards model

detail.abstract: Survival analysis faces a fundamental tension between model performance and interpretability. Traditional statistical methods like the Cox model provide interpretability but fail to capture complex nonlinear relationships, while deep learning approaches offer superior predictive accuracy at the cost of transparency. This paper proposes SINCox+IG, an interpretable deep survival framework that integrates sparse neural networks with the Cox proportional hazards model. Our approach addresses three key challenges: (1) balancing performance and interpretability through sparse network architecture, (2) designing specialized loss functions combining survival likelihood with regularization, and (3) establishing robust interpretation evaluation using synthetic datasets with predefined feature importance. Comprehensive experiments on four synthetic and five real-world datasets demonstrate that SINCox achieves state-of-the-art performance in both C-index and Brier score while significantly reducing computational complexity. Crucially, SINCox+IG provides more accurate feature importance interpretations than SHAP-based approaches, as validated through controlled experiments.

title: AI Governance in Practice: Symbolic Governance, Structural Drivers, and Design Solutions

detail.title: AI Governance in Practice: Symbolic Governance, Structural Drivers, and Design Solutions
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) governance has become central to organisational oversight, yet existing research largely assumes the organisational capacity required to implement it. This paper challenges that assumption by introducing Symbolic Governance, defined as the formal adoption of governance structures that signal responsibility without enabling effective oversight. Using a theory-building integrative review with empirical anchoring, the study synthesises AI governance literature and draws on evidence from 351 organisations. The findings show that governance roles are often weakly integrated, under-resourced, and lack decision-making authority, indicating that symbolic governance is an empirically dominant organisational condition. To explain this, the paper develops the Governance Misalignment Triad, capturing the decoupling of responsibility, authority, and organisational capacity. It further identifies key structural drivers and examines the risks that arise when governance exists in form but not in function. The paper concludes by proposing design solutions that reposition AI governance as a problem of organisational architecture rather than normative intent.

title: Architectural Fragility of General-Purpose AI in Operations: A Failure Taxonomy and the Domain-Specific Operational Intelligence (DSOI) Framework
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Architectural Fragility of General-Purpose AI in Operations: A Failure Taxonomy and the Domain-Specific Operational Intelligence (DSOI) Framework

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or animal subjects. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding; all authors conducted this work as independent researchers.

detail.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into operations and supply chain management has produced a critical paradox: while organizational adoption is accelerating, operational trust remains persistently low. This paper argues that this trust deficit is caused by the fundamental mismatch between the probabilistic nature of general-purpose artificial intelligence (GPAI) and the deterministic requirements of operational environments. Adopting a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, we address this incompatibility through three contributions. First, we derive a taxonomy of five endogenous failure modes that emerge when GPAI is deployed in operational decision-making contexts: Precision Failures, Context Collapse, Accountability Gaps, Temporal Inconsistency, and Constraint Blindness. Second, we bridge this gap by proposing the Domain-Specific Operational Intelligence (DSOI) framework. We formalize five normative architectural requirements-Operational Grounding, State Persistence, Decision Consistency, Constraint Compliance, and Operational Adaptability-that shift the field's trajectory from capability-based exploration ("what can AI do?") to requirement-based specification ("what must AI be?"). Third, we operationalize these requirements via the DSOI Maturity Model, a diagnostic instrument classifying systems' trustworthiness across five levels of operational maturity. The DSOI framework provides a meta-level requirements specification applicable to any operational AI architecture-whether agentic, symbolic, hybrid, or retrieval-based-extending existing governance standards by defining the necessary conditions for resilient autonomous execution.

title: Retinex-INR: Advancing Low-Light Image Enhancement with Retinex-based Implicit Neural Representation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Retinex-INR: Advancing Low-Light Image Enhancement with Retinex-based Implicit Neural Representation
detail.abstract: Existing low-light image enhancement (LLIE) methods either rely on image-domain Retinex decomposition or lack continuous illumination modeling, resulting in spatial inconsistency, structural artifacts, and limited robustness under severe noise. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Retinex-based Implicit Neural Representation (R-INR) framework for low-light image enhancement. Specifically, we push Retinex model into Implicit Neural Representation (INR) in latent space, enabling more continuous and fine-grained illumination modeling as well as better disentanglement of reflectance and illumination. Additionally, we design a Structure-Aware Denoising Module (SADM) to suppress noise before R-INR, and introduce an auxiliary structure enhancement branch to compensate for high-frequency detail loss caused by the smoothing nature of INRs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art approaches in both visual quality and quantitative metrics.

title: Visibility and Protection: A Structural Framework for Career Trajectory and Institutional Value Conversion
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: Visibility and Protection: A Structural Framework for Career Trajectory and Institutional Value Conversion
detail.abstract: Career advancement is commonly framed as a function of performance made visible. Individuals are encouraged to produce high-quality work and ensure that their contributions are recognized. While visibility is necessary, it is not sufficient. This paper advances a structural framework distinguishing between visibility and protection as separate institutional functions governing whether contribution is merely observed or converted into a durable advantage. Visibility renders contribution legible within an organization. Protection determines whether that contribution is preserved, advocated for, and translated into opportunity under conditions of competition, ambiguity, and constraint. When visibility exceeds protection, a structural imbalance emerges in which contribution is consumed rather than compounded. This paper formalizes that imbalance as the Visibility–Protection Law, develops a dynamic model of how high-performing individuals become stabilized within roles that maximize output while limiting advancement, and introduces a diagnostic matrix for assessing institutional behavior. The framework identifies a structural mechanism that operates independently of individual performance, engagement, or organizational awareness and that disproportionately governs the trajectories of those whose contributions are most relied upon and least structurally protected.

title: noēPFN: A Domain-Specific Prior-Data Fitted Network for Workforce Analytics
affiliations: and ESCP Business School

detail.title: noēPFN: A Domain-Specific Prior-Data Fitted Network for Workforce Analytics
detail.abstract: Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) achieve strong tabular prediction performance through transformerbased in-context learning over millions of synthetic training datasets. General-purpose PFNs such as TabPFN are trained on domain-agnostic synthetic data and do not encode the causal structure available in mature applied literatures. We introduce noēPFN, a domain-specific PFN for workforce analytics, trained on causally structured synthetic data generated from a structural equation model (SEM) whose coefficients are drawn from organisational behaviour meta-analyses. We develop a mutual-information-based diagnostic that distinguishes corpus undercalibration from architectural limitation by jointly analysing feature-target signal strength and classical-model performance ceilings, and use it to drive two iterative corpus repairs. We test five pre-specified hypotheses across four model generations and three corpus versions using K-paired-draw evaluation, in which train/test partitions are independently re-sampled K times and statistical comparisons are paired by data seed. Against gradient-boosted trees at matched data budgets, noēPFN wins on all ten benchmark tasks (mean ΔR² = +0.155) and lifts mean cross-industry Spearman ρ from 0.637 to 0.824 (+29.3%, all five industries paired-t p<.001 at K=40). Against TabPFN, noēPFN produces one robust task-specific advantage on emotional exhaustion (Δ=+0.022, p<.001), mechanistically anchored to a Job Demands-Resources structural-equation repair, with a context-sizedependent crossover near N≈75-100 separating regimes where the domain prior versus the general-purpose prior dominates. Out-of-distribution analyses under symmetric and asymmetric covariate-shift protocols show that the domain-grounded prior confers structural robustness to feature-distribution mismatch unavailable to general-purpose tabular models. We further provide a real-world replication of the small-N sample-efficiency claim on a cohort-level voluntary attrition panel constructed from operational humanresources data of a global health-technology enterprise (n = 541 cohort-period observations, 47,480 FTE, 3,127 voluntary attrition events). Benchmarked against both TabPFN v2.6 (Hollmann et al., 2025) and the May 2026 TabPFN v3 release (PriorLabs, 2026), noēPFN significantly outperforms both TabPFN versions at N = 25

detail.abstract:
This paper presents the public edition of CVE Case Study #3: Multi-Regime Observations Across Fifteen Digital Asset Windows, published under the 135 Research imprint using authenticated Kaiko market data under the CVE v2.1 framework.

The study extends prior single-window and multi-asset CVE work into a fifteen-window regime observation panel. Across fifteen independent 72-hour UTC windows, the same six-asset observation structure is rebuilt at one-minute resolution across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, USDC, and USDT. Each regime is treated as a bounded observation record, with documented venue assignments, panel conditions, figure references, verification artifacts, and SHA-256 fingerprints.
