       A technology-agnostic linear storage model is employed. Four representative EMS are evaluated, namely filter-based, deadzone-based, MPC-based, and fuzzy-logic-based approaches. These are benchmarked against a reference dispatch optimization with perfect forecast. The study is conducted across multiple storage configurations and representative load profiles, resulting in approximately 10 000 investigated setups. For each setup, EMS parameters and system size are optimized using evolutionary algorithms.
      A clear performance ranking of the EMS emerges. Deadzone-based EMS perform best, followed by fuzzy-logic-based, MPC-based, and filter-based EMS. Performance differences are small for most EMS, with required relative system overdimensioning typically between 3 % and 10 %. EMS performance was found to be governed by load profile characteristics. The variability of the load profile is identified as the dominant predictor. All EMS exhibit worse sizing performance with increasing variability. Different dispatch strategies yield similar system sizing, indicating low sensitivity of sizing to dispatch details. Optimized EMS parameters show strong clustering, indicating robustness and enabling the derivation of heuristics for EMS parameter selection.​
       The results imply that EMS tuning and system sizing can be decoupled with limited performance loss. This enables a separation of the HESS design process into sizing and EMS design, improving transparency, explainability, and modularity. Deadzone-based EMS provide strong baseline performance and constitute a benchmark for future EMS development.

title: AGI, ANI and Economic Growth
affiliations: Tsinghua University and

detail.title: AGI, ANI and Economic Growth
detail.abstract: This paper develops an endogenous growth model formalizing the "Foundation Model + Adaptation" paradigm, featuring an Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) as the foundation model and downstream Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI) as the domain-specialized applications. We characterize and compare BGPs in the decentralized economy, the social planner's solution, and a novel AGI super-monopolist scenario, highlighting AGI-ANI complementarity, interactions and coupling. The analysis examines scale effects on AI industry structure, as well as alternative growth engines that generate divergent intelligence evolution trajectories. Standard decentralized equilibrium exhibits suboptimally depressed growth with intelligence misallocation (insufficient AGI advancement). This inefficiency stems from the disruption in profit transmission and the monopoly-induced inefficient AI training, which create a dynamic tension between AGI and ANI incentives. While a higher AGI markup stimulates growth in the standard decentralized economy, a super-monopolist that internalizes and manipulates macroeconomic dynamics strategically suppresses growth. A composite subsidy regime or the vertical integration in AI industry can restore social optimality in both scenarios whereas AGI price regulation fails, suggesting stimulative rather than restrictive policies in the age of AGI.

title: Talking to Digital Twins: Selective Disclosure and Belief Measurement in Financial Social Media
affiliations: Mays Business School at Texas A&M University, Nuffield College University of Oxford, Texas A&M University and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Finance Area

detail.title: Talking to Digital Twins: Selective Disclosure and Belief Measurement in Financial Social Media
detail.abstract: Social media affect financial markets, but public posts by financial media personas are voluntary disclosures. What is not disclosed is therefore usually unobserved. We address this measurement problem by conducting repeated, real-time interviews of "digital twins" built from monitored finfluencers' X accounts under a fixed protocol. The interviews recover stocklevel public-persona belief proxies even when no public recommendation is made. Because the interviews are generated and archived before the relevant return windows, the design avoids the look-ahead bias that arises when LLMs are queried ex post. The evidence shows that information obtained from these digital-twin interviews predicts the cross section of S&P 500 stock returns in the expected direction. Repeated real-time interviews therefore show how selective disclosure can be turned into measurable panels of market views.

reference: Case Western Reserve Journal of International Law Vol. 58 (2026) pp 491-543
title: Ecocide and the International Criminal Court: Reassessing the African Union-ICC Impasse
affiliations: University of Silesia in Katowice - Poland Faculty of Law and Administration

detail.title: Ecocide and the International Criminal Court: Reassessing the African Union-ICC Impasse

declarations.funderStatement: The Polish National Science Centre with grant number UMO-2021/41/N/HS5/01227

publicationDetails.detailsText: Case Western Reserve Journal of International Law Vol. 58 (2026) pp 491-543

detail.abstract:
The refusal of the African Union (AU) and its leaders to cooperate with the International Criminal Court (ICC) led to the negotiation of the Protocol on Amendments to the Protocol on the Statute of the African Court of Justice and Human Rights 2014 (the Malabo Protocol). The Protocol incorporates the core crimes of the Rome Statute and, in addition, expands on the meaning of international crime by defining crimes related to the
environment, among others. Although the Malabo Protocol is innovative in its provisions, it lacks the potential to prevent ecocide in Africa or to serve as a model for an international legal instrument on ecocide. First, it reduces the definition of illicit exploitation of the environment to, mainly, a breach of a contract for such exploitation or a lack of such a contract. Furthermore, African leaders have not shown any serious commitment to seeing the protocol enter into force. However, in 2021, the Independent Expert Panel for the Legal Definition of Ecocide proposed a definition of ecocide, recommending that the Rome Statute be amended to bring crimes against the environment under the ICC jurisdiction.This proposal is significant in the context of Africa, where the business activities of transnational corporations (TNCs) have caused significant environmental harm, particularly given the lack of a clear-cut international accountability mechanism to address these abuses. Therefore, this Article aims to examine the effectiveness of the ICC in redressing environmental harm committed, especially by TNCs in Africa, having regard to the strained relationship between the ICC and
the AU. This Article concludes that Africa’s natural environment and resources will be better protected under the ICC regime and calls on African leaders to champion the amendment of the ICC Statute to include ecocide as one of the core international crimes.

title: The Growth of Small Firms in Emerging Markets
affiliations: Duke University, Fuqua School of Business

detail.title: The Growth of Small Firms in Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises are central to economic life in emerging markets, yet many struggle to convert short-run profitability into sustained growth. Existing research offers two dominant explanations. One view emphasizes constraints, arguing that small firms lack adequate capital, skills, and market access. A second view emphasizes agency, showing that entrepreneurs in these settings are adaptive, strategic, and capable of growth despite severe constraints. I argue that both views miss how institutional environments determine whether strategic gains accumulate over time. Drawing on administrative, high-frequency operational, survey, and qualitative data from South Africa's minibus taxi industry, I document four stylized facts: the sector is dynamic, growth is fragile, high-impact idiosyncratic shocks are recurrent, and recovery from these shocks is difficult. I develop a framework in which performance depends on strategy, shock exposure, recovery capacity, and survival thresholds. The paper suggests that institutional incompleteness undermines growth by preventing firms from recovering from recurrent shocks.

title: Wasserstein Query-Error Control for Reusable Low-Rank Graph-Operator Computation
affiliations: and Beijing Institute of Technology

detail.title: Wasserstein Query-Error Control for Reusable Low-Rank Graph-Operator Computation
detail.abstract: Streaming weighted graphs on a fixed vertex set arise where edge weights evolve over time. Recomputing a low-rank graph-operator representation at every observation wastes effort when the underlying distribution is stable, while reusing an outdated representation distorts downstream queries. We develop a computational statistical method for this reuse-versus-recompute problem. The method represents the stream through probability measures on the space of symmetric hollow matrices and controls the effect of deterministic rank-r compression through a Wasserstein query-error bound. For an L q-Lipschitz query, the W 1 distance between the original and compressed query laws is bounded by L q times the expected Hilbert-Schmidt projection residual. This bound combines with a structural-stability CUSUM statistic into a testtriggered reuse rule: cached representations are reused before threshold crossing and recomputed after structural change is detected. We give a surrogate-cost bound for non-linear graph-operator pushforwards. Simulations examine sharpness of the bound, finite-sample behavior of the trigger, and conservatism of the surrogate-cost bound. An empirical study of rolling correlation operators on Fama-French 49 industry portfolio returns illustrates the resulting query-error/recomputation trade-off against periodic and adaptive baselines.

title: Permanent Currency Swap Lines as an Endogenous Mechanism for Precautionary Demand Reduction

detail.title: Permanent Currency Swap Lines as an Endogenous Mechanism for Precautionary Demand Reduction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract: The Mar-a-Lago Accord framework, as articulated in A User's Guide to Restructuring the Global Trading System (Miran 2024), identifies dollar overvaluation as the structural source of U.S. current-account deterioration and advocates a weak-dollar policy as the corrective instrument. The framework, however, proposes only coercive and externally imposed instruments-Plaza-style multilateral coordination, unilateral user fees on Treasury holders, and securityconditioned currency realignment-none of which constitute an endogenous structural mechanism by which dollar demand falls. This paper proposes that a negotiated expansion of Permanent Currency Swap Lines (PCSL)-from the current five-central-bank standing arrangement to all treaty allies and key strategic partners-constitutes precisely that missing mechanism. Under PCSL access, the institutional floor supporting the precautionary component of global dollar demand is removed. Individual nations' total dollar holdings may remain stable or rise, driven by their own investment and trade dynamics; but the aggregate precautionary demand floor falls across the network, producing long-run structural downward pressure on the dollar's equilibrium exchange rate. Simultaneously, dollar hegemony is reinforced, as swap dependency deepens the institutional embedding of the dollar in global financial architecture. The proposal is operationalized as a positive-sum negotiation instrument with two binding conditions-expansion of recipient central banks' U.S. Treasury balance sheets, and structural financial system reform as a prerequisite for access-and one non-binding encouragement: the gradual reduction of precautionary USD cash holdings in favor of Treasury securities. This structure replaces Miran's coercive posture with a self-enforcing institutional contract. The result is a coherent triad-long-run dollar weakness, hegemony consolidation, and allied financial system alignment-that the Miran framework requires but does not deliver.

reference: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2026-10
title: Making Sense of Labor-Market Indicators Amid Data Imperfections
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, Princeton University, University of Texas at Austin and Federal Reserve Bank of New York

detail.title: Making Sense of Labor-Market Indicators Amid Data Imperfections

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2026-10
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Interpreting real-time labor market conditions is challenging because commonly used indicators are noisy, revised over time, and often send conflicting signals. In practice, policymakers and market participants describe labor market developments using a shared narrative language centered on labor demand, labor supply, and matching frictions. In this paper, we show that empirical measures of these narrative concepts can be recovered from latent factors that summarize the joint movements of a broad set of high-frequency U.S. labor-market indicators. We use ninety-four labor-market indicators, over the period from 1960 to 2026, and construct measures for labor demand, long-run labor supply, short-run labor supply, and matching efficiency by selecting the factors that satisfy a limited set of restrictions on how underlying forces map into observed data. We find that labor demand and short-run labor supply account for most of the common variation in labor-market indicators. Our results also show that assigning narrow interpretations to individual indicators can lead to misleading conclusions about underlying labor market conditions. Applying the framework to the post-pandemic period reveals that although labor demand recovered briskly after the acute phase of the pandemic, it cannot account for the large rise in vacancies and quits. Instead, movements in short-run labor supply and matching efficiency play a central role. We also show that the "soft-landing" episode from 2023 through 2025 was characterized by a joint decline in labor demand and short-run labor supply, which slowed payroll growth while generating only a moderate increase in the unemployment rate.

title: The Fear Multiplier: Cyclical Layoff Risk and Aggregate Demand

detail.title: The Fear Multiplier: Cyclical Layoff Risk and Aggregate Demand
detail.abstract: How does individual consumption respond to cyclical changes in layoff risk, and does this response amplify aggregate shocks? I estimate the microeconomic response by combining consumption data from the Panel Study of Income Dynamics with a novel, granular measure of layoff rates that I construct from the Quarterly Workforce Indicators. Exploiting within-state variation in layoff rates across demographics and industries of employment, I find strong state-dependence concentrated during the Great Recession, plausibly driven by the severe consequences of job loss: a 1 percentage point increase in a group's layoff rate caused food expenditure to fall by 1.3%, whereas the response is negligible during expansions. I then introduce countercyclical layoff risk in an otherwise canonical equilibrium model with incomplete markets. Households respond more to a given change in expected income if it arises from increased layoffs rather than from a fall in future earnings conditional on employment. Accordingly, aggregate demand responds more on impact to a given expected change in future aggregate income if this is concentrated through layoffs rather than diffused through wage cuts. Spending down of aggregate savings then reverses the relative effect in later periods. In general equilibrium, this fear-driven front-loading of aggregate demand amplifies the impact fiscal multiplier by 40% while accelerating subsequent recoveries.

title: Revenue-targeted Core-selecting Mechanisms
affiliations: University of Piraeus and Utrecht University

detail.title: Revenue-targeted Core-selecting Mechanisms
detail.abstract: We propose a revenue-targeted core-selecting payment rule where payments are minimally adjusted to reach a chosen core-compatible revenue benchmark, such as the minimum-revenue or seller-optimal core. The rule discourages aggressive bid shading and preserves aggregate revenues of nearest-core selection. Overall, it strengthens stability and revenue performance while retaining the economic intuition of VCG pricing.

title: Firms' Internal Information Practices and Minority Wage Differences
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis, Boston College - Department of Accounting and Washington University in St. Louis

detail.title: Firms' Internal Information Practices and Minority Wage Differences
detail.abstract: We study whether workplaces with higher-quality internal information practices exhibit smaller minority wage differences. Using restricted U.S. Census data linking workers to establishments, we analyze production workers in manufacturing plants observed across multiple waves of the Management and Organizational Practices Survey. Using restrictive worker-by-establishment fixed effects, we find that improvements in internal information quality are associated with higher wages overall and disproportionately larger wage gains for Black workers, resulting in narrower minority wage gaps. Additional results are consistent with two mechanisms, though others may also play a role. First, better internal information practices may help to reduce racial discrimination by giving managers more objective employee performance data. Second, better internal information systems may improve the relative productivity of minority employees by giving them better access to performance data.

title: A Theory of Redistribution and Public Good Provision Under Non-democracy

detail.title: A Theory of Redistribution and Public Good Provision Under Non-democracy
detail.abstract: Two office-motivated politicians compete for power by making promises to citizens. Unlike in voting models, a citizens' political activity is observable and subject to retaliation if the citizen happens to back the wrong politician. In equilibrium, a citizen supports the politician that is expected to win the political contest, not the one who promises her the most. Consequently, the incentives for politicians to redistribute resources and provide public goods are different from those in voting models. Citizens who are better able to coordinate with others receive more resources in equilibrium. Transition to democracy is not voluntary in this model.

title: Interest on Reserves and Monetary Policy Transmission

detail.title: Interest on Reserves and Monetary Policy Transmission
detail.abstract: Using monthly U.S. data from 1967M1 to 2018M10, I estimate a structural vector autoregression with short-and long-run restrictions to test whether monetary base expansions had weaker effects on output and prices after the Federal Reserve began paying interest on reserves (IOR) in October 2008. I compare the macroeconomic effects of monetary base shocks across pre-IOR (1967M1-2008M10) and post-IOR (2008M11-2018M10) subsamples. In the pre-IOR period, a one-standard-deviation monetary base shock raises output by approximately 0.31 percent at its peak and produces a permanent increase in the price level of approximately 0.29 percent, with the output response significantly above zero for roughly 55 months. In the post-IOR period, the same shock produces muted and statistically imprecise responses for both variables. Forecast error variance decompositions reveal a complementary shift: monetary policy shocks account for 86 percent of monetary base variation on impact in the pre-IOR period but only 44 percent in the post-IOR period, with money demand shocks absorbing the difference. These results are consistent with a weakening of the aggregate transmission of monetary base expansions to the real economy.

title: On the Asymptotic Properties of the Conditional Maximum Likelihood Estimator for Time Series Regression Models with Conditional Heteroskedasticity
affiliations: University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB), University of California Santa Barbara and University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB)

detail.title: On the Asymptotic Properties of the Conditional Maximum Likelihood Estimator for Time Series Regression Models with Conditional Heteroskedasticity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This paper fills a gap in the literature by providing sufficient conditions under which the Conditional Maximum Likelihood Estimator (CMLE) for ARMAX-GARCH models is efficient. Key contributions include a direct proof of strong consistency of the CMLE, the establishment of asymptotic normality and efficiency, the derivation of geometric convergence rates for recursive approximations, and the demonstration of the consistency of the outer product of score contributions.

title: The GENIUS Act Standard: Why Canada Should Align Its Stablecoin Regulation with the Emerging De Facto Global Standard

detail.title: The GENIUS Act Standard: Why Canada Should Align Its Stablecoin Regulation with the Emerging De Facto Global Standard
detail.abstract: Over the past year, there has been an exponential growth in interest across the world for fiat-backed stablecoins, as well as the question of how they should be regulated. Canada currently answers the latter question with an interim regulatory regime, characterizing fiat-backed stablecoins as securities, a response shaped by the "regulatory dance" between external pressures, industry and academic commentary, and Canada's domestic institutional capacity. This Article argues that, while it is understandable how that interim regime came to fruition given its context, the time has come to ensure that Canada's longterm regulatory framework for fiat-backed stablecoins aligns with emerging global norms. The Article conducts a geopolitical analysis, demonstrating that, because of several factors contributing toward an expectation of regulatory convergence, the American model is likely to become the de facto global standard for stablecoin regulation. Accordingly, the Government of Canada should ensure its long-term framework (via the newly enacted, but yet to be implemented, Stablecoin Act) is substantially similar to that of the GENIUS Act, while improving upon it where possible, and can therefore interoperate with the rest of the world. Crucially, it should do so in conjunction with both industry feedback and communications with the U.S. Department of the Treasury, with a view to officially securing a "comparable" finding pursuant to Section 18 of the GENIUS Act. That way, the Canadian market will become more attractive to foreign issuers/developers, and the Canadian dollar will stand a chance in international stablecoin markets.

reference: European Corporate Governance Institute – Finance Working Paper No. 1142/2026
title: Complex Organizations, Leverage, and Interest Rates
affiliations: University of Turin - Department ESOMAS and University of Turin

detail.title: Complex Organizations, Leverage, and Interest Rates

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Corporate Governance Institute – Finance Working Paper No. 1142/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: European Corporate Governance Institute (ECGI) - Finance Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Our trade-off model studies optimal leverage responses to interest rates within a sponsor–backed unit structure. This setup captures organizational forms-including private equity, parent–subsidiary, and securitization arrangements- in which a sponsor provides contingent support to an affiliated unit. When interest rates fall below a cutoff, the sponsor chooses zero leverage, while the backed unit increases borrowing. Unlike stand-alone firms, whose leverage declines monotonically as interest rates fall, backed units generate higher expected default costs in low-interest-rate environments. Our results show how complex organizations can reallocate leverage toward less constrained entities, highlighting a new governance channel shaping borrowing decisions.

title:
What Suppresses Nash Equilibrium Play in Large Language Models? 
Mechanistic Evidence and Causal Control
affiliations: University of Crete and University of Crete

detail.title:
What Suppresses Nash Equilibrium Play in Large Language Models? 
Mechanistic Evidence and Causal Control
detail.abstract:
LLM agents are known to deviate from Nash equilibria in strategic interactions, but nobody has looked inside the model to understand why, or asked whether the deviation can be reversed. We do both. 
     Working with four open-source models (Llama-3 and Qwen2.5, 8B to 72B parameters) playing four canonical two-player games, we first establish the behavioral picture through self-play and cross-play experiments, then open up the 32-layer Llama-3-8B model and examine what actually happens during a strategic decision.
      The mechanistic findings are clear. Opponent history is encoded with near-perfect fidelity at the very first layer (96% probe accuracy) and consumed progressively by later ones, while Nash action encoding is weak throughout, never exceeding 56%. There is no dedicated Nash module. Instead, the model privately favors the Nash action through most of its forward pass, but a prosocial override (a bias toward cooperative, other-regarding behavior rooted in pretraining on human text and further modulated by RLHF) concentrated in the final layers reverses this, reaching 84% probability of cooperation at layer 30. When we inject a learned Nash direction into the residual stream, the behavior shifts bidirectionally and causally, confirmed through concept clamping. 
      The behavioral experiments surface six scale-and architecture-dependent findings in self-play, the most notable being that chain-of-thought reasoning worsens Nash play in small models but achieves near-perfect Nash play in models above 70B parameters. The crossplay experiments reveal three phenomena invisible in self-play: a small model can unravel the cooperation of any partner simply by defecting early; two large models reinforce each other's cooperative instincts indefinitely; and who moves first in a coordination game determines which Nash equilibrium the system lands on. The central finding is that LLMs do not lack Nashplaying competence. They compute it, then suppress it.

title: "Forecasting Female STEM Graduation Rates in the OECD: So Far or So Close?"
affiliations: ,  and Chilean Economic Development Agency (CORFO)

detail.title: "Forecasting Female STEM Graduation Rates in the OECD: So Far or So Close?"

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of Interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human subjects
declarations.funderStatement: No funder

detail.abstract: This paper addresses the persistent underrepresentation of women in STEM fields within OECD countries. Using a longitudinal panel for 35 OECD members (1998-2017) drawn from international education, labor, and institutional datasets, this paper estimates fractional-response generalized linear models to identify structural drivers of women's STEM graduation shares and to project regional trajectories. Higher income inequality, higher adolescent fertility, and a larger share of women in full-time working couples are associated with higher female STEM graduation. Conversely, stronger women's political rights, higher female labor-force participation, longer father-specific parental leave, and higher GDP per capita are linked to lower STEM shares, consistent with expanded career choice in more egalitarian, affluent contexts. Projections to 2077 suggest parity is plausible in several regions but unlikely in Latin America and North America under baseline conditions. These results support policies that pair incentives with interventions addressing norms, belonging, and the perceived social value of STEM.

title:
Tail Index Sensitivity of Standard Causal Estimators
A Monte Carlo Characterisation

detail.title:
Tail Index Sensitivity of Standard Causal Estimators
A Monte Carlo Characterisation
detail.abstract: Standard asymptotic inference in observational econometrics relies on moment conditions that implicitly require the error distribution's tail index α to exceed two, guaranteeing finite variance. This assumption is never stated, tested, or defended in applied work, despite empirical evidence that α < 2 is common in financial and macroeconomic data. We formally characterise three consequences of relaxing it. First, OLS instability rises monotonically from α = 1.9-well within the empirically plausible range-not only at the Cauchy boundary α = 1. Second, the IV amplification ratio (IV IQR / OLS IQR) reaches 23.85× at α = 2 for a weak instrument (δ = 0.04) and compresses monotonically as α falls-not because IV improves, but because OLS deteriorates faster in proportional terms, a pattern not previously documented across the full α spectrum. Third, Newey-West HAC confidence interval coverage at α = 1.5 is 0.920 at N = 5,000-three percentage points below the nominal 0.95-and this deficit does not close as N grows from 1,000 to 5,000, directly contradicting the standard asymptotic * All errors are my own. defence of HAC. We propose that applied researchers report Hill-estimated tail indices alongside standard diagnostics and conduct sensitivity analysis across plausible α values.

title: The Gubarev Case: Terminal Commitment and Reflexive Practice

detail.title: The Gubarev Case: Terminal Commitment and Reflexive Practice
detail.abstract: This article examines the case of Pavel Gubarev—trained historian, first-wave Donbas volunteer, former “People’s Governor” of Donetsk, and infantry soldier in the post2022 war—as a diagnostic instrument for understanding the structural condition this article designates as terminal commitment: the conversion of bodily risk into the primary medium of political subjectivity under conditions of systematic voice foreclosure. Gubarev is not selected as a representative case but as an extreme one: his biographical trajectory compresses the full arc from institutional engagement to terminal commitment into a single subject, while his unusual degree of reflexive self-awareness renders explicit the mechanisms that, in less articulate subjects, operate below the threshold of direct statement. The analysis proceeds through six distinct interpretive voices—the subject himself, a state propagandist, a liberal press commentator, an anti-Putin diaspora commentator, a liberal media analyst, and a horizontal witness from within the nationalist milieu—each of which reads the same events through an incompatible framework yet produces observations that converge on the same structural description. This convergent testimony from hostile witnesses is treated as primary analytical evidence: when irreconcilable interpretive positions agree on what they observe while disagreeing only on its evaluation, the structure they are all describing is real. The article contributes to the emerging literature on Russian wartime subjectivity by demonstrating that terminal commitment is not a psychological pathology but a structural position occupiable by subjects across the full spectrum of reflexive capacity, and that the mechanism of voice foreclosure— the systematic closure of legitimate channels for political expression—is its primary enabling condition. The article makes two theoretical contributions. First, it proposes terminal commitment as a necessary fourth element of Hirschman’s exit-voice-loyalty framework: a response that becomes structurally available when voice has been not merely ignored but preventively alienated — converted from a channel of political expression into an instrument of surveillance and sanction. Classical Hirschmanian analysis presupposes substantively operative voice channels; terminal commitment describes the condition that emerges when this presupposition fails. Second, the article extends and respecifies Agamben’s account of bare life and the state of exception: where Agamben theorizes the production of politically unrecognizable life through sovereign decision, terminal commitment designates the active response of subjects who have been so produced — the conversion of bare life’s irreducible bodily existence into the primary available medium of political assertion. The body that cannot be made to speak is made, instead, to act irreversibly.

title: Socio-Economic Determinants of Women's Labour Force Participation in Rural Jammu and Kashmir
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Socio-Economic Determinants of Women's Labour Force Participation in Rural Jammu and Kashmir
detail.abstract: This study investigates the socioeconomic factors influencing women's labour force participation in rural Jammu and Kashmir. Despite the crucial role played by women in agriculture, horticulture, livestock management, handicrafts, and household-based enterprises, their participation in formal labour markets remains relatively low compared with male participation. Using secondary datasets including the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) publications, government reports, and international labour statistics, the study examines the role of education, household structure, cultural norms, and participation in self-help groups in determining women's engagement in economic activities. The study adopts a simple econometric framework in which women's labour force participation is treated as the dependent variable and education, household structure, cultural norms, and self-help group participation are treated as explanatory variables. The findings suggest that higher levels of education significantly increase women's probability of participating in economic activities. Similarly, membership in self-help groups improves women's access to financial resources and entrepreneurial opportunities, thereby positively influencing their participation in labour markets. However, the analysis also highlights that traditional social norms and restrictive household arrangements often limit women's access to employment opportunities. The study therefore emphasizes the importance of policy interventions aimed at improving female education, promoting rural entrepreneurship, strengthening women's self-help groups, and addressing gender-based social constraints. The findings contribute to the broader literature on gender economics and rural development and provide policy insights for enhancing women's economic Participation in Jammu and Kashmir.

title: Notes on Organizational Contradiction Inclusion, Governance, and the Gap between Claim and Operation
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: Notes on Organizational Contradiction Inclusion, Governance, and the Gap between Claim and Operation
detail.abstract:
Organizations increasingly present themselves through the language of inclusion, ethics, governance, and social purpose, yet many operate through arrangements that predictably frustrate the very commitments they publicly affirm. This essay develops the concept of organizational contradiction to describe that patterned gap between claim and operation.

The central argument is that contradiction is not best understood as simple hypocrisy, implementation failure, or episodic misconduct. Nor is it adequately captured by existing accounts of loose coupling (Meyer & Rowan, 1977) or means-ends decoupling (Bromley & Powell, 2012). Rather, it is a durable organizational condition in which commitments are institutionalized unevenly: robust enough to generate symbolic and reputational value, but too weakly embedded in authority, incentives, and evaluative routines to govern ordinary practice. Contradiction is distinguished from neighboring concepts by three features: it is patterned rather than episodic, architectural rather than attitudinal, and predictively aligned with the preservation of existing distributions of discretion and convenience.

The essay makes three contributions. First, it provides a sharper conceptual vocabulary for distinguishing contradiction from neighboring ideas and explains why existing institutional frameworks underspecify the normative asymmetry of the phenomenon—specifically, the asymmetry between those who benefit from the commitment’s symbolic value and those who bear the costs of its operative weakness. Second, it explains why contradiction can persist as an organizationally useful arrangement rather than merely a governance defect. Third, it shows why inclusion-branded domains are especially revealing sites for contradiction, because they demand interactional change that cannot be satisfied by procedural apparatus alone.

reference: Re: Structure Lab Briefs Series
title: The Economics of Forced Labour in Global Value Chains

detail.title: The Economics of Forced Labour in Global Value Chains

declarations.funderStatement: The author is grateful t0 Re:Structure Lab and the Humanity United Action and Ford Foundation for project funding.

detail.abstract: Efforts to measure the prevalence of human trafficking, forced labour, and modern slavery have advanced significantly through global estimates produced by the International Labour Organization, the Walk Free Foundation, and the International Organization for Migration. While these figures provide valuable benchmarks for the scale of the issue, they lack the sectoral and firm-level detail needed to inform accountability and policy design. At the same time, a growing body of empirical research — including national surveys, sectoral studies, and NGO-led investigations — offers localized insights that remain fragmented and underutilized. This paper aims to address that gap by using artificial intelligence (AI) tools to systematically extract, code, and synthesize prevalence data from a wide range of field-based studies. The resulting dataset disaggregates estimates by country, sector, demographic group, and form of coercion, creating a platform to compare methodologies and assess how prevalence varies across contexts. Beyond assembling new data, the project advances a framework for linking prevalence to the structural drivers of forced labour. Building on Manning’s monopsony model, the paper proposes that estimating labour supply elasticities can reveal degrees of employer power and the threshold at which monopsony conditions tip into forced labour. Data collection on forced labour must also be enriched by incorporating information on firm characteristics, positions within global value chains, and exposure to international trade, which would allow to move beyond descriptive prevalence reporting and towards an explanation of the economic forces sustaining severe exploitation. The combination of AI-assisted synthesis and structural modelling provides both a methodological contribution and a push to reform data collection: it deepens our understanding of where forced labour is most likely to occur and how it is measured, and highlights the need for firm-level and systemic variables to understand how they shape its persistence.

title: Regulatory Architecture, Epistemic Failure, and the Political Economy of Ghana's Cocoa Crisis

detail.title: Regulatory Architecture, Epistemic Failure, and the Political Economy of Ghana's Cocoa Crisis
detail.abstract: This article reframes Ghana's 2025/26 cocoa sector crisis-conventionally interpreted as a commodity price shock-as the systemic output of a regulatory architecture in which three of Lessig's four modalities of governance operate while the fourth is underdeveloped relative to the regulatory obligations it must support. Law, market incentives, and social norms are present. What is underdeveloped is the technological regulatory infrastructure that makes legal mandates consistently enforceable, market signals epistemically reliable, and governance norms disciplined by verifiable accountability. The 2023/24 production forecast deviation-which triggered US$1.3 billion in forward contract losses-was not primarily a forecasting error but an epistemic failure: the institution produced a projection on data structurally incapable of reflecting ground-truth conditions. Drawing on Lessig's modalities framework, Lipsky's street-level bureaucracy theory, Deming and Juran's quality systems theory, and Wang and Strong's information quality framework, the article argues that structural reform requires not additional legislation-laws already exist-but technological regulatory infrastructure through which those laws apply completely and consistently-capable of surfacing patterns of selective enforcement and rent-seeking where they occur. The fourth modality's underdevelopment is not explained by resource constraint: it has served those who benefit from regulatory gaps at the expense of the farmers the framework is designed to protect.

title: Structural Transformation Beyond Productivity: Subsistence Organization and Agricultural Commercialization in the United States
affiliations: The New School

detail.title: Structural Transformation Beyond Productivity: Subsistence Organization and Agricultural Commercialization in the United States
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether historical commercialization of agriculture has shaped current dependence on food assistance across U.S. states, using a non-monocausal framework that embeds subsistence within a wider system of socioeconomic provisioning. I use a two-sector structural transformation model with heterogeneous subsistence thresholds to recover state-level subsistence parameters from data on agricultural employment and labor productivity, and then relate these parameters to both historical crop specialization and current SNAP enrollment. Higher past specialization in soybeans is associated with lower inferred subsistence requirements, which are in turn associated with greater SNAP participation today. Instrumental-variable estimates with region fixed effects, using soybean specialization as the instrument, remain significant across alternative calibration-quality assumptions.

title: Landholders leverage over rainfall and resilience of Amazon rainforest
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Delft University of Technology, Stockholm University - Stockholm Resilience Center, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Stockholm University - Stockholm Resilience Center

detail.title: Landholders leverage over rainfall and resilience of Amazon rainforest
detail.abstract: The Amazon rainforest regulates the regional water cycle in South America, yet the role of human land-use decision-making in shaping these moisture flows remains poorly understood. Ongoing deforestation and other land conversions threaten to disrupt these moisture flows, with potential consequences for regional rainfall, agricultural production, and the resilience of the Amazon rainforest. Here, we assess the leverage dominant landholder groups have over rainfall across South America and the resilience of the Amazon rainforest. We combine high-resolution land-use/land-cover data with outputs from a moisture-tracking model to assess the extent of landholders' influence on regional rainfall. We find that the dominant landholder groups differ substantially in their contributions to regional rainfall, both in magnitude and destination. Large landholder-dominated regions contribute the greatest to rainfall across South America (4.7×103 km3 yr-1), with substantial contributions to forests (43%), croplands (25%), and pastures (6%). Smallholder- and medium-landholder-dominated regions contribute relatively less to total rainfall, estimated at 3.0×103 km3 yr-1 and 0.6×103 km3 yr-1, respectively. However, a larger proportion of their contributed rainfall falls over forests (52-56%). We also find that reductions in this vegetation-regulated moisture from landholder-dominated regions can produce spatially heterogeneous losses in Amazon forest resilience, with the highest risk of tipping observed along the southern and eastern Amazon and in parts of the Andean–Amazon transition zone. These findings show that land-use decisions can impact rainfall far beyond the location of land conversion, redistributing hydrological risks across forests, agricultural systems, and other downwind actors. Recognizing atmospheric moisture flows as a shared regional ecosystem service can help strengthen land-use governance and associated risk management across South America.

title: Volatility Arbitrage under Discrete Delta Hedging

detail.title: Volatility Arbitrage under Discrete Delta Hedging

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants or animals.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract:
This paper studies volatility arbitrage under discrete delta hedging within a geometric Brownian motion framework. While continuous-time models suggest that volatility arbitrage yields deterministic profits when implied and realized volatility differ, discrete delta hedging introduces cumulative hedging errors that fundamentally alter the performance of the strategy.       This paper characterizes the cumulative hedging error without assuming a discretetime analogue of the Black-Scholes-Merton partial differential equation and shows that it converges to zero as the rebalancing frequency increases. 
      Monte Carlo simulations support the theoretical results and provide insights into the distribution of the cumulative hedging errors. The findings illustrate that volatility arbitrage is inherently risky in discrete time and that its performance critically depends on the rebalancing frequency and the price path of the underlying asset.

title: The use of GenAI in team science: Exploring the role of team size, task independence and geographical dispersion
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The use of GenAI in team science: Exploring the role of team size, task independence and geographical dispersion
detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) remains contested in its adoption within scientific research. While research on team science has increased, the role of GenAI in collaborative research settings remains underexplored. Drawing on a large-scale international survey of researchers’ reported use of GenAI in scientific publications, this study examines how structural conditions of team science, task independence and geographical dispersion, and their interaction with team size is associated with GenAI use. We find that neither task independence nor geographical dispersion alone significantly predicts GenAI adoption. However, both factors interact with team size such that larger teams are more responsive to these structural conditions than smaller teams. We interpret these findings as evidence that GenAI use in team science, while still contested, is driven by coordination needs, with stronger associations in larger, more dispersed, or task-independent teams. We further discuss how GenAI adoption in research teams is closely linked to competitive pressures in science. As a policy implication, we suggest that efforts to govern GenAI in research should move beyond individual-level prescriptions and instead emphasize shared norms, collective responsibility, and team-level governance.

title: The Myth of Polycentricity Why Mission-Oriented Infrastructure R&D Remains an 'Exclusive Club'
affiliations: KDI School of Public Policy and Management - KDI School of Public Policy and Management, Students, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Department of Decision Sciences, George Washington University

detail.title: The Myth of Polycentricity Why Mission-Oriented Infrastructure R&D Remains an 'Exclusive Club'
detail.abstract: While polycentric governance is advocated to democratize innovation, this study uncovers a critical paradox: structural decentralization can mask deepening resource monopolies. Utilizing longitudinal data from 1999 to 2025, the research investigates the structural inertia that concentrates state funding within elite institutions despite policy efforts to diversify participation in national infrastructure R&D programs. Network analysis reveals a transition into hierarchical polycentricity, a state where outward structural fragmentation coexists with a rigid financial hierarchy. Employing a Stochastic Actor-Oriented Model (SAOM), the study identifies the causal drivers of elite entrenchment. Results show two powerful, reinforcing mechanisms: reputational signaling and structural assimilation. First, a signaling effect drives partner selection: while high prior funding attracts partners, elite actors prefer vertical alliances over collaborating with similarly funded peers. Second, stratified synchronization reinforces the divide: once institutions enter the elite cluster, they benefit from financial acceleration, yet this process preserves the vertical distance between the dominant core and the periphery. This study provides a significant theoretical advancement in the literature on polycentric governance while enriching the empirical and methodological understanding of infrastructure R&D collaboration networks.

title: Do Finer Pricing Grids Reduce Market Volatility? Evidence from a Tick Size Reform in an Emerging Market
affiliations: Boise State University - College of Business and Economics, King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM) and Boise State University - College of Business & Economics

detail.title: Do Finer Pricing Grids Reduce Market Volatility? Evidence from a Tick Size Reform in an Emerging Market
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether finer pricing grids reduce volatility in an emerging market. We study the June 29, 2025 tick size reform on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul), which lowered tick sizes for stocks in several price bands while leaving others unchanged. Using daily data for 339 stocks in a 40-trading-day event window, we estimate difference-in-differences models with firm and day fixed effects. Treated stocks experience a significant decline in range volatility relative to control stocks; the baseline estimate implies a 14.5% reduction relative to the treated firms' pre-reform mean. The effect appears across all treated price bands and is robust to winsorization, an alternative volatility measure, and a placebo test. The findings suggest that finer pricing grids improved short-horizon market quality in Tadawul.

title: Experimental evaluation of multi-agent reinforcement learning for corridor-level traffic signal control
affiliations: , Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, , , , Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and

detail.title: Experimental evaluation of multi-agent reinforcement learning for corridor-level traffic signal control
detail.abstract: Although recent research has advanced adaptive traffic control, significant challenges remain in optimizing signal phase timing, coordinating across heterogeneous multi-intersection corridors, and validating performance under real-world traffic conditions. This paper presents a signalized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach and validates its performance within a novel hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) framework, using actuated control as the baseline for comparison. The proposed framework integrates a real-world traffic controller with a digital twin calibrated simulation model, enabling real-time communication between simulation and traffic control infrastructure. The MARL algorithm runs on a roadside unit edge device and updates signal phases across three intersections. Both single and dual-ring signal configurations are evaluated within the framework to reflect typical real-worldtraffic configurations. The digital twin is calibrated using traffic data from the City of Coral Gables, Florida, USA. The MARL-informed HiL results show a 31% reduction in travel delay (sec/mi) in the morning and a 46% reduction in the afternoon, indicating significant improvements in traffic flow efficiency during peak periods compared to actuated control.

title: Physics-informed Accelerated Reconstruction of Randomly Fragmented Trajectories: A Solution Space Compression based Method
affiliations: Tongji University, Tongji University, University of Canterbury, Tongji University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Physics-informed Accelerated Reconstruction of Randomly Fragmented Trajectories: A Solution Space Compression based Method
detail.abstract: Vehicle trajectory data are frequently fragmented by sensing failures, occlusions, and re-identification errors, making trajectory reconstruction essential for traffic analysis and management. Existing methods often struggle to simultaneously achieve high accuracy and computational efficiency because physical constraints are not fully exploited and redundant computations remain in the reconstruction process. This challenge is particularly pronounced for randomly fragmented trajectories due to unknown temporal and spatial gaps, enlarging the association search space compared with determined missing patterns. To address this issue, a bi-level smoothness-aware trajectory reconstruction model is proposed to jointly optimize fragment association and trajectory imputation. A decoupled solution strategy incorporating a multi-window Savitzky–Golay filter reformulates the optimization problem into a computationally tractable two-stage framework. A physics-informed heuristic pruning mechanism compresses the association search space using kinematic constraints, followed by an uncertainty-aware refinement strategy to improve association reliability. The framework is evaluated in highway and urban scenarios using simulation and the NGSIM dataset. On the simulated dataset, the physics-informed pruning mechanism achieves an average improvement of 48.28% in reconstruction accuracy and reduces runtime per trajectory by 47.66% compared with the unpruned baseline. On the NGSIM dataset, the proposed approach achieves an average accuracy improvement of 35.67% and reduces runtime per trajectory by 83.53% compared with the online Negative Cycle Cancellation (NCC) method. The framework is further implemented using field data from Shanghai to demonstrate real-world applicability. The proposed approach provides a scalable and efficient solution for large-scale trajectory reconstruction, supporting both offline and real-time applications.

title: The Role of Techniques: Artifact Complementarity in the Emergence of Innovation
affiliations: WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management, Vienna University of Economics and Business, University of Queensland and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Role of Techniques: Artifact Complementarity in the Emergence of Innovation
detail.abstract: One of the most important and intriguing questions in management is how innovation emerges. When people develop solutions for their needs, they have two fundamental means at their disposal: developing artifacts or doing something in a skillful, novel way (i.e., developing novel techniques). We argue that a strong complementarity between human techniques and artifacts drives innovation. Thus, a more advanced understanding of human techniques is needed to investigate the antecedents and consequences of such technique–artifact complementarity. This paper proposes an initial framework that integrates techniques and artifacts as modular components that can yield novel outcomes. To this end, we develop a 2×2 matrix that shows the different technique–artifact configurations, which in turn enable us to formulate propositions regarding the role of techniques in the emergence of innovation. This framework can explain under which conditions people make changes in artifacts to achieve an outcome and when they choose to develop novel techniques. Due to their strong complementarity, changes in techniques will lead to changes in artifacts over time and vice versa. Insights on the technique–artifact complementarity contribute to research on user innovation, the identity of technological objects, and how human skills are integrated into artifacts.​

title: Integrated Weekly Rostering and Overnight Charging Scheduling Optimization for Heterogeneous Electric Bus Fleets
affiliations: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology, Jiangsu University of Science and Technology and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST)

detail.title: Integrated Weekly Rostering and Overnight Charging Scheduling Optimization for Heterogeneous Electric Bus Fleets
detail.abstract: Most existing electric bus (EB) scheduling models adopt a single-day planning horizon and consequently overlook the multi-day energy coupling that arises when overnight charging resources are constrained. This paper investigates an integrated optimization problem that jointly determines weekly rostering and overnight charging schedules for heterogeneous EB fleets. The objective is to minimize the total cost, including both operating and charging costs, over a weekly horizon while ensuring service feasibility. We formulate the problem as a mixed-integer linear programming model that explicitly captures EB state-of-charge evolution and competition for shared overnight charging piles across consecutive days. To solve large-scale practical instances, we develop a tailored adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm that exploits the temporal structure and resource coupled nature of the problem. A key component of the proposed algorithm is a temporal backtracking charging repair mechanism that retroactively shifts charging demand from congested later periods to underutilized charging windows in earlier days, thereby resolving energy infeasibility caused by limited charging resources. Computational experiments based on real-world operational data demonstrate that our algorithm matches the optimal solutions of a commercial solver on small instances and scales effectively to large instances where exact methods fail to converge within reasonable time limits. The numerical results further quantify the trade-off between charging infrastructure capacity and fleet operating cost, revealing that limited overnight charging capacity forces operators to substitute economical short-range EBs with more expensive long-range alternatives.

title: A Novel Two-Stage Machine Learning Framework for Physician Churn Prediction and Promotion Period Estimation in Family Health Information Systems A Hybrid Feature Selection and Multi-Model Approach with Statistical Validation
affiliations: Adana Alparslan Turkes Science and Technology University

detail.title: A Novel Two-Stage Machine Learning Framework for Physician Churn Prediction and Promotion Period Estimation in Family Health Information Systems A Hybrid Feature Selection and Multi-Model Approach with Statistical Validation
detail.abstract: Family Health Information System (FHIS) vendors in Turkey operate in a market of approximately 20 competitors where annual physician attrition rates of 8–10% create significant revenue erosion. This paper proposes the first domain-specific two-stage machine learning framework for FHIS physician churn, addressing both at-risk physician identification and optimal promotion period estimation. Stage 1 employs Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM (CatBoost-equivalent configuration; implemented via sklearn.GradientBoostingClassifier for reproducibility without external library dependencies)), Logistic Regression (interpretable baseline), and Support Vector Machine (SVM; four kernels) for binary churn classification on 4,229 physician records (churn rate: 24.5%). Stage 2 employs LightGBM, XGBoost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for promotion duration regression (0–6 months) on 3,195 records. A novel Hybrid Feature Selection Algorithm (Hybrid FSA) is proposed, combining true mRMR (Peng et al. 2005), Relief-F (Kononenko 1994), and F-statistic through a three-stage consensus mechanism (majority voting → correlation scoring [IS+D] → priority ranking). A comprehensive ablation study with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests establishes the statistical significance of all reported comparisons. Results (10-fold CV): RF achieves Accuracy=92.74%, Precision=99.32%, F1=82.67%, AUC=0.948, significantly outperforming all SVM variants and Logistic Regression (p<0.001); GBM achieves statistically equivalent F1=82.51% (p=0.577, ns) but with 5× more false positives (24 vs. 5), highlighting a key operational trade-off. LightGBM achieves MAE=0.930±0.020 months and R2=0.646, significantly outperforming XGBoost (p=0.010) and MLP (p<0.001). Critically, the Hybrid FSA reveals that three support-call behavioral features—training calls (EğitimAramaSayısı), informational calls (BilgiAramaSayısı), and complaint calls (ŞikayetAramaSayısı)—are robustly identified as primary predictors across all three selectors, providing an immediately actionable operational signal for FHIS vendor retention management. Ablation reveals FSA-induced dimensionality reduction yielded no significant improvement in classification F1 (all p>0.05, ns) but led to a non-trivial increase in regression MAE (Relief-F subset: MAE=1.65 vs all-features: MAE=0.93), demonstrating that FSA's contribution lies in interpretability and operational transparency—clarifying the distinct roles of feature selection across classification and regression tasks—rather than incremental predictive gain in Stage 2. Both findings are reported transparently as domain insights.

title: Tight Lower Bounds for Multi-Secretary Problem via Bellman Certificates
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Department of Information, Operations, and Management Sciences

detail.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Multi-Secretary Problem via Bellman Certificates
detail.abstract:
This paper studies additive regret in the multi-secretary problem, measured as the gap between the prophet benchmark and the optimal online policy. Previous work shows that the regret is logarithmic for bounded-density distributions with connected support, while log-squared upper bounds are known for bounded-density distributions with support gaps. Whether this extra logarithmic factor was unavoidable remained open even for the one-resource multi-secretary problem. 
We prove that it is unavoidable. For a mixture of two separated uniform distributions and the critical capacity k T = ⌊qT ⌋, where q is the mass of the upper support, the prophet-online regret is Ω((log T) 2). Thus an O(log T) policy is impossible for this basic gapped instance. This lower bound makes the log-squared upper bounds of Besbes et al. (2024) and, in the broader network revenue management setting with bounded-density continuous reward distributions, Jiang et al. (2025a) tight already in the one-resource specialization. We also prove matching lower bounds for two related distributional regimes studied in Besbes et al. (2024): connected support with density vanishing like distance β near the critical quantile, and separated supports with gap-facing densities vanishing like distance β. 
The proof is based on a Bellman-certificate framework. The optimal prophet-online regret satisfies an exact Bellman recursion. Any feasible certificate for the corresponding Bellman inequality gives a valid regret lower bound. We construct such certificates for the connectedsupport, bounded-density gapped, and gap-facing vanishing-density cases. The framework identifies the mechanism behind the log-squared lower bound: in the gapped case, order-statistic fluctuations generate slack near the support boundaries adjacent to the gap, while the flat empty interval suppresses the finite-difference penalty that would otherwise offset this slack.

title: Workforce Management Challenges in Myanmar SMEs: The Impact of Labor Migration and Economic Crisis on Strategic Decision-Making
affiliations: IMU University

detail.title: Workforce Management Challenges in Myanmar SMEs: The Impact of Labor Migration and Economic Crisis on Strategic Decision-Making

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was conducted in accordance with ethical research standards. Participation was voluntary, and informed consent was obtained from all respondents. The data collected were kept confidential and used solely for academic purposes.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: SMEs play a crucial role in national economy development by creating employment opportunities and poverty reduction, although they face challenges to operate their operations within limited resources. After the pandemic crisis (COVID-19 pandemic) and 2021 political instabilities, SMEs in Myanmar have encountered increasing difficulties in retaining a stable, skilled, and productive workforce. Labor migration, driven by safety concerns, pollical conditions, and economic uncertainty, has intensified workforce shortage, increased competition for talent, and weakened business competitiveness. However, there is critical gap of scientific evidence how the effect of labor migration and economic crisis impact on workforce management challenges and the development of strategic decision-making among SMEs in Myanmar. The current study adopts a quantitative approach and integrates decision-making framework such as the Cynefin framework, the OODA loop, and the PCDA cycle to analyze how SMEs respond to uncertainty. Primary data are collected through self-administered questionnaire from 126 SME owners, managers, and senior staff. The data are analyzed using SPSS (version 27), employing One-way ANOVA, and linear regression. The findings showed that labor migration has a significant negative impact on workforce management, leading to shortages of skilled labor, increased recruitment difficulties, higher wage expectations, and reduced productivity. Moreover, the economic crisis increases operational costs, employee financial stress, and limits investment in workforce development. The results indicate regional differences in how SMEs experience these challenges. Both labor migration and economic instability are found to significantly influence strategic decision-making. SMEs adopt various coping strategies, including offering competitive wages, training employees, hiring temporary staff, and utilizing automation. The study recommends Kotter’s 8-step change model to support long-term organizational resilience and systematic workforce management improvement.

title: Reproducible Multi-Objective Metaheuristic Optimisation of a Physics-Informed Surrogate for Grid-Coupled PEM Electrolysers: NSGA-II Pareto Front, Rolling-Horizon Dispatch, and Conformal Uncertainty Quantification
affiliations: University of Namibia, University of Namibia, University of Namibia and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Reproducible Multi-Objective Metaheuristic Optimisation of a Physics-Informed Surrogate for Grid-Coupled PEM Electrolysers: NSGA-II Pareto Front, Rolling-Horizon Dispatch, and Conformal Uncertainty Quantification

keywords.keywords: PEM water electrolysisPhysics-informed neural networkNSGA-IIRolling-horizon dispatchConformal predictionVariable renewable energyGreen hydrogen

detail.abstract: Operating-point recommendations for proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysers under variable renewable input require reproducibility evidence sufficient for project finance and dispatch latencies compatible with rolling-horizon control. Existing surrogate-driven optimisation pipelines satisfy neither requirement consistently: scalarised single-algorithm metaheuristics return solutions whose reproducibility cannot be assessed across the individual decision-objective components, and deterministic surrogate evaluations expose recommendations to heteroscedastic prediction error in the sparsely-trained operating envelope without uncertainty discounting. This paper develops a unified surrogate-driven optimisation, dispatch, and uncertainty-quantification pipeline that addresses both shortcomings simultaneously. A voltage-targeted physics-informed neural network (PINN) trained on 1,200 PEM operating records serves as the inner-loop surrogate. Five population-based metaheuristics — particle swarm optimisation (PSO), grey wolf optimiser (GWO), whale optimisation algorithm (WOA), honey badger algorithm (HBA), and NSGA-II — are compared on the bi-objective (𝐻2 , SEC) problem. The NSGA-II non-dominated set collapses to two points along an SEC-saturated 𝐻2 ridge at the surrogate’s lower-voltage feasibility bound, exposing a structural feature of the trained surrogate that any deployment must account for. A per-component coefficient of variation (CV) reproducibility diagnostic is introduced and shown to detect algorithm-dependent multimodality that the scalarobjective CV does not: under a 24-hour rolling-horizon dispatch case study driven by measured NASA POWER irradiance for Walvis Bay (Erongo Region, Namibia) on 15 January 2025, the per-component CV(𝐻2 ) crosses 10% at 58 of 96 dispatch intervals (60%), with the per-algorithm exceedance counts ranging from 2 (NSGA-II) to 58 (GWO), while the scalar-objective CV remains below 1% throughout for PSO, WOA, and NSGA-II. A sensitivity analysis on the scalarisation weights (𝑤SEC, 𝑤𝐻2 ) over a 9 × 9 grid identifies the narrow weight band 𝑤𝐻2 ∈ [0.5, 0.6] as operationally robust at the 5% threshold. Split-conformal prediction wrappers calibrated on the validation partition produce 90% prediction intervals (𝑞𝛼 = 0.249 V, mean locally-weighted width 0.510 V) with empirical coverage 0.911 on the held-out test set. The conformal-discounted optimisation reroutes the WOA recommendation from the deterministic boundary point (𝑗, 𝑇 ) = (1.23 A cm−2 , 403 K) to a non-saturating interior point (1.80 A cm−2 , 314 K) that simultaneously increases nominal hydrogen production by 47% and reduces the worst-case voltage uncertainty by 85% — a strict Paretoimprovement that turns the conformal extension into a corrective for boundary-saturated deterministic optima. The combined pipeline is identified as the methodologically defensible approach for surrogatedriven PEM dispatch under variable renewables, with direct application to hyper-scale projects in Namibia and other renewable-rich African settings targeting levelised hydrogen costs of USD 1.50– 2.00 per kilogram.

title: Sustainable Leadership and Learning Organizations in Schools: The Roles of Innovative Work Behavior and Corporate Social Responsibility
affiliations: Firat University, Firat University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sustainable Leadership and Learning Organizations in Schools: The Roles of Innovative Work Behavior and Corporate Social Responsibility
detail.abstract: This study examines how sustainable leadership contributes to learning organizations in public schools through teachers’ innovative work behavior and perceived corporate social responsibility (CSR). Drawing on dynamic capabilities and social exchange theories, the study proposes a moderated mediation model in which innovative work behavior mediates the relationship between sustainable leadership and learning organization capacity, while perceived CSR strengthens this mechanism. Data were collected from 960 teachers working in public K–12 schools in Türkiye and analyzed using structural equation modeling with robust maximum likelihood estimation. The findings indicate that sustainable leadership positively predicts both innovative work behavior and learning organization capacity. Innovative work behavior partially mediated this relationship, whereas perceived CSR significantly moderated both the direct relationship between sustainable leadership and innovative work behavior and the indirect effect on learning organization. Specifically, the indirect effect became stronger under higher levels of perceived CSR. These findings suggest that sustainable leadership contributes to the development of learning organizations not only through direct managerial influence but also through teachers’ innovative behaviors within a socially responsible organizational climate. The study provides theoretical and empirical contributions to the literature on sustainable leadership, organizational learning, and CSR in public-sector educational settings.

title: Stock Return Path Generation and Portfolio Optimization using GAN-VAE Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

detail.title: Stock Return Path Generation and Portfolio Optimization using GAN-VAE Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: Portfolio optimization traditionally relies on historical data, often leading to overfitting and poor generalization due to data scarcity and market non-stationarity. This study proposes an integrated framework combining generative modeling and reinforcement learning (RL) to address these challenges. A hybrid Generative Adversarial Network-Variational Autoencoder (GAN-VAE) generates synthetic daily stock return paths that replicate key empirical characteristics, such as heavy tails and skewness. These synthetic data augment RL training environments, enabling Deep Q-Network (DQN) and tabular Q-learning agents to learn adaptive allocations optimizing the Sharpe ratio. Out-of-sample evaluations on 2023-2024 real data demonstrate DQN's superiority over Q-learning and baselines (equal-weight, buy-and-hold, random-action) in cumulative wealth, maximum drawdown, volatility, and Sharpe ratio. Agents trained on synthetic data match or exceed those with an additional year of real data, highlighting synthetic augmentation's regularization benefits. Results affirm that GAN-VAE synthesis enhances RL data efficiency, yielding robust, risk-adjusted strategies without temporal modeling. This work advances financial machine learning by showing generative models as effective simulators for decision-making under uncertainty, with implications for algorithmic trading and risk management.

title: Learning-Driven Autonomy in Traffic Flow: A multi-modal perception, forecasting and planning
affiliations: Birla Institute of Technology

detail.title: Learning-Driven Autonomy in Traffic Flow: A multi-modal perception, forecasting and planning
detail.abstract: Urban traffic management increasingly requires closed-loop autonomy rather than isolatedestimation, forecasting, or local signal timing. This article develops a learning-drivenautonomy framework for traffic flow management in which traffic evolves through a recurrentbelief–forecast–control loop. The framework integrates: (i) a multimodal belief space thatfuses traffic, infrastructure, temporal, and contextual signals into compact latent statesummaries; (ii) a structured control context encoding current actions, inertia, feasibility, anddwell-time persistence; (iii) an action-aware conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE)that predicts future traffic states under uncertainty; and (iv) a chance-constrained modelpredictive control (MPC) layer that manages congestion risk, queue spillback, and operationalfeasibility. In the present implementation, the multimodal conditioning is instantiated as a104-dimensional vector composed of a 64D context embedding, a 32D control embedding, andan 8D plan embedding. The empirical pipeline compares 10 forecasting variants, performsmulti-seed statistical evaluation, calibrates predictive uncertainty, and studies closed-loopcontrol behavior using the benchmark traffic workflow. The resulting formulation positionstraffic flow management as a problem of learning-driven autonomy under uncertainty ratherthan deterministic traffic prediction alone.

title: Three Frameworks, One Worker? The Demographic Gradient of Automation Risk in Latin America
affiliations: Universidad Adolfo Ibañez and

detail.title: Three Frameworks, One Worker? The Demographic Gradient of Automation Risk in Latin America

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N o conflict of Interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human Subjects
declarations.funderStatement: See acknowledgements

detail.abstract: Latin American economies are entering the Fourth Industrial Revolution with high informality, persistent gender, education, and age inequalities, and limited institutional buffering against technological displacement. Whether automation amplifies those inequalities depends on whether the workers most exposed are also those already disadvantaged. We test this by integrating the three leading automation-risk frameworks-Frey and Osborne (2017), Autor, Levy, and Murnane (2003), and Webb (2020)-as three independent measurements of a latent worker-level exposure, estimated jointly through a generalised linear model with an expectation-maximisation algorithm (Ibrahim, 1990). Using harmonised worker-level microdata from the World Bank's STEP and OECD's PIAAC surveys for seven Latin American economies (Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Mexico, Peru) and an OECD comparison group, we recover the joint skilltask-demographic structure of automation risk under all three frameworks simultaneously. Four findings emerge. First, average automation risk in Latin America ranges from 0.54 in Bolivia (the same as the OECD average) to 0.65 in El Salvador, with the regional premium driven primarily by El Salvador, Mexico, Peru, and Colombia. Second, the education and age gradients converge across all three frameworks: less-educated and younger workers face elevated exposure under Frey-Osborne, Autor, and Webb simultaneously. Third, the gender direction does not converge: under Frey-Osborne and Autor women face higher average risk than men in every LAC country, whereas under Webb's patent-based lens the inverse holds (men face higher average risk than women in every LAC country), a divergence the authors of the underlying estimates also flag explicitly. Fourth, in the subsample of five countries with comparable household-survey data (Bolivia, Chile, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru), occupation-level risk shows a robust negative association with employment growth, particularly for occupations starting in the upper part of the wage distribution under the routine-based frameworks (F&O and Autor); no systematic average wage effect emerges. Automation in Latin America does not strike at random; the education-and-age gradient lands on the same workers under every reasonable definition of the word, while the gender margin reveals which technological frontier — routine or cognitive — a given measurement framework anticipates.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Renewable Energy Forecasting and Its Influence on Economic and Financial Stability
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence in Renewable Energy Forecasting and Its Influence on Economic and Financial Stability
