detail.abstract: While renewable energy systems are now dominating global energy markets, their natural intermittency creates challenges for forecasting energy generation and for maintaining market stability, macroeconomic performance, and the functioning of financial systems downstream. AI has become the necessary technology solution for these prediction needs and can deliver improvements in prediction accuracy of several orders of magnitude compared to conventional, statistically-driven approaches. Although AI technologies for forecasting renewable energy sources have made significant strides, the link between greater accuracy and economic and financial outcomes remains poorly understood and quantified. There is a lack of a unified policy framework and financial institution methodologies to link AI forecasting performance with macroeconomic resilience and financial risk indicators, hindering evidence-based investment and regulatory decisions. The present study develops and validates an integrated AI–Renewable Energy–Economic–Financial Stability (IREEF) framework, aims to evaluate the economic and financial stability benefits of AI-based renewable energy forecasting, and provides evidence-driven policy advice on AI-based energy economics. This methodological approach is a hybrid that combines deep learning architectures (Bidirectional LSTM, CNN-LSTM hybrid, Transformer-based models) with panel econometric methods (System GMM estimation, Johansen cointegration, Granger causality, GARCH volatility modeling). Data span 40 economies over 2005–2023. To measure the effectiveness of the proposed model, the study employs 10 AI models, starting with ARIMA and SVR, then moving to CNN-LSTM and Transformer, with results from both combinations displayed. To quantify the effectiveness of the proposed model, the study uses 10 AI architectures, ranging from ARIMA and SVR to CNN-LSTM and Transformer, and shows the performance of both combinations. A 10 percentage point increase in the accuracy of AI forecasts leads to an 8.3% decrease in energy price volatility, a 6.7-point increase in Economic Stability Index scores, and a 14.2 basis point decrease in financial system risk exposure. The carbon intensity in the Integrated AI+RE scenario is 42%, and the Financial Stability Index is 88. Economies with high levels of AI use (index > 0.88) and high renewable energy penetration (> 45%) perform significantly better on ESG scores, have a lower sovereign credit risk premium, and have 2.8 percentage points higher sustainable GDP growth per year than those with low AI-RE integration.

title: OccluSAR: Bio-Inspired Multi-Stage Optimization for Real-Time Underwater Human Detection in Search and Rescue
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: OccluSAR: Bio-Inspired Multi-Stage Optimization for Real-Time Underwater Human Detection in Search and Rescue
detail.abstract: Underwater search and rescue (SAR) operations require robust human detection systems that perform reliably under the severe visual degradations that may arise as a result of turbidity, occlusion, and variable illumination. This paper describes OccluSAR, a deployment-oriented underwater human detection framework that systematically combines SAR-specific dataset augmentation, architecture selection, and post-training inference optimization to improve reliability in difficult underwater scenes. The proposed system used  YOLOv8m with Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) and Artificial Protozoa Optimization (APO) and it  was observed to have the best balance between accuracy and efficiency among multiple architectures. Without additional retraining, post-training inference optimization achieved an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 85.25% with recall improving to 98.66%, while maintaining real-time performance. Qualitative studies validate the improved localization of partially occluded human targets. The proposed OccluSAR detector offers a practical solution with real-time functionality for underwater SAR applications where minimization of missed detections is crucial.

title: The Riksbank Liquidity Vacuum: High-Frequency Evidence of Monetary Policy Transmission Friction

detail.title: The Riksbank Liquidity Vacuum: High-Frequency Evidence of Monetary Policy Transmission Friction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Standard econometric models exhibit latency and aggregation limitations when evaluating high-frequency microstructure dynamics. To bypass these constraints, this study introduces an event-driven computational infrastructure. The architecture executes vectorized processing of high-fidelity Top-of-Book tick data to quantify the EUR/SEK liquidity vacuum surrounding Riksbank interest rate announcements. The analysis relies on retail ECN pricing as a scale-invariant proxy for primary interbank venues. The core detection methodology applies an empirically calibrated 5.3-sigma anomaly threshold (Z > 5.3). This isolates systemic bid-ask spread expansions from exogenous Eurozone noise. Within a longitudinal sample of monetary policy shocks (N = 69) spanning 2014 to 2026, the engine records a global vacuum hit rate of 63.8%. Structural liquidity withdrawal manifests at a mean temporal offset (delta t) of 91.70 seconds preceding official rate publications. This anticipatory shift imposes a mean execution penalty of 3.85 basis points (BPS) on uninformed participants.

Microstructural decay does not operate as a continuous mathematical function. It manifests as a discrete phase transition. The structural comparison utilizes a Bayesian Beta-Binomial framework to evaluate regime-dependent liquidity dynamics across constrained samples. This generative architecture directly models the latent probability of liquidity failure. It bypasses the continuous asymptotic assumptions typically forced onto binary data. The transition from the 2022-2024 high-inflation shock into the 2025-2026 normalization phase tracks a severe drop in adverse selection. This stabilization survives strict prior sensitivity checks. The posterior difference maintains a strictly positive 94% Highest Density Interval (HDI) even when subjected to pessimistic historical failure rates. The recovery of market depth is a physical reality, not a statistical artifact.

Microstructural evidence points towards a non-linear Regime Vulnerability. A multifactor regression utilizing heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors (HC3) isolates the endogenous shock from broader Eurozone turbulence. Maximum liquidity degradation occurs exclusively at the intersection of a local policy surprise and elevated global uncertainty. When European equity volatility (VSTOXX) crosses a calculated threshold of 19.6, the market ceases to absorb information smoothly. Liquidity fractures.

Mapping the physical mechanics of this collapse requires mixed-distribution sampling. A Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) extracts the posterior states. Pareto Smoothed Importance Sampling Leave-One-Out (PSIS-LOO) cross-validation mathematically rejects continuous linear scaling in favor of a bimodal architecture. With a 98.6% posterior probability of direction, the interaction effect confirms algorithmic liquidity withdrawal operates as a deterministic transaction tax. Facing acute information asymmetry, liquidity providers execute a preemptive, coordinated retreat. This mechanism suggests that central bank communication design directly dictates market depth during policy shocks.

title: Spatio-temporal Evolution and Network Structure of Water Consumption Rebound Effect in the Yellow River Basin
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Guizhou University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Spatio-temporal Evolution and Network Structure of Water Consumption Rebound Effect in the Yellow River Basin
detail.abstract: To investigate the spatiotemporal evolution and spatial network characteristics of the water resource consumption rebound effect (WRE) in the Yellow River Basin, this study uses panel data from 91 prefecture-level cities in the basin based on data from 2010 to 2023. Exploratory spatial data analysis, a modified gravity model, and social network analysis are employed. The results show that: temporally, the WRE exhibited a pattern of “fluctuating increase–accelerated growth,” with an average value of 0.174 during the study period. The upward trend accelerated following the implementation of the national strategy in 2019. Spatially, the WRE showed significant positive spatial autocorrelation and formed an “east-to-west” gradient pattern characterized by lower WRE in the east and higher WRE in the west. Downstream cities achieved negative rebound through technological upgrading, whereas resource-based cities in the middle and upper reaches maintained relatively high rebound levels due to industrial structure constraints. In terms of network structure, the average density of the spatial association network was 0.164, and the network connectivity remained at 1. Network efficiency showed an increasing trend, and intercity linkages became increasingly close. Regarding block functions, the four major blocks exhibited differentiated characteristics of “net spillover–broker–net beneficiary–bidirectional spillover.” The broker block played a critical bridging role in cross-regional transmission. The WRE in the Yellow River Basin demonstrates significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity and spatial dependence. Differentiated and coordinated governance strategies should therefore be adopted for different blocks to provide policy references for coordinated water resource regulation across the basin.

title: The Iberian Blackout: A Black Swan or a Gray Rhino? A Protection-Aware Dynamic Voltage Security Assessment
affiliations: Vanderbilt University and Vanderbilt University

detail.title: The Iberian Blackout: A Black Swan or a Gray Rhino? A Protection-Aware Dynamic Voltage Security Assessment
detail.abstract: On 28 April 2025, the Iberian mainland power system collapsed after a rapid voltage rise, widespread generation disconnections, and loss of synchronism. The ENTSO-E Expert Panel final report attributes the blackout to multiple interacting factors including ineffective voltage control, fixed power factor reactive behavior, fast generation ramps, protection settings not aligned with requirements, slow or unavailable reactive absorption, and limited observability outside the transmission system. This paper uses the incident as a motivating case for a broader operational voltage security problem: given the present grid state, can the next plausible trip, ramp, topology action, or shunt action push protected downstream voltages above relay thresholds before available voltage controls can respond? We develop a protection-aware dynamic voltage security assessment for this question. Starting from a nonlinear hybrid differential-algebraic equation (DAE) model, we derive mode wise finite window voltage maps that include automatic voltage regulators (AVRs), inverter-based resources (IBRs), static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs), high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) links, loads, shunts, transformers, protection functions, and limiter behavior whenever the corresponding models are available. We define normalized overvoltage margin erosion at the protection measurement side and time resolved lower bounds on useful control response. We then develop a monotone pickup cascade screen, robust data-limited certificates under uncertain relay and protected-voltage data, and a mitigation optimization that computes the minimum fast reactive action needed to keep protected voltages below relay thresholds. Case studies on a 2000-bus mechanism replica and multiple dynamic benchmark systems show that the screen predicts nonlinear cascade propagation, ranks risky operator actions, identifies missing-data limits, and computes useful fast-control actions before nonlinear simulation is run. The implementation and replication artifacts are made publicly available to support reproducible studies of protection-driven overvoltage cascades and to enable researchers to test new screening, uncertainty, and mitigation methods.

title: Carbon Taxes and Banking Stability: A Prudential Analysis for Chile
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Carbon Taxes and Banking Stability: A Prudential Analysis for Chile
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the potential prudential effects of an increase in carbon taxation on the banking sector in Chile. Using micro-level data on firms and their credit relationships with banks, we estimate how higher carbon taxes affect firms’ probability of default (PD) and translate these effects into changes in bank capital requirements through provisions and risk-weighted assets. The results suggest that the PD of firms in the electricity sector could increase significantly following higher carbon taxes, with additional effects observed across other industries. At the system level, an increase in the carbon tax to USD 200 per ton of CO₂ emitted would reduce capital adequacy ratios by up to 6 basis points, corresponding to losses equivalent to 6 basis points of total assets. Moreover, some institutions could experience declines in capital adequacy levels of up to 14 basis points. The main limitations of the analysis are the uncertainty regarding the future path of carbon taxation and the absence of firms’ dynamic adaptation mechanisms.

title: Impact of Prediction Error Characteristics on Energy Storage Economics for Photovoltaic Power Trading: A Model-Agnostic Parametric Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Impact of Prediction Error Characteristics on Energy Storage Economics for Photovoltaic Power Trading: A Model-Agnostic Parametric Analysis
detail.abstract: The economic viability of battery energy storage systems (BESS) for mitigating deviation penalties in photovoltaic (PV) power trading depends critically on the statistical characteristics of prediction errors, not merely on the choice of prediction algorithm. This paper presents a model-agnostic framework that quantifies the risk-adjusted economic value of degradation-aware BESS as a continuous function of two error parameters: dispersion σ and tail heaviness ν. Closed-form expressions are derived for expected deviation penalty, optimal BESS capacity, and degradation cost using a t location-scale error model, cycle-aging formulation, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) metric. A parametric analysis over a wide range of (σ, ν) combinations reveals that the penalty increases more than proportionally with dispersion, with halving σ reducing optimal BESS capacity by 55-68%. Heavy-tailed errors (ν < 5) widen the CVaR-based risk premium by 5-11% relative to near-Gaussian errors, establishing tail weight as a first-order economic determinant. Degradation-aware sizing further reduces optimal capacity by 18-26% while improving the benefit-cost ratio. Applied to a 30-MW PV case study, the framework shows that BESS investment becomes economically viable (BCR > 1) at penalty factors of α ≥ 1.5, with the exact threshold depending on the prediction error characteristics.

title: Discharge Coefficient Prediction of Throttling Devices Based on Multi-Fidelity Transfer Learning Model
affiliations: China University of Petroleum (East China), China University of Petroleum (East China) - College of Pipeline and Civil Engineering, China University of Petroleum (East China) - College of Pipeline and Civil Engineering, China University of Petroleum (East China) - College of Pipeline and Civil Engineering, China University of Petroleum (Huadong), China University of Petroleum (East China), China University of Petroleum (East China), China University of Petroleum (East China) - College of Pipeline and Civil Engineering, China University of Petroleum (East China) and China University of Petroleum (East China) - College of Pipeline and Civil Engineering

detail.title: Discharge Coefficient Prediction of Throttling Devices Based on Multi-Fidelity Transfer Learning Model
detail.abstract: The determination of the discharge coefficient of throttling devices is a key task in the field of fluid measurement. However, high cost calibration seriously restricts the construction and development of high-precision models. This study proposes a multi-fidelity transfer learning deep neural network (MF-TL-DNN) model, which establishes a mapping relationship between the flow structure features of the throttling device and the discharge coefficient, aiming to achieve fast and accurate prediction of the discharge coefficient of the throttling device. The model adopts a two-stage training paradigm of "pre-training and transfer fine-tuning", fully utilizing the complementary information between low-fidelity simulation data and high-fidelity experimental data, fine-tuning with 26 sets of experimental data can achieve cross domain feature alignment and model detail calibration, and using a 5 fold cross validation strategy to verify the stability of the model. Finally, the MF-TL-DNN model was compared with single low-fidelity model (SLFM), single high-fidelity model (SHFM), and Co-Kriging model. The research results demonstrate that the MF-TL-DNN model can use the least amount of high-fidelity training data to approach the most realistic discharge coefficient calibration results, and has better prediction accuracy and generalization ability on the high-fidelity test sets. It provides an effective solution for predicting the discharge coefficient of throttling devices under high-fidelity data scarcity conditions.

title: A Composite Indicator Framework for Measuring Tourism Contributions to the SDGs in Data-Scarce Territories: Evidence from Carchi, Ecuador
affiliations: Universidad Politécnica Estatal del Carchi and Universidad Politécnica Estatal del Carchi

detail.title: A Composite Indicator Framework for Measuring Tourism Contributions to the SDGs in Data-Scarce Territories: Evidence from Carchi, Ecuador
detail.abstract: Measuring tourism contributions to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains challenging in subnational territories where data are scarce and fragmented. This study develops and applies the Tourism SDG Composite Assessment Framework (TSDG-CAF), a composite indicator framework designed to assess observable tourism contributions to the SDGs in Carchi, Ecuador. The framework integrates surveys, semi-structured interviews, tourism registry data, territorial development plans, ordinances, and environmental and cultural heritage documents. Five SDGs were prioritized: SDG 8, SDG 11, SDG 12, SDG 15, and SDG 17, due to their links with decent work, sustainable communities, responsible consumption, biodiversity conservation, and multi-stakeholder governance. The framework is structured into two complementary indices: the Tourism SDG Performance Index (TSDGPI), which measures sector-level tourism performance, and the Territorial Enabling Conditions Index (TECI), which assesses territorial conditions that enable or constrain tourism sustainability. Results reveal moderate sector-level tourism performance, with critical gaps in disability inclusion, accessibility, and inclusive tourism training. In contrast, all cantons showed high territorial enabling conditions. This gap suggests that territorial planning, ordinances, cultural heritage, and environmental assets do not automatically translate into sustainable tourism practices. The study contributes a traceable, adaptable, and replicable methodological architecture for assessing tourism-related SDG performance in rural, border, heritage, natural, or emerging destinations with limited data availability.

title: Evaluating the influence of weather uncertainty on resilience and cost-optimality in urban energy systems design optimization
affiliations: Technical University of Munich, Technical University of Munich, Technical University of Munich and Technical University of Munich

detail.title: Evaluating the influence of weather uncertainty on resilience and cost-optimality in urban energy systems design optimization
detail.abstract: The increasing share of weather-dependent renewable energy sources amplifies the influence of weather uncertainty on the design of urban energy systems. Consequently, selecting representative weather years has become a critical challenge for ensuring resilient and cost-optimal system configurations. However, the impact of different weather years and design approaches on system resilience has not yet been systematically assessed. This study investigates how weather years affect the outcome of deterministic urban energy system design optimization approaches, including perfect-foresight and rolling-horizon optimization. Furthermore, the influence of demand-side flexibility on system resilience is evaluated. An urban energy system optimization model focused on the heating sector, with jointly optimizing district heating network expansion and building-specific supply technologies, is applied. System resilience is assessed using the indicators loss-of-load, loss-of-load duration (stability), robustness, and cost-optimality across 68 historical and future weather years. The results show that robustness increases exponentially with the calculated design peak demand. Demand-side flexibility mainly improves system stability by reducing the 95th percentile of the sequential loss-of-load duration from approximately 100 to below 15 hours. The typical meteorological year performs worse than most actual weather years, yielding the 17th-highest median cumulative loss-of-load with 842 MWh. The design year 2018 results in the most robust system configuration, with zero hours of load loss, but also the highest system costs. However, future weather years derived from IPCC scenarios demonstrate high robustness with improved cost-effectiveness.  The best trade-off between cost-optimality and robustness is achieved using the design year 1971. Overall, the findings demonstrate that weather-year selection strongly influences the outcomes of urban energy system design. Furthermore, the proposed rolling-horizon optimization approach enhances system robustness, underscoring the importance of accounting for additional peak capacities in the design process.

reference: Intertax, volume 52, issue Issue 5, 2024[10.54648/taxi2024040]
title: Tax Incentives and Private Saving in Sub-Saharan Africa: Using Taxation to Incentivize Saving
affiliations: University Leipzig,  and University Leipzig

detail.title: Tax Incentives and Private Saving in Sub-Saharan Africa: Using Taxation to Incentivize Saving
detail.abstract: Tax-based saving promotion programs are gaining global attention as a means of mobilizing funds for domestic investment, increasing employment levels, and consequently generating greater economic growth. Despite this, such programs have remained an exception in Sub-Saharan Africa. Whereas the study of saving promotion schemes in the region has been of high interest, no attempts have been made to study how tax policy could be used to augment these efforts. This article contributes to alleviating this deficiency by linking saving promotion schemes with tax policy. The authors use descriptive statistics of region-and country-specific data to assess Sub-Saharan Africa's private saving landscape and its current use of tax incentives. Through a systematic literature analysis, the article reveals heterogeneous challenges to private saving in the region subsequently leading to inherently low saving levels. Consequently, tax-policy interventions to boost savings in the region remain impractical, especially if the region's current political economy, business, and demographic environment remain the same. The key barriers to private saving are evaluated, and multidimensional policy suggestions are made for improving the use of tax-based incentives. While the policy recommendations have been specifically tailored for Sub-Saharan Africa's local socioeconomic circumstances, some of them may apply well to other low-middle-income countries (LMIC) that share similar or related characteristics.

title: DANTE: A Lightweight Hybrid CNN‐Transformer Network for Efficient Image Classification
affiliations: Instituto Politécnico Nacional

detail.title: DANTE: A Lightweight Hybrid CNN‐Transformer Network for Efficient Image Classification
detail.abstract: Abstract.,Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved remarkable accuracy but suffer from high computational and memory costs, typically relying on large‐scale pre‐training. Hybrid CNN‐Transformer models attempt to combine local feature extraction with global attention, yet most suffer from redundant fusion, parameter inefficiency, or dependence on pre‐trained backbones. We propose DANTE_Optimized, a lightweight hybrid architecture designed to be trained from scratch on small‐to‐medium datasets. DANTE introduces: (i) a three‐stage convolutional stem that aggressively downsamples spatial resolution while expanding channels, producing a compact token sequence; (ii) a multi‐head self‐attention module with learnable relative positional bias (DanteAttention) that generalises across input sizes; and (iii) a hierarchy of Transformer blocks with pre‐LayerNorm, gated MLP, and residual connections, using only 7.1 M parameters. Without any pre‐training or external data, DANTE is evaluated on five benchmarks (CIFAR‐10, CIFAR‐100, Tiny ImageNet, STL‐10, SVHN) against ResNet50, EfficientNet‐B0, MobileNetV3, and ConvNeXt‐Tiny under identical training protocols. DANTE achieves the highest top‐1 accuracy on CIFAR‐100 (67.26%, +5.0 pp over ResNet50) and SVHN (96.14%), while using 3‐4× fewer parameters. On CIFAR‐10 it matches ResNet50 (87.68% vs 88.26%) with a 3.3× parameter reduction. Ablation studies confirm that the convolutional stem is critical (removing it drops accuracy by 13 pp) and that depth=6 offers a better efficiency‐accuracy trade‐off. Although DANTE has higher FLOPs than pure CNNs (0.44 G vs 0.08 G on 32×32 inputs), its parameter efficiency makes it ideal for memory‐constrained deployment. Code and benchmark are open‐source and reproducible on Apple Silicon.

title: The Dialectical Space: Resolving the Semantic Translation Gap in Disjoint Neural Experts via Contrastive Alignment
affiliations: , , University of Salerno, University of Salerno and University of Salerno

detail.title: The Dialectical Space: Resolving the Semantic Translation Gap in Disjoint Neural Experts via Contrastive Alignment
detail.abstract: Neural experts are often combined only after they have already reached their conclusions. Nevertheless, when each expert observes only a fragment of the world, final predictions may conceal the very evidence needed for collective understanding. This paper examines whether independently trained neural experts can move beyond static ensembling and instead exchange intermediate representations that are meaningful to one another.We introduce the Dialectical Space, a latent-communication framework for decentralised inference under strictly disjoint observations. In a horizontally partitioned MNIST setting, one expert observes only the upper half of each digit while another observes only the lower half. Since their latent spaces are trained independently, their internal representations are not directly interchangeable. We identify this incompatibility as the Semantic Translation Gap and address it by training bidirectional latent translators with a cross-view supervised contrastive objective. During inference, each expert selectively incorporates translated evidence from its partner through a receiver-side entropy gate, allowing uncertain experts to listen more while confident experts resist potentially harmful influence.Across five seeds, the final SupCon-aligned Dialectical Space achieves 98.12\% ± 0.11 accuracy, improving over a strong Late Fusion baseline at 97.60\% ± 0.08. Ablations show that naïve latent exchange can propagate errors, MSE alignment plateaus, and instance-level contrastive alignment suffers from false negatives. The key improvement emerges only when latent translation is both class-structured and uncertainty-gated.These results suggest that decentralised neural systems can benefit not merely from aggregating predictions, but from learning how to translate, negotiate, and selectively accept intermediate evidence. The study provides a controlled step toward collaborative latent reasoning among disjoint neural experts, while leaving privacy, bandwidth, real-time deployment, and general multimodal robustness as open challenges.

title: How Reliable are Behavioral Estimates from Neural Choice Models?
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS), Ajou University, , Arizona State University (ASU) - School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment and National University of Singapore (NUS)

detail.title: How Reliable are Behavioral Estimates from Neural Choice Models?
detail.abstract: Neural network-based discrete choice models (neural DCMs) have demonstrated consistent gains in predictive accuracy over classical econometric specifications due to their flexible functional form. Yet, the reliability of their behavioral outputs for statistical inference has received little scrutiny. This paper argues that inference variance in neural DCMs arises from two conceptually distinct sources: sampling uncertainty from finite sample variability, and optimization uncertainty arising from non-convex loss surfaces and over-identification, where different initializations of neural weights converge to different utility function shapes. This decomposition is critical because the two sources have different remedies: sampling uncertainty shrinks with more data, but optimization uncertainty does not and instead threatens the reproducibility of behavioral inference. To separately quantify these two uncertainties, we apply a bootstrap decomposition framework across different model specifications under two Monte Carlo simulation studies of increasing complexity. The results confirm four hypotheses motivated by the structural properties of these architectures. First, Multinomial Logit (MNL) exhibits confident misspecification, with narrow uncertainty bands that conceal large systematic bias. Second, DCMs based on unconstrained neural networks suffer from substantial optimization uncertainty that renders single-run inferences unreliable. Third, regularization in the Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) reduces optimization uncertainty in simpler settings, but posterior uncertainty becomes increasingly miscalibrated as preference heterogeneity compounds; yet, wide credible bands fail to cover the bias induced by prior shrinkage. Fourth, the Monotonic Neural Network (MNN) achieves the best bias-variance trade-off across both studies, as behavioral constraints simultaneously enforce interpretability and stabilize the optimization landscape, yielding a more favorable decomposition than either classical econometric models or unconstrained neural networks. These findings directly address the need for rigorous uncertainty quantification in neural DCMs, where behavioral outputs such as willingness-to-pay and elasticities inform consequential policy decisions yet are routinely reported without accounting for optimization-induced variability.

title: EAGLE: An Element-Aware Graph Learning Engine for Hybrid Mesh Smoothing
affiliations: National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology, Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, Dalian University of Technology, Zhejiang University, Dalian University of Technology and National University of Defense Technology

detail.title: EAGLE: An Element-Aware Graph Learning Engine for Hybrid Mesh Smoothing
detail.abstract: Hybrid meshes are widely adopted in industry due to their generation efficiency and superior capability to balance computational accuracy and cost. However, initially generated hybrid meshes often compromise element regularity to guarantee topological validity and boundary fitting, making mesh smoothing an indispensable post-processing procedure to rectify local distortions. Since heterogeneous elements in hybrid meshes involve divergent optimization objectives, most existing smoothing methods remain restricted to isomorphic meshes such as all-triangular or all-quadrilateral meshes. Furthermore, the majority of current approaches struggle to effectively eliminate negative-area elements, which severely limits their practical applicability in complex scenarios.To address these challenges, we proposes EAGLE, an Element-Aware Graph Learning Engine, for unsupervised hybrid mesh smoothing. The framework integrates three key components: (1) a lightweight graph neural network to extract features of heterogeneous mesh elements, (2) a geometric constraint module to maintain structural consistency during the smoothing process, and (3) a plug-and-play loss function to support end-to-end unsupervised optimization. Extensive experiments conducted on surface meshes with several geometries verify that the proposed method achieves superior performance over existing baselines across various evaluation metrics. Notably, the EAGLE shows impressive robustness through its zero-shot generalization when applied to isomorphic meshes.

title: Deep Learning Model Fusion for Short-term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
affiliations: China Three Gorges Corporation and China Three Gorges Corporation

detail.title: Deep Learning Model Fusion for Short-term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
detail.abstract: The volatility and randomness of solar power generation pose significant challenges to the stable and safe operation of the power grid. Improving the accuracy of photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is therefore crucial for integrating renewable energy into the grid. Machine learning and deep learning models are the mainstream approaches for PV power forecasting. However, PV forecasting is often affected by multiple factors, such as weather, season, and temperature, which a single model may fail to fully capture. To address this issue, this paper adopts an ensemble learning approach to combine the strengths of multiple deep learning models, thereby improving PV power forecasting accuracy. After data preprocessing, key meteorological influencing factors are identified based on correlation analysis. The weighted power data from the three historical samples with daily irradiance most similar to the target day are used as model inputs. The base models include MLP, GRU, Transformer, LSTM, and Attention-LSTM. For ensemble learning, GLM, SVR, LightGBM, and GBDT are selected as meta-models for comparison. Empirical results validate the effectiveness of deep learning model fusion, showing that the proposed fusion approach improves forecasting accuracy by 3% to 8%, outperforming all individual base models.

title: Internal versus External Innovation: The Role of Competition in Shaping Productivity Returns
affiliations: University of Tennessee, Knoxville - College of Agricultural Sciences and Natural Resources - Department of Agricultural Economics and Kyungpook National University

detail.title: Internal versus External Innovation: The Role of Competition in Shaping Productivity Returns
detail.abstract: While existing research focuses on how competition shapes R&D investment levels, less attention has been paid to how competitive environments affect the productivity returns of different innovation strategies. This study examines how internal and external R&D influence firm-level productivity under varying degrees of market competition. Using firm-level panel data from South Korea (2006–2018), we estimate total factor productivity and address endogeneity through a fixed-effects instrumental variable approach. We distinguish between internal and external R&D as two distinct innovation channels and show that their productivity and spillover effects vary systematically with market competition.The results reveal that internal R&D generates stronger direct productivity gains, particularly in highly competitive, low-markup environments where firms face strong pressure to improve efficiency. In contrast, knowledge spillovers are more pronounced in less competitive, high-markup markets, where firms can better absorb and internalize external knowledge. Spillovers associated with external R&D are generally more substantial than those from internal R&D, highlighting the role of external knowledge sourcing in industry-wide diffusion. These findings contribute to the literature on innovation strategy and knowledge diffusion by showing that internal capability building and external knowledge sourcing play complementary roles in productivity growth, and that their effectiveness depends critically on market structure.

title: A Lightweight Spiking SOM for Unsupervised Topological Clustering
affiliations: University of Alcala, University of Alcala, University of Alcala and University of Alcala

detail.title: A Lightweight Spiking SOM for Unsupervised Topological Clustering
detail.abstract: This work presents a lightweight unsupervised Spiking Neural Network inspired by Self-Organizing Maps and Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity. The proposed learning rule applies STDP only to the winning output neuron for each input sample and propagates the resulting synaptic update to the remaining neurons through a distance-dependent neighborhood factor. This strategy preserves the topological organization of SOMs while reducing the number of direct STDP updates required during training. The model is evaluated on MNIST, where it achieves 87.36\% accuracy with a 14$\times$14 output grid after one training epoch, while also producing spatially coherent class clusters. The results show that the proposed approach is not intended to outperform larger SNN-SOM models in accuracy, but rather to provide a compact baseline for unsupervised topological clustering under resource constraints.

title: The Exploration of Complementary Knowledge Distillation

detail.title: The Exploration of Complementary Knowledge Distillation
detail.abstract: We study how overlap between teacher and student training sets affects knowledge distillation. We introduce an $\alpha$-overlap framework that continuously varies the fraction of shared samples and evaluate its effect on generalization across four benchmark datasets. Complementary partitioning ($\alpha=0$) often reduces the student's generalization gap, with the strongest effect on Glass ($\Delta=-0.055$, $p<0.01$), whereas the benefit largely vanishes under full overlap ($\alpha=1$). This effect remains robust across teacher--student allocation ratios $\beta \in [0.2,0.6]$ when the student retains sufficient data. A comparison with label smoothing shows that complementary distillation can provide regularization beyond generic soft-target smoothing on some datasets, but this advantage is conditional rather than universal. These results suggest that data complementarity is a useful but dataset-dependent factor in the regularization effect of knowledge distillation.

title: CARE-ECG: A Capacity-Aware Clinical Review Agent for Safer Electrocardiogram Deployment Under Limited Review Capacity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: CARE-ECG: A Capacity-Aware Clinical Review Agent for Safer Electrocardiogram Deployment Under Limited Review Capacity
detail.abstract: Deep learning has substantially advanced electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis, but most prior studies focus on diagnosis rather than on deployment-time decisions about when automated outputs are sufficiently trustworthy to bypass clinician review. We developed CARE-ECG, a capacity-aware clinical review agent that combines an SSL-pretrained ECG foundation model with structured physiologic evidence to estimate review risk and decide whether an ECG should be automatically accepted or deferred under limited review capacity. CARE-ECG was evaluated in pooled multi-center deployment, bidirectional cross-center transfer, and PTB-XL external validation. At a fixed 15% review budget, CARE-ECG consistently outperformed confidence-only triage. In pooled evaluation, accepted error decreased from 18.9% to 15.8% and review precision increased from 55.3% to 72.0%. In Georgia-to-Zhengzhou transfer, accepted error decreased from 33.3% to 26.0% and review precision increased from 38.2% to 77.1%. On PTB-XL, accepted error decreased from 45.8% to 40.2% and review precision increased from 63.0% to 95.2%. These gains translated into higher clinical utility, with captured errors per 1,000 ECGs increasing from 83 to 108 in pooled evaluation and from 57 to 116 in Georgia-to-Zhengzhou transfer. Under strict exact-budget control, the reason-aware extension further improved safety, particularly at the 30% operating point. CARE-ECG functions as a deployment-time safety layer that makes the accepted set safer and prioritizes clinician review toward higher-risk tracings.

title: Enhancing YOLO Robustness Against Adversarial Patch Attacks Using Multimodal Detection and Image Restoration
affiliations: American International University Bangladesh, American International University Bangladesh, American International University Bangladesh, American International University Bangladesh and American International University Bangladesh

detail.title: Enhancing YOLO Robustness Against Adversarial Patch Attacks Using Multimodal Detection and Image Restoration
detail.abstract: Adversarial patch attacks pose a significant threat to real-time object detection systems by introducing localized perturbations that suppress valid detections while remaining physically realizable in the real world. This vulnerability is particularly critical for YOLO-based detectors applied in surveillance, autonomous systems, robotics, and edge AI applications. To address this challenge, we propose a multimodal adversarial patch defense framework that integrates adversarial patch generation, detection, and image restoration within a unified pipeline. The proposed defense fuses convolutional neural network (CNN) spatial features, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-based frequency descriptors, and saliency-driven gradient features to accurately identify adversarial regions. The detected patches were subsequently neutralized using an inpainting-based restoration process before the downstream YOLO inference. A study on the INRIA Person dataset demonstrated that adversarial patches drastically degrade clean detection performance from 0.926 to 0.046 mAP@0.5, while the RFAConv-enhanced ADYOLO sustains 0.253 under attack. The proposed multimodal defense achieved the best recovery performance with 0.482 mAP@0.5, substantially outperforming Gaussian filtering, JPEG compression, LGS, and SAC-style baselines. Ablation, transferability, and statistical robustness analyses further validated the effectiveness and generalizability of the framework for enhancing adversarial resilience in YOLO-based detectors.

title: Increasing Milk Production and Milk Quality with Supplementation of Forage Legumes in Small-scale Dairy Farmers of Rwanda
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Rwanda Agriculture Board

detail.title: Increasing Milk Production and Milk Quality with Supplementation of Forage Legumes in Small-scale Dairy Farmers of Rwanda
detail.abstract: Low dietary protein and poor- quality forages continue to limit productivity in smallholder dairy systems in Rwanda. This study evaluated the effects of incorporating forage legumes into grass- based diets on milk yield and milk composition of crossbred dairy cows managed under smallholder conditions. Experimental diets were formulated by mixing grass with 0,15, and 30% forage legumes (Calliandra C, Leucaena L, and Desmodium I in even proportions).  Feed samples from each diet were collected weekly, dried, ground, and analyzed for dry matter, crude protein, and mineral content using standard AOAC methods to confirm nutrient composition. Diets were formulated to be isonitrogenous (17% CP) and isocaloric (2.2 Mcal/kg DM). Six Freisian x Ankole lactating crossbred dairy cows (415±40.3kg BW kg) were assigned to the three dietary treatments using a replicated 3 x 3 Latin square for 3 periods, each period made of 7d of adaptation and 7 days of data collection. Cows were fed diets at 3% BW on a DM basis and were fed twice a day. Milk yield and dry matter intake (DMI) were daily recorded during the collection period. Milk samples collected at the end of each period were analyzed for crude protein (CP) and Crude fat. Data were analyzed using the GLM procedure of RStudio 4.4.2. Legume supplementation significantly increased milk yield from 5. 7 L/day to 6. 1 L/day (p = 0. 04). Milk crude protein and fat content were not affected by dietary treatment(p> 0. 05). Dry matter intake increased numerically from 12. 4 to 13. 3 kg/day with legume inclusion. Average daily gain (0. 4 to 0. 0.5kg/day) and feed conversion ratio (2. 6 to 2.0. 0) showed numerically improved values but were not statistically significant. These findings indicate that moderate inclusion of forage legumes (15% - 30%) in grass- based diets enhances nutrient quality, increases feed intake, improves milk production, and promotes animal growth without affecting milk composition. Integrating legumes such as Calliandra C, Leucaena L, and Desmodium I, into smallholder feeding systems represents a practical strategy to improve dairy cow performance while reducing dependence on expensive commercial concentrates.

title: Combined Standardized AUC: A Robust Metric for Multi-Class Model Evaluation and Selection
affiliations: University of Central Florida, The University of Texas at El Paso and University of Central Florida

detail.title: Combined Standardized AUC: A Robust Metric for Multi-Class Model Evaluation and Selection
detail.abstract: Model performance metrics are fundamental to the model selection process, as they balance accuracy, fairness, and task-specific objectives. This study introduces the Combined Standardized Area Under the Curve (CS-AUC) as a robust and comprehensive metric for evaluating multiclass classification models, particularly within the Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) framework. The proposed CS-AUC exhibits four major advantages. First, it accommodates both ordinal and nominal multiclass classification tasks. Second, in contrast to conventional metrics, it is independent of arbitrarily chosen probability thresholds. Third, its standardization procedure alleviates the effects of class imbalance, which is a persistent challenge in multi-class problems. Lastly, it enables fair and consistent comparisons across models and datasets while quantifying the uncertainty. In addition, the CS-AUC achieves greater efficiency and accuracy than the multiclass AUC (MAUC) optimization method introduced by Yang et al. [1], particularly for the large sample sizes commonly encountered in modern data science applications. Compared with additional alternatives such as the Volume Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Surface (VUS), the Hypervolume Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Manifold (HUM) and M metric, which are restricted to prespecified orders among the classes, our proposed method can generalize more broadly.The CS-AUC is constructed using a One-vs-One (OvO) framework across all classes, which an approach shown to be more efficient than the One-vs-All (OvA) design. Each pairwise AUC is standardized using corresponding variance and then aggregated through weighted averaging to produce a single unified metric. This design allows the CS-AUC to generalize across diverse multiclass scenarios while simultaneously addressing class imbalance and ensuring fairness in evaluation. The utility of the proposed metric is validated through both simulated and real-world datasets. Empirical results confirm that our proposed method can provide a robust, interpretable, and computationally efficient tool for model evaluation within the AutoML framework.

title: Optimized Trainable Sample Selection (TSS) for One-Class Classification in High Dimension Space
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Optimized Trainable Sample Selection (TSS) for One-Class Classification in High Dimension Space
detail.abstract: Apart from high dimensional data, the massive number of trainable samples may lead computing challenges for machine learning (ML) applications. For anomaly detection or one-class classification (OCC) tasks; presence of massive number of trainable samples leads to undesired computational overhead especially; for the decision boundary-based classifiers such as support vector data descriptor (SVDD) and one-class support vector machine (OCSVM). For such classifiers, the identification of support vectors (decision boundary points) is the most important concern whereas the other samples do not contribute enough information. With this motivation, the present research proposes an optimized novel trainable samples selection (TSS) technique via means of Gaussian transformation, hyperspherical coordinates (radius and angles in d- dimension space) followed by angular bins. The key assumption of this approach is that the data distribution is Gaussian with identity covariance in nature, and in case of other distribution, the data points must be transformed in Gaussian distribution of the class-of-interest (CoI) samples (target class samples). The proposed approach approximates the convex boundary in angle space. Diverse datasets ( Iris, MNIST, UCI default credit card, Indian Pines, Glass and svmguide) have been experimented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: From Pilot to Policy: Experimental Evidence from Scaling Online Tutoring
affiliations: Ministerio de Inclusi´on, ESADE Center for Economic Policy and World Bank, CUNEF Universidad, , Universidad de Alicante and Instituto de Empresa Business School

detail.title: From Pilot to Policy: Experimental Evidence from Scaling Online Tutoring

detail.abstract: We study a randomized controlled trial of an online mathematics tutoring program scaled from a successful pilot and implemented entirely by regional education authorities in Spain, using interim public-school teachers rather than specially recruited tutors. Assignment to tutoring increased end-ofyear grades by 0.15σ and standardized math test scores by 0.11σ-approximately one-third of pilot effects. An experimental socio-emotional module improved affective outcomes but not academic gains. Results provide realistic benchmarks for the "voltage drop" policymakers should anticipate when scaling evidence-based interventions.

title: Detecting AI in Doctoral Dissertations: An Exploratory Empirical Analysis of EdD Dissertation Integrity and Implications for Doctoral Program Design

detail.title: Detecting AI in Doctoral Dissertations: An Exploratory Empirical Analysis of EdD Dissertation Integrity and Implications for Doctoral Program Design
detail.abstract: This exploratory study examined the level of inappropriate AI usage in doctoral dissertations, specifically across 100 EdD dissertations published in 2025 within the fields of the Educational Leadership and Administration. These fields represent the primary academic home of the Doctor of Education (EdD) degree, which has been the focus of substantial rethinking over the last twenty years in an attempt to refashion the degree to support educational leaders as "practitioner-scholars." This study found that 56% of dissertations contained more than negligible (>10%) AI-generated writing; moreover, 19% of dissertations contained more than 50% AI-generated text. Additional suggestive findings included that lower AI use was correlated with an institution being an R1 or R2 institution, while higher AI use was correlated with an institution being private non-profit. This paper concludes with some thoughts regarding strengthening specific doctoral programmatic features vis-à-vis issues academic integrity and legitimacy and next steps for future research.

title: RAPIDS: A Risk-Adaptive Privacy-Preserving Intelligent Data-Sharing Expert System for IoT-Fog-Cloud Environments
affiliations: and Lecturer

detail.title: RAPIDS: A Risk-Adaptive Privacy-Preserving Intelligent Data-Sharing Expert System for IoT-Fog-Cloud Environments
detail.abstract: This paper presents RAPIDS, a risk-adaptive privacy-preserving intelligent data-sharing expert system for IoT--fog--cloud environments. RAPIDS treats each sharing request as a joint decision problem over sharing action, processing location, and privacy mechanism, and combines hard governance rules, machine-learning-based privacy-risk prediction, multi-objective strategy optimization, and explanation generation to recommend \textit{allow}, \textit{conditional allow}, \textit{deny}, or \textit{expert review}. To evaluate this setting, we construct a fused benchmark from the UCSD ExtraSensory mobile/wearable sensing dataset and 43,927 Android Data Safety Label profiles, preserving real sensing contexts and real app-declaration signals while generating the remaining request context through a reproducible protocol. Experiments on all 60 ExtraSensory users with repeated user-level cross-validation, twelve baselines, five ablations, sensitivity and robustness analysis, statistical testing, and runtime profiling show that RAPIDS improves on interpretable and optimization-based baselines while maintaining zero critical false-allow behavior. RAPIDS also reduces conditional exposure risk, supports calibrated recovery of low-risk \textit{allow} decisions, and completes online decision plus explanation in 0.2908~ms/request. These results show that RAPIDS provides an effective and explainable expert-system layer for privacy-aware IoT data sharing across device, fog, and cloud environments.

title: The Road to Fiscal Armageddon
affiliations: The Wharton School and

detail.title: The Road to Fiscal Armageddon
detail.abstract: We study how sovereign fiscal stress builds before macroeconomic collapses. Using a panel of developed and emerging economies from 1950 to 2023, we show that the interest-expense-to-revenue ratio strongly predicts GDP and consumption disasters, as well as hyperinflation, while debt-to-GDP has little predictive power once financing costs are accounted for. The relationship is highly nonlinear, especially in emerging economies. We develop a quantitative open-economy model with rollover risk that matches these patterns to study the impact of anticipated transitions toward higher government spending in advanced economies. The model highlights how financing conditions, monetary policy, and fiscal adjustment jointly shape macroeconomic fragility.

title: Fiscal Sustainability in the Philippines: A Literature Review on Elevated Post-Pandemic National Government Debt, Fiscal Deficits, and Durable Revenue Capacity

detail.title: Fiscal Sustainability in the Philippines: A Literature Review on Elevated Post-Pandemic National Government Debt, Fiscal Deficits, and Durable Revenue Capacity

The research relies exclusively on publicly available government, legislative, and institutional reports.

detail.abstract: This literature review examines the extent to which Philippine fiscal sustainability is threatened by elevated post-pandemic National Government debt, persistent fiscal deficits, and limited durable revenue capacity. Using 2021 as the baseline for pandemic-era fiscal expansion, the review analyzes Philippine government fiscal reports, CPBRD budget analysis, the IMF 2025 Article IV Consultation, and AMRO's 2025 Annual Consultation Report. The review finds that the Philippines does not currently face an immediate fiscal crisis, as National Government debt remains serviceable and supported by a relatively prudent debt profile, including domestic borrowing, fixed-rate instruments, and medium-to long-term maturities. However, fiscal sustainability remains conditional and vulnerable to medium-term risks. Elevated debt constrains fiscal space, persistent deficits prolong borrowing requirements, and limited durable revenue capacity weakens the government's ability to consolidate without compressing productive expenditure. The review argues that revenue capacity is the most structural vulnerability, while growth underperformance is the key stress trigger. Overall, Philippine fiscal sustainability is threatened to a moderate but manageable extent, depending on whether the government can sustain growth, implement credible revenue reforms, control debt-service pressures, and convert post-pandemic recovery into a durable fiscal path.

title: The Duty to Explain: Fiduciary Intelligibility Under ERISA

detail.title: The Duty to Explain: Fiduciary Intelligibility Under ERISA

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: This Essay examines whether the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (“ERISA”) contains an emerging principle of fiduciary intelligibility within its participant disclosure framework. ERISA requires Summary Plan Descriptions (“SPDs”) to be written in a manner “calculated to be understood by the average plan participant.” While modern pension disclosure has become increasingly sophisticated and financially technical, this Essay argues that administrative and financial disclosure are not necessarily equivalent to fiduciary intelligibility. The Essay does not propose a formally recognized standalone fiduciary duty to disclose internal deliberations. Rather, it identifies a participant-facing practice of fiduciary justification potentially latent within ERISA’s disclosure architecture itself. In a post-Loper Bright environment emphasizing statutory interpretation over accumulated administrative convention, the Essay argues that ERISA’s SPD framework may reveal a continuing commitment to participant-facing fiduciary stewardship rather than technical disclosure alone.

title: Beyond LSTMS: A Comparative Analysis of Transformers, CNN-LSTMS, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNS) and Reinforcement Learning in Financial Time-Series Forecasting
affiliations: and Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur

detail.title: Beyond LSTMS: A Comparative Analysis of Transformers, CNN-LSTMS, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNS) and Reinforcement Learning in Financial Time-Series Forecasting
detail.abstract: Financial time-series forecasting remains one of the most challenging domains in quantitative finance due to the inherent stochasticity and non-stationary nature of market data. In this study, utilizing the finlearner library, we present a comprehensive comparative analysis of modern Deep Learning architectures, specifically benchmarking Transformers, CNN-LSTMs, and conventional Recurrent Neural Networks (LSTMs, GRUs) against a Buy-and-Hold benchmark. Additionally, we evaluate a Reinforcement Learning (RL) approach using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to explore active decision-making capabilities. We introduce a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) approach as a novel mechanism to extract the underlying drift parameter (µ) from noisy price trajectories, modeled via Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM). Our empirical results on a tech-heavy portfolio (2020-2025) demonstrate that Transformers utilizing rich feature sets achieve a superior cumulative return of +66.68%, significantly outperforming the market benchmark (+52.42%) by approximately 14%. Furthermore, we show that while deep learning models optimize for predictive accuracy, PINNs offer a crucial layer of explainability by recovering interpretable physical parameters governing the stochastic process. We also find that while PPO shows promise, it requires careful feature engineering to overcome convergence issues in sparse data environments.

title: Buchanan v. Samuels: The Cedar Rust Case Redux
affiliations: University of Central Florida

detail.title: Buchanan v. Samuels: The Cedar Rust Case Redux
detail.abstract: One of the most fascinating sessions at the 2025 meeting of the History of Economics Society (HES) was a roundtable on “The 50th anniversary of the Buchanan-Samuels Exchange.” As it happens, this intellectual exchange was motivated by an old takings case—Miller v. Schoene, decided in 1928—and takings law is one of my areas of expertise. The remainder of my paper reframes the Buchanan-Samuels exchange as a three-act drama and is thus organized as follows: Act I sets the stage of our story by revisiting the dispute in Miller v. Schoene. Next, Act II compares and contrasts Samuels’s framing of this case with Buchanan’s alternate framing. For Samuels, in brief, Miller v. Schoene is a textbook case of reciprocal harms, while for Buchanan, this case is about the sanctity of property rights. Lastly, Act III concludes with the climax and Buchanan’s denouement.

title: From Bitter Lemons to Lemonade: The Fiscal Promise of Digital Service Taxes in Sub-Saharan Africa
affiliations: , Makerere University - College of Business and Management Sciences and Makerere University - College of Business and Management Sciences

detail.title: From Bitter Lemons to Lemonade: The Fiscal Promise of Digital Service Taxes in Sub-Saharan Africa

declarations.ethicsApproval: The Research did not use any data on human or animal subjects.

publicationDetails.detailsText: This Manuscript has been accepted conditionally by the European Journal of Public Finance

detail.abstract: This paper assesses the performance of digital service taxes and related fiscal measures in sub-Saharan Africa. Using an unbalanced panel of 47 countries over 2017-2022 and a differencein-difference-indifferences (DDD) framework, it estimates the effect of digital tax adoption on goods-and-services tax revenue relative to payroll taxes-a fiscally unrelated comparison tax head. The results show that digital tax adoption is estimated to increase consumption-based tax revenue by about 1.8 percentage points of GDP. However, gains are uneven-depending on governance quality, digital readiness, and policy design. The study highlights implementation challenges and draws policy lessons for sustainable digital taxation.

title: The Mortality Input Problem: Trajectory-Dependent Death and the Lifecycle Model

detail.title: The Mortality Input Problem: Trajectory-Dependent Death and the Lifecycle Model
detail.abstract: Heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics has reformed the income and wealth sides of the household problem. The HANK program established that aggregate dynamics require the cross-sectional distribution of marginal propensities to consume, balance-sheet exposures, and permanent income. Every model in this program inherits, without examination, a smooth actuarial mortality hazard calibrated to population life tables. This is the last unreformed input, and it is structurally wrong. The expected residual life of an agent is a value function defined on a manifold whose boundary is death. That function has a geometric property rarely stated in the economic literature: its curvature diverges at a specific powerlaw rate as the agent approaches the boundary. Every lifecycle model that represents mortality as a smooth hazard imposes a bounded-curvature approximation on a function whose curvature is unbounded. No function in the smooth hazard class can encode the shock structure of catastrophic diagnoses that dominate individual mortality trajectories near the boundary, regardless of how many parameters the hazard contains. We establish three structural consequences. First, the population-level response to symmetric interventions is asymmetric: the worsening direction systematically exceeds the improving direction by a factor governed by a single cross-sectional moment, the covariance between boundary curvature and intervention exposure. Second, this covariance is not a small correction in clinical settings: unlike the borrowing-constraint analog in macroeconomics, where the boundary binds for a minority of agents, the mortality boundary is universal, and the population-level curvature integral diverges in a way the macroeconomic scaling intuition cannot accommodate. Third, the representation class that correctly encodes the boundary geometry exists: trained networks with piecewise-linear activation produce value functions that are exactly tropical polynomials in the max-plus semiring, with the density of the piecewise structure near the boundary encoding the curvature divergence that smooth functions cannot. A constellation of puzzles that the lifecycle literature has documented and not resolved, covering wealth decumulation, bequest dispersion, annuitization, retirement timing, portfolio composition, health expenditure at end of life, long-term care insurance, Social Security claiming, and pension tax choices. These are projections of a single geometric fact. Correcting the mortality input generates each of them as equilibrium properties of the model rather than as calibrated parameters or behavioral anomalies.

title:
Axiomatic Coherence of Fixed-Point Target Identification 
A Constitutional Mathematics Framework for Deterministic Antibiotic Discovery

detail.title:
Axiomatic Coherence of Fixed-Point Target Identification 
A Constitutional Mathematics Framework for Deterministic Antibiotic Discovery
