title: From Policy to Practice: Closing the Gap in AI Public Procurement
affiliations: Free University of Bolzano-Bozen

detail.title: From Policy to Practice: Closing the Gap in AI Public Procurement
detail.abstract: Most AI systems used for algorithmic governance are acquired through procurement contracts with private technology vendors at the local, state, and federal levels. Scholars and policymakers widely contend that public procurement offers a powerful regulatory lever for shaping the use of AI in government. Yet a relevant question remains largely overlooked: do procurement contracts actually deliver on this promise? This Article explores this question through a systematic review of publicly available state-level procurement contracts governing the acquisition of AI systems. It examines contractual provisions across a set of critical dimensions, including data access and confidentiality, ownership and intellectual property rights, stakeholder engagement, assessment and testing procedures, and data security and cybersecurity. The analysis reveals a persistent gap between policy aspirations and procurement practice. Contracts governing AI acquisition are frequently inadequate to accomplish their intended regulatory purposes, as they fail to address the unique risks associated with algorithmic governance. As a result, public procurement remains a blunt regulatory instrument. Building on these findings, the Article identifies structural factors that weaken the ability of state agencies to leverage public procurement as an effective regulatory tool, including limited bargaining power, significant information asymmetries, and an overreliance on generic contractual templates. Drawing also on emerging comparative experiences, the analysis advances a set of normative proposals aimed at recalibrating procurement practices through targeted legislative intervention, centralized and collective purchasing strategies, and the development of standardized AI contractual models.

title: Microeconomic Industry Analysis: Oman's Automotive & Transportation Sector
affiliations: and Sultan Qaboos University

detail.title: Microeconomic Industry Analysis: Oman's Automotive & Transportation Sector

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known personal or financial relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract:
The report employs microeconomics to analyse the automotive and transportation industry in Oman. It is divided into four sub-markets that are structurally different . The four sub-markets include Mwasalat public bus transit, new car imports, used vehicles and the growing electric vehicle (EV) market. After a 67% demand drop from 2014 to 2023 due to oil-price shocks, the industry bounced back to $3.23 billion in 2025.

HHI and CR3 concentration ratios are utilized to identify four market configurations – natural monopoly (Mwasalat), oligopoly (new vehicle imports, HHI lower bound of ≈ 2,439, with Toyota accounting for 47.2%), competitive market (used cars), and growing oligopoly (EVs). Compared to similar GCC and international studies, estimates of price elasticity of demand (PED) show that bus fares are elastic (PED ≈ −1.3), brand-level switching is highly elastic (PED ≈ −2.0), and EV adoption is elastic (PED ≈ −1.8), versus inelastic demand for car ownership at the category level (PED ≈ −0.6).

Three market failures are identified: underadoption of EVs due to a positive externality, underproduction by Mwasalat due to a natural monopoly and principal-agent mismatch, and the negative externality of ICE car emissions. The welfare analysis in partial equilibrium with explicit consumer surplus, producer surplus and deadweight loss diagrams supports three policy recommendations: a tiered EV rebate programme (OMR 1,000-2,500) combined with a PPP charging network mandate; performance-based Mwasalat funding linked to passenger-kilometre KPIs; and emissions-differentiated import tariffs phased in over a three-year period.

The findings show that Oman’s Vision 2040 goals, including 15% EV penetration by 2030, can only be met with simultaneous infrastructure investment and fiscally integrated incentive systems. Five methodological constraints are expressly recognized, including the qualitative character of the PED estimations and the partial equilibrium scope, which restrict accuracy but do not impair the directional validity of the suggestions.

title: CoJDA-Net:A Contrastive Joint Domain Adaptation Network for Reliable Fault Diagnosis of High-Speed Train Bogies Under Variable Operating Conditions
affiliations: Sichuan University, Sichuan University, Southwest Jiaotong University and Sichuan University

detail.title: CoJDA-Net:A Contrastive Joint Domain Adaptation Network for Reliable Fault Diagnosis of High-Speed Train Bogies Under Variable Operating Conditions
detail.abstract: The reliability of bogie transmission systems is paramount for the safe operation of high-speed trains. However, developing robust data-driven fault diagnosis models remains challenging due to distribution shifts caused by variable operating conditions and the scarcity of labeled data. Although existing deep domain adaptation methods effectively align global distributions, they often neglect the discriminability of features within specific classes, leading to fuzzy decision boundaries and intra-class confusion during transfer tasks. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel transfer learning framework termed the Contrastive Joint Domain Adaptation Network (CoJDA-Net). This method synergizes a Convolutional Neural Network backbone with a dual-alignment strategy to ensure both domain invariance and class discriminability. Specifically, Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy is employed to align the joint distributions of deep features and classifier predictions across domains. Complementing this, a pseudo-label-guided Supervised Contrastive Learning module is introduced to explicitly minimize intra-class variance and maximize inter-class separability in the target domain, thereby resolving the confusion near decision boundaries. Extensive experiments conducted on the laboratory-scale BJTU-RAO bogie dataset demonstrate that CoJDA-Net achieves superior diagnostic performance, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The framework exhibits robust generalization capabilities in challenging cross-speed and cross-load scenarios, providing a promising solution for the intelligent condition monitoring of railway transportation systems.

title: Phased deployment of PV generation plants using compound real options
affiliations: National University of San Juan - Faculty of Engineering, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Phased deployment of PV generation plants using compound real options
detail.abstract: Phased deployment of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) projects offers flexibility, improved risk management, and opportunities to benefit from learning effects, cost reductions and emerging technologies. However, splitting capacity also incurs in higher unit costs due to foregone economies of scale. This paper evaluates the economic implications of phased investment strategies in PV projects, using a compound real options framework to quantify the trade-off between flexibility gains and the cost penalties of modular construction. A nested least-squares Monte Carlo (LSM) algorithm is used to jointly value a portfolio of sequential expansion options under jump-diffusion investment costs and a multi-factor electricity price model. Results show that, for empirically realistic economies-of-scale coefficients, lump-sum deployment dominates phasing, with staging only becoming preferable when fragmentation raises unit costs by marginal amounts. Optimal staging is highly non-linear in cost overruns and in the long-term electricity price level. Declining technology costs can nevertheless make phased designs more attractive when current conditions favor deferral, by allowing developers to postpone later modules to a lower-cost epoch. The framework is positioned as an integrative methodological extension of prior compound-option valuations of PV plants, with explicit log-scale CAPEX functions, stop-and-go penalties, and long-term electricity price uncertainty. The insights are most directly applicable to utility-scale market-driven, PV deployments under forward-contract remuneration.

title: Multi-domain data integration for a predictive geometallurgy framework applied to MgO control in phosphate beneficiation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidade de São Paulo

detail.title: Multi-domain data integration for a predictive geometallurgy framework applied to MgO control in phosphate beneficiation
detail.abstract: The control of magnesium oxide (MgO) content in apatite concentrates is a critical challenge in phosphate processing plants hosted in carbonatite deposits, as elevated MgO levels degrade concentrate quality and impair downstream fertilizer production. This study presents a data-driven geometallurgical framework to forecast MgO content in the final concentrate by integrating geological, chemical, metallurgical, and operational variables through machine learning. A comprehensive dataset from 258 phosphate ore stockpiles was compiled, encompassing lithological proportions, head-sample chemistry, grinding parameters, and plant performance data. Among five regression algorithms evaluated, Support Vector Regression (SVR) demonstrated the most robust performance under Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV), achieving a satisfactory R2 of 0.69 and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of approximately 13%. Model stability and uncertainty were rigorously assessed using bootstrap confidence intervals and k-fold validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the underlying logic of the model, identifying plant feed MgO, micaceous lithologies, and Al-/Fe-bearing phases as the primary controls on MgO deportment. To bridge the gap between complex modeling and industrial routine, a simplified linear surrogate equation was derived and validated against an independent external dataset. The proposed framework provides a transparent, operationally relevant tool for stockpile management and blending strategies, enabling proactive quality control in phosphate beneficiation.

title: G-Diag: Graph-Based Bottleneck Diagnosis for Pipeline-Parallel LLM Training
affiliations: Zhejiang Lab, Zhejiang Lab and Zhejiang Lab

detail.title: G-Diag: Graph-Based Bottleneck Diagnosis for Pipeline-Parallel LLM Training
detail.abstract: Pipeline Parallelism (PP) is essential for hyperscale Large Language Model (LLM) training, yet existing profilers, planners, and simulators either overlook PP-specific dependencies in measured executions or fail to quantify which bottlenecks are actionable and how much workload can be safely rebalanced before bottleneck migration. We propose G-Diag, a trace-driven framework for PP-aware structural bottleneck diagnosis. G-Diag reconstructs profiler traces into a Pipelined Execution Graph (PEG) and introduces Optimization Dominance, a provable metric that separates actionable bottlenecks from critical but non-dominant microsteps. Building on this formalism, G-Diag parameterizes movable workload through trace-derived computation time, respects forward--backward coupling and workload-conservation constraints, and computes feasible rebalancing directions with a Dominance-guided optimization algorithm. We evaluate G-Diag on two production clusters and models up to 236B parameters, and validate its trace-derived workload parameterization against measured PP scaling. G-Diag uncovers up to 12.26% projected optimization headroom, reveals persistent group-specific bottlenecks at scale, and supports a production MoE-32B reconfiguration whose realized makespan matches the projection within 7.80%.  Additional simulation shows that the same PEG-based formulation extends from canonical 1F1B to virtual-stage schedules, providing a theoretically grounded and practical approach for diagnosing structural inefficiencies in hyperscale PP training.

title: Bi-level optimization strategy for market trading in virtual power plant with shared energy storage and gas-electric coupling
affiliations: Xiangtan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Xiangtan University, Xiangtan University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Bi-level optimization strategy for market trading in virtual power plant with shared energy storage and gas-electric coupling
detail.abstract: A high proportion of renewable energy integration into the grid can cause dynamic frequency deviations. Integrating widely distributed, low-capacity idle energy storage from information infrastructure can effectively alleviate grid frequency regulation pressure, and power-to-gas technology can assist energy storage in gas-electricity coupling. Based on this, a two-layer optimization strategy for virtual power plant participation in the electricity-frequency regulation market transactions with shared energy storage and gas-electricity coupling is proposed. The dispatchable capacity of shared energy storage in 5G base stations and internet data centers is analyzed. Subsequently, a two-layer optimization model for virtual power plant participation in the electricity-frequency regulation market is constructed. The upper-layer model sets the power-exchange price based on electricity demand and frequency regulation services, thereby guiding the shared energy storage to align its power-exchange demand with the grid's peak-shaving and frequency regulation needs. The lower-layer model develops a bidding strategy to minimize the market participation cost of the virtual power plant. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly increases the virtual power plant's market revenue and substantially eases the grid's peak-shaving and frequency-regulation pressure.

title: Female Leadership and Disclosure Clarity in an Era of Gender Policy Reforms
affiliations: Liverpool Business School, Liverpool John Moores University

detail.title: Female Leadership and Disclosure Clarity in an Era of Gender Policy Reforms
detail.abstract: This study examines whether top leadership gender influences the clarity of corporate narrative disclosures. Drawing on Voice Effect Theory and the United Kingdom’s evolving gender-governance regime, it distinguishes between women in executive roles with substantive reporting authority and women serving as board chairs in oversight positions. Using FTSE 100 firm data from 2011 to 2021, we estimate ordinary least squares regressions with firm and year fixed effects and examine whether the Davies Review, the Hampton–Alexander Review, and the transition to the FTSE Women Leaders agenda altered the association between female leadership and disclosure clarity. The results show that firms led by female chief executives produce significantly more readable annual reports than firms led by male chief executives, whereas firms with a female board chair show no comparable reduction in narrative complexity. Additional policy tests indicate that the female-CEO readability effect persists across successive reform periods but is not significantly amplified after 2016 or during the post-2020 transition. Overall, the findings suggest that substantive executive authority, rather than symbolic oversight, is the leadership channel most consistently associated with clearer corporate disclosure. The policy implication is that gender-diversity reforms improve transparency when they support women’s advancement into executive leadership more effectively.

title: Climate-driven variability and management-stabilized yield in winter rapeseed systems of the Yangtze River Basin
affiliations: Huazhong Agricultural University, Huazhong Agricultural University, Shanghai Customs College, Auburn University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), Huazhong Agricultural University, Huazhong Agricultural University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Climate-driven variability and management-stabilized yield in winter rapeseed systems of the Yangtze River Basin
detail.abstract: CONTEXTClimate change is reshaping crop production systems by increasing environmental stress and altering yield stability. Winter rapeseed is an important oilseed crop in the Yangtze River Basin (YRB), where production is increasingly exposed to heat and drought stress under changing climatic conditions. Understanding how environmental factors and management practices jointly regulate crop productivity and resilience is essential for sustainable intensification.OBJECTIVEThis study aimed to quantify the relative contributions of environmental conditions, climatic stressors, and management practices to winter rapeseed yield formation and yield stability in the YRB under current and future climate scenarios.METHODSThe process-based crop model CROPGRO-Canola was calibrated and evaluated using multi-year and multi-site field experimental data and subsequently applied for regional-scale simulations across the YRB. Sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess the effects of temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation changes on crop yield. In addition, future climate scenarios for 2081–2100 under different emission pathways were used to evaluate changes in yield variability and regional vulnerability.RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONSpatial variation in winter rapeseed yield across the YRB was primarily associated with environmental gradients, whereas yield stability was strongly regulated by interactions between climatic stress and management practices. Heat and drought stress emerged as the dominant drivers of yield instability. Sensitivity analysis showed that temperature increases exerted the strongest negative effects on yield, followed by reductions in precipitation and changes in solar radiation. Under current climatic conditions, optimized management practices increased yield by up to 17.6%, indicating substantial opportunities for adaptive management. Future climate projections suggested increasing yield variability and yield reductions of up to 12% under high-emission scenarios, with highly productive regions exhibiting greater vulnerability to climate stress. These findings reveal a trade-off between productivity and resilience in winter rapeseed systems under climate change.SIGNIFICANCEThis study provides a system-level assessment of how environmental and management factors interact to shape crop productivity and stability in winter rapeseed systems. The findings contribute to the development of climate adaptation strategies and management optimization for sustainable rapeseed production in the Yangtze River Basin and other climate-sensitive agricultural regions.

title: Unlocking Legal Efficiency Gains in School Switch Programs
affiliations: Lund University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Unlocking Legal Efficiency Gains in School Switch Programs
detail.abstract: We study school switches in which students who have already been assigned seats request reassignment. Unlike in regular school choice, stability need not be legally binding in such programs, since students’ priority-based claims have already been satisfied upstream. Efficiency then naturally becomes the primary design objective. To quantify the potential legal efficiency gains, we compare Deferred Acceptance (DA) with Top Trading Cycles (TTC) and an efficiency-adjusted DA (EADAM) using Swedish data. TTC and EADAM triple switching rates compared to DA. This difference is driven by the absence of slack in effective capacity and shrinks rapidly when introducing additional seats.

title: Dynamic Evolution of Corporate Emissions Determinants
affiliations: King's College, London, University of Zurich - Department Finance, King’s College London and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Dynamic Evolution of Corporate Emissions Determinants
detail.abstract: This paper examines how firm-level determinants of industrial emissions evolve over time as firms adapt to environmental regulation, economic conditions, and organisational constraints. Using a panel of 204 U.S. industrial facilities observed from 1992 to 2023, we link facility-level emissions from the Toxics Release Inventory to firm financial characteristics, managerial attributes, local labour market conditions, and aggregate macroeconomic indicators. We employ a time-varying mean-group estimator that allows average relationships to change smoothly over time while accommodating persistent heterogeneity across facilities. We find several covariates display episodic associations with emissions growth. The results reveal pronounced stage-like dynamics in emissions determinants, with firm-level characteristics and aggregate conditions dominating in different periods. From an innovation-policy perspective, the findings highlight that firms’ responses to environmental regulationare time-dependent and shaped by their adaptive capacity.

title: Quantifying Predictive Precision: A Macroeconomic Threshold Analysis of Annual Equity-Bond Spreads for Recession Prediction

detail.title: Quantifying Predictive Precision: A Macroeconomic Threshold Analysis of Annual Equity-Bond Spreads for Recession Prediction
detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between the annual return spread defined as the realized annual total return on the S&P 500 minus the realized annual total return on the 10-year U.S. Treasury bond and subsequent U.S economic recessions over the period 1928-2026. Using an annual return dataset, we identify a novel empirical regularity regarding the non-linear predictive power of equity-bond return differentials. We found that the depth at which the return spread turns negative, rather than the mere sign change, is the dominant predictor of financial distress. A return spread below (-)15 percentage points precedes a recession within two years in 81% of historical cases, with the predictive accuracy rising to 100% for spreads below (-)25 percentage points. By contrast, a bare sign reversal (any negative spread) produces only a 52% precision rate, suggesting that binary "inversions" in realized returns are insufficient signals without accounting for magnitude. These findings are distinct from the traditional yield-curve inversion literature, which operates on yield differentials rather than realized investor outcomes and suggest that annual return spread dynamics contain complementary information about recession risk.

title: Reducing energy consumption and processing time by smart robot-workpiece position planning in robotic manufacturing processes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, TU Wien, Institute of Production Engineering and Photonic Technologies and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Reducing energy consumption and processing time by smart robot-workpiece position planning in robotic manufacturing processes
detail.abstract: This paper presents a novel method for pre-processing optimization of robot–workpiece configuration in manufacturing processes based on a continuous end-effector toolpath with a defined feed-rate. Industrial robots are widely used in applications involving low cutting forces (such as additive manufacturing, grinding, polishing, abrasive waterjet and laser cutting, welding, and large-format 3D printing) especially to produce complex-shaped parts. As the adoption of such processes increases, so does their contribution to energy consumption in manufacturing. Unlike conventional methods based on inverse dynamics or data-driven models, the proposed approach leverages the robot’s kinetic energy profile and its integral along the toolpath as an optimization criterion. This simplification significantly reduces computational effort while maintaining sufficient accuracy to distinguish between different configurations. A genetic algorithm (type of evolutionary algorithm) is used to minimize kinetic energy and, consequently, power consumption. A key innovation of the method lies in its ability to determine the optimal mutual position of the robot and the workpiece for the entire process motion of the end-effector, in contrast to existing approaches that typically address auxiliary movements. Experimental validation performed with two industrial robots and two different manufacturing processes using a rotary-tilting table showed energy savings of up to 9.6%. These results confirm the method’s effectiveness and its potential for wide industrial application.

reference: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20201211
title: The Personafication System™ Why in ABM The Unit of Analysis is Always the Person, Not the Account
affiliations: Fondazione ITS Meccatronica e Avionica

detail.title: The Personafication System™ Why in ABM The Unit of Analysis is Always the Person, Not the Account
detail.abstract:
Account-based marketing (ABM) practice has long operated on a structural misconception: that the account-the legal and financial entity-is the appropriate unit of analysis for complex B2B commercial programs. 
This paper argues that this assumption is empirically and neurologically incorrect, and introduces the Personafication System™ as a methodological correction. Drawing on published research from Gartner, Forrester, Edelman-LinkedIn, Bain & Company, McKinsey, and neuroscience literature on embodied cognition, mirror neuron activation, and oxytocin-mediated trust (Damásio, 1994; Rizzolatti & Craighero, 2004; Zak, 2017), the paper demonstrates that B2B purchasing decisions in complex industrial contexts are determined by specific human individuals embedded in relational networks-not by organizational abstractions.
The paper examines the pre-commercial window in which shortlists are assembled before any formal evaluation begins, the structure of modern B2B buying teams (6–22 stakeholders per decision, 74% experiencing internal conflict), the champion problem and shortlist architecture, the phenomenon of the invisible buyer operating through the dark funnel, and the systematic failure of category-level buyer personas to address individual-level decision dynamics.
The Personafication System™, developed by Alberto Regis (IperLeads) as the operational expression of Marketing Lento methodology, inverts conventional ABM logic by moving from the specific target account inward to the real individuals whose trust and comprehension determine commercial outcomes. The system's eight sequential phases constitute a pre-commercial trust architecture whose documented outcomes include deal sizes averaging 200% higher than those generated by conventional commercial processes, with fully executed programs generating qualified pipeline of comparable scale within six months of program initiation.

title: Season-specific national peak load forecasting: A large-scale benchmark of econometric, machine learning, and deep learning forecasting models
affiliations: Changwon National University and Yonsei University

detail.title: Season-specific national peak load forecasting: A large-scale benchmark of econometric, machine learning, and deep learning forecasting models
detail.abstract: Accurate national peak load forecasting is essential for reliable and cost-effective power system operation; however, comparisons across model classes are often distorted by inconsistent covariates, preprocessing, and validation protocols. This study presents a season-specific benchmark for South Korea’s daily national peak load, using fixed calendar and weather covariates, leakage-free train–test splits, algorithm-level reporting, and peak-aware evaluation. A total of 58 winter and 61 summer candidate configurations including traditional econometric methods, tabular machine learning models, sequence-aware deep learning models, structured regression, and simple mean ensembles were assessed. Results showed a strong seasonal dependence. In winter, the best-performing single algorithm was Time-Series Dense Encoder (TiDE), achieving a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 2,052 MW; this was an improvement of 39.3% over the strongest traditional baseline, Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Regressors and Fourier Terms (SARIMAX-Fourier), which recorded an RMSE of 3,379 MW. In summer, multivariate regression emerges as the suitable single model (RMSE: 2,402 MW), while a top-5 mean ensemble yields the best overall accuracy (RMSE: 2,037 MW). However, average accuracy did not ensure peak-day fidelity. In the summer test window, the lowest-RMSE algorithm missed the actual peak date by 28 days and yielded a 5.18% absolute percentage error (APE) on that day. In contrast, SARIMAX-Fourier correctly identified the peak date and achieved a substantially lower APE of 0.61%. These findings highlight that model selection should be both season-specific and objective-driven, balancing overall accuracy with peak-day magnitude and timing.

title: Creative Destruction or Structural Scarring? An Agent-based Model of the AI Transition

detail.title: Creative Destruction or Structural Scarring? An Agent-based Model of the AI Transition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial relationships with any individuals or organisations that could be perceived to have influenced this study. The model was developed independently using open-source software (NetLogo). The author’s institutional affiliations — Adjunct Associate Professor at the University of Technology Sydney and Honorary Research Associate at Judge Business School, University of Cambridge — are disclosed for transparency; neither institution provided funding for or exercised influence over this research.

All analysis is based on a computational agent-based simulation calibrated to publicly available aggregate employment statistics (UK Office for National Statistics). No ethics approval or participant consent was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was conducted independently and entirely at the author’s own expense, with no financial support from any public, private, or charitable organisation.

detail.abstract: Transformative AI (TAI) could be one of the most consequential economic revolutions in history. Previous automation displaced routine labour while complementing cognitive work, generating the skill premium that made retraining worthwhile. When AI reaches parity with cognitive labour, that complementarity breaks down, and with it the scarcity rent that has sustained skilled wages. Dominant economic theory suggests that when job displacement equals reinstatement, the long-term effects on the economy reequilibrate. This abstraction ignores the implications of the transition path itself. We build a heterogeneous-agent-based model of an advanced economy that tracks 10,000 heterogeneous workers across four labour market states-employed, frictionally unemployed, in training, and structurally unemployed. Workers interact with firms through a Cobb-Douglas matching function, a micro-level wage Phillips curve, and a net present value retraining calculus. We simulate eight plausible AI adoption pathways over a twenty-year horizon. The headline result is that retraining friction alone-even when AI creates as many jobs as it destroys-produces structural unemployment, much like a scenario in which displaced jobs are never replaced. Three further findings emphasise the importance of considering the transition path when determining long-term economic outcomes. First, pre-emptive reinstatement, in which new tasks appear before displacement, prevents the simultaneous spike in unemployment and unfilled vacancies that would otherwise destabilise the labour market. Second, the speed of adoption shapes the path of unemployment but converges to a similar long-run level of structural unemployment. Third, a fifty per cent retraining subsidy eliminates structural unemployment when the binding constraint is mismatch, but is ineffective when jobs are genuinely scarce. The policy instrument must match the diagnosis. The relevant question for governments preparing for AI is not how many jobs will be created or destroyed, but how fast institutions can absorb displaced workers before structural unemployment becomes permanent.

title: Dynamic Identity
affiliations: University of Southern California, Marshall School of Business

detail.title: Dynamic Identity
detail.abstract: Consumers form impressions of marketplace actors not from a single message, but from sequences of signals encountered over time. How does the variation across this history shape what consumers come to believe? A multimethod investigation, combining text embeddings on nearly 20,000 sponsored posts from 940 influencers with preregistered controlled experiments, reveals an inverted U-shaped relationship between identity breadth and consumer response: moderate breadth outperforms both narrow and highly diffuse identities. Taking a dynamic view, new content performs best when it deviates moderately from prior posts, with shifts into related product categories outperforming both repetition and moves across distant categories. Moderate variation works because it balances coherence with new information, thereby sustaining interest while preserving perceived authenticity. Further, the effects depend on influencer lifecycle and post goals. Together, these findings reconceptualize identity as a dynamic, cumulative inference and demonstrate how automated text analysis can be used to study identity dynamics.

title: Customer and Market Research
affiliations: PES University

detail.title: Customer and Market Research
detail.abstract:
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) communication has emerged as a critical determinant of consumer brand relationships in contemporary markets. Despite growing organisational investment in CSR messaging, empirical evidence quantifying the direct effect of CSR communication quality on brand loyalty remains limited. This study addresses that gap by examining the influence of CSR communication quality on consumer brand loyalty through simple linear regression analysis.
A quantitative, descriptive, and explanatory research design was adopted. Primary data were collected from 164 valid respondents using a structured questionnaire administered via Google Forms. The questionnaire comprised Likert-scale items measuring CSR communication quality as the independent variable and brand loyalty as the dependent variable across seven and eight items respectively. Cronbach's alpha confirmed good internal consistency reliability for both constructs, recording 0.824 for CSR communication quality and 0.831 for brand loyalty.
Descriptive statistics revealed mean scores of 3.434 (SD = 0.560) for CSR communication quality and 3.498 (SD = 0.562) for brand loyalty, indicating moderately positive perceptions across both constructs. Pearson correlation analysis confirmed a moderate positive linear relationship between the variables (r = 0.677, p < 0.001). The regression model was statistically significant (F(1, 162) = 137.288, p < 0.001), with CSR communication quality explaining 45.9% of the variance in brand loyalty (R² = 0.459). The regression coefficient was positive and significant (B = 0.680, t = 11.717, p < 0.001), confirming that H₁ is supported.
The findings demonstrate that transparent, consistent, and authentic CSR communication significantly enhances consumer brand loyalty, providing actionable empirical evidence for brand managers and marketing practitioners seeking to leverage CSR communication as a strategic loyalty driver.

title: AI Presence Drift: A Longitudinal Re-Baseline of Five Brand Categories

detail.abstract:
This paper reports a longitudinal re-baseline of the five categories first measured in the v0.6 cross-category baseline of the AIAS measurement program — project management software, premium running shoes, premium olive oil, premium facial skincare, and personal finance applications — at a second time point approximately seven days later. The study closes Phase 2 of the AIAS program by giving each baseline category a t₂ measurement and provides the data spine for Phase 3 construct-validity work. Six hypotheses with explicit numerical thresholds were committed to a pre-registration document locked at git commit f8cebbd (tag v0.9-prereg-locked) prior to any t₂ data collection. Methodology decisions — the matched 2-model subset (claude-sonnet-4-6 and gpt-5.4-mini, the original v0.6 lineup) for longitudinal deltas, retroactive mode classification of v0.6 data, and registry freeze at v0.6's final state — were locked at git commit e6428a4 prior to the pre-registration.

The headline result is decisive. Five formal hypotheses were confirmed and the sixth landed at the predicted stability band. Per-brand drift across all 5 categories on the matched subset (n = 103 brand-level deltas) was small: 88.3 percent of brands within ±5 percentage points and 99.0 percent within ±10 percentage points (H1 confirmed). Top-three brands at t₁ remained in the top-five at t₂ in every category (H2 confirmed, 5 of 5). Within-category brand-presence variance ordering across the five categories at t₂ correlated with t₁ at Spearman ρ = 0.8 (H3 confirmed). The Mint phantom-brand stayed at 41.7 percent matched-subset gross Presence at t₂ versus 44.8 percent at t₁ — a −3.1 percentage-point delta within the predicted stability band (H4 stability, the predicted outcome). Pattern 4 discourse-language bias replicated under the strict reading: Spanish olive oil aggregate Presence at 11.5 percentage points fell below the 12.5-percentage-point threshold derived from the International Olive Council production share, and K-beauty aggregate Presence in skincare at 1.0 percentage point fell well below the 5-percentage-point threshold (H5 confirmed strict; partially confirmed under an inclusive reading that adds Graza, a US-headquartered Spanish-sourced brand). Per-brand cross-model spread between the two matched-subset models correlated between t₁ and t₂ at Pearson r ≥ 0.7 in every category (H6 confirmed, 5 of 5).

A post-hoc test of v0.6's Pattern 1 (cross-model variance and discourse coherence) at the category level — distinct from H3's within-category brand variance test — was performed against the same matched-subset data. Per-category mean cross-model spread between Sonnet and gpt-5.4-mini ranks at Spearman ρ = 0.800 between t₁ and t₂, and at ρ = 0.900 between t₂ and v0.6's qualitative ordering (personal finance > olive oil > project management > skincare > running). Pattern 1 as v0.6 stated it replicates at v0.9 with the t₂ ranking better-matched to v0.6's narrative than t₁ is.

A meta-finding emerged from the H5 work: the v0.6 skincare registry contains a single K-beauty brand among thirty-one entries, mirroring inside the registry construction the same Anglo-discourse bias the test is designed to detect. The H5 strict-versus-inclusive sensitivity confirms what v0.6 §4.4 already articulated — that discourse-language bias operates at the brand-marketing-language tier rather than country-of-origin — by isolating the diagnostic case of Graza, a Spanish-sourced English-marketed brand whose inclusion in the Spanish cohort breaches the H5 threshold while its exclusion confirms it.

The combined result set is interpreted as a longitudinal validity argument for the AIAS measurement program. AI Presence behaves like a real underlying construct — drift is small, leaderboards are stable, structural variance patterns replicate (both within-category brand variance and cross-model spread by discourse coherence), the phantom-brand persistence mechanism holds across waves at gross Presence, and cross-model relative behavior is preserved. The argument unblocks Phase 3 construct-validity work, which requires at least three categories at two time points and now has data for five.

title: Can Washington State Change Pharmaceutical Advertising Forever?

detail.abstract: Pharmaceutical advertisers spend roughly $18 billion annually in the United States to deliver targeted drug pitches-an effort that depends on collecting and processing consumer health data through advertising IDs, IP addresses, and similar persistent identifiers. Washington State's recently enacted My Health My Data Act (MHMD) defines "collection" and "processing" of consumer health data in unusually expansive terms and reaches data that can be "reasonably" linked back to an identifiable consumer. Because Washington hosts several of the largest cloudservice providers in the country, and because piecemeal compliance is impractical, MHMD is poised to function as a de facto national standard-a "Washington Effect" analogous to the California or Brussels Effects observed in other privacy contexts. This essay maps MHMD's operative provisions against the standard practices of pharmaceutical targeted advertising, identifies the compliance pathways available to advertisers (statutory opt-in consent, de-identification, synthetic or aggregated data), and explains why each is likely to be tested in litigation. It argues that proactive compliance, rather than waiting for the anticipated wave of class actions, offers the best path forward for advertisers, publishers, and consumers alike.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of social media has fundamentally transformed marketing communication, with influencer-driven content increasingly shaping consumer decisions across age groups. This study investigates the factors that determine the impact of social media influencers on consumer purchase behaviour, with a specific focus on the role of perceived trust. Using a structured questionnaire-based survey administered to a mixed-age sample (n=30, predominantly in the 25-32 age group), primary data was collected and subjected to descriptive analysis to identify key behavioural patterns. Findings indicate that Instagram is the dominant platform, with an average usage of 3-5 hours per day, and that consumers primarily use influencers as an information source rather than as a direct purchase trigger. Trust in the influencer-encompassing perceived authenticity, credibility, and relatability-emerges as the most significant determinant of purchase intent. Notably, consumers demonstrate independent decision-making, suggesting influencers play an awareness and consideration role rather than a persuasion role. This study contributes to the growing literature on digital marketing and consumer autonomy, and offers implications for brands designing influencer-led campaigns. Future research with larger samples and inferential statistical methods is recommended to validate these findings.

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is restructuring labor markets in ways that earlier analyses did not anticipate. Adjustment has not fallen uniformly across experience levels; it concentrates on entry-level workers. This critical narrative literature review examines the empirical evidence from 2022 through early 2026 on how generative AI has affected hiring, wages, and the composition of junior positions in four high-exposure sectors: technology, finance, consulting, and administration. Beyond the synthesis itself, the paper makes two original contributions. First, it presents a structured effect-size synthesis of the available estimates, organized by margin of adjustment, that makes explicit a pattern obscured by prose summaries: large negative effects on junior hiring and wages and large positive effects on within-firm productivity describe two distinct operating margins of the same phenomenon, not contradictory results. Second, it proposes a twoby-two framework—institutional flexibility × AI adoption intensity—that locates each study in one of four regimes and derives a predicted pattern of adjustment for each. The framework offers a structured explanation for the divergence between strong U.S. effects (Hosseini & Lichtinger, 2025; Brynjolfsson, Chandar, & Chen, 2025; Azar, Giné, & Sanz-Espín, 2025) and the precise null effects in Denmark (Humlum & Vestergaard, 2025), and identifies Latin American and SubSaharan African labor markets as the most under-documented quadrant. The paper closes by mapping policy implications onto each regime.

detail.abstract:
The AIAS™ Presence Measurement Protocol operationalizes AI Availability — the brand-level probability of retrieval, recommendation, or selection by an AI intermediary — as a measurable construct alongside Ehrenberg-Bass Mental Availability and Physical Availability. Protocol v1.4 (SSRN 6799479) extends AI Availability into a multi-component construct (Recognition × Recall) anchored empirically by the Iwachu dissociation in v0.17 (SSRN 6802261). This paper reports v0.18, which tests two pre-registered hypotheses orthogonally: (a) the three-leg joint Identity-Load moderator hypothesis closing the AMBIGUOUS verdict left by the v0.16/v0.17 panel (v0.16 PARTIAL, v0.17 FALSIFIED on panel inadequacy), and (b) the generalization of the Recognition × Recall dissociation from the cross-cultural Japanese-cell substrate to a same-language IL-gradient substrate. The substrate is indie fragrance, sampled across three cells stratified by Identity Load: mass-prestige (medium IL), designer-niche (medium-high IL), and indie/artisan (high IL). Each cell holds 8 brands (worldwide n = 24 pre-floor; C1 floor n ≥ 12). The reference panel is the locked six-slot v0.17 panel. Phase B uses a three-frame query battery (niche / independent / perfumistas).

All three pre-registered hypotheses returned PARTIAL verdicts. H_Regime4_indie_fragrance resolved at C3, with C1 panel adequacy and both C2 conditions (within-cell concentration and IL-gradient separation) clearing. The three-leg joint H_IdentityLoad_moderator returned PARTIAL, indicating the moderator operates but with substrate-specific qualifications. H_Recognition_Recall_dissociation_generalization returned DISSOCIATION_PARTIAL: 9 Iwachu-pattern cases identified across 2 of 3 cells, concentrated in the highest-IL Cell B (6 of 8 cell brands, 75%). The Recognition × Recall multi-component construct (Protocol v1.4) generalizes to a same-language substrate, strengthening v1.4's foundational construct claim beyond its original cross-cultural empirical anchor. Cell C's pivot cascade exhausted at the "niche fragrance" Recognition probe (mean C_P ≈ 0.25/6 across the 6-slot panel) — documented as DEVIATIONS Entry 1 and treated as a substantive finding that the IL-gradient operates on Recognition itself, not only on Recall. The pre-registration discipline (commit 183386c, tag v0.18-prereg-r1, refined through r4 at commit 1195cb8) locks panel, hypotheses, decision rules, and dissociation thresholds ex-ante.

affiliations: , , WU Vienna, University of Tübingen - Faculty of Economics and Social Sciences and

detail.title: Choosing a Difference-in-Differences Estimand and Estimator for Heavy-Tailed Outcomes: A Practitioner’s Companion

publicationDetails.detailsText: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This guide is a practitioner’s companion to Winkler, Hotz-Behofsits, Wlömert, Papies, and Liaukonytė (2026), “Does TikTok Promote or Cannibalize Music Streaming? Estimands and Identification with Heavy-Tailed Outcomes.” It provides a decision workflow for choosing a difference-in-differences estimand and estimator when outcomes are heavy-tailed or approximately power-law distributed. Such outcomes are common in digital markets, platforms, and media settings, where a small share of products, users, creators, or pieces of content account for most of the economically relevant activity. In these settings, common DiD specifications can answer different economic questions even when applied to the same research design, because they place implicit or explicit weight on different parts of the outcome distribution. The guide distinguishes three common estimands: the typical-unit proportional effect, the population-total proportional effect, and the level effect. It then links each estimand to diagnostic checks and estimator choices, including log OLS, weighted log OLS, levels OLS, and Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (PPML) with a log link. The central message is that the estimand should be dictated by the research question, while the estimator should be chosen based on the estimand, the outcome distribution, and the credibility of the corresponding counterfactual trend restriction. PPML is often useful in these settings because it avoids ad hoc log transformations, accommodates zeros, allows robust inference under heteroskedasticity, and targets a conditional-mean estimand that is often well aligned with aggregate economic questions. The guide can be read independently, but the full methodological argument and empirical application appear in the parent paper.

title: Is an Educated Consumer the Best Customer? The Value of Consumer AI
affiliations: , University of Texas at Dallas, Naveen Jindal School of Management, The University of Texas at Dallas, Jindal School of Management and University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management

detail.title: Is an Educated Consumer the Best Customer? The Value of Consumer AI
detail.abstract: Abstract Consumer AI—AI tools that assist consumers in their purchase decisions—is becoming ubiquitous in online retailing. Unlike traditional product-centric technologies that focus on product-related information, consumer AI centers on consumers by providing expert information about them. In this paper, we develop a game-theoretic model to examine the impact of consumer AI on both manufacturers and consumers. We consider a manufacturer that sells two products to consumers whose utility depends on both the severity of their needs and how well the products satisfy their needs. With AI, consumers are better informed in both dimensions. We find that the value of AI to the manufacturer critically depends on the type of products and the quality of AI. When the products serve a niche market, AI always benefits the manufacturer. In contrast, when the products serve an excessive mass market, AI always hurts the manufacturer. When the products serve a mass market but market penetration is not very high, whether AI hurts the manufacturer depends on AI quality—it hurts the manufacturer if AI's fit precision is low and its valuation precision is moderate. Moreover, although consumer AI is designed to help consumers, we find that it does not always benefit them, as AI adoption leads to higher prices. AI can even hurt both the manufacturer and consumers, resulting in a “lose-lose” outcome. Jointly considering consumer AI and product-centric technologies, we show that AI that improves consumer knowledge about their idiosyncratic needs and product-centric technologies that improve consumer knowledge about product quality can complement each other from the manufacturers' perspective. Therefore, to fully realize the value of consumer AI, manufacturers should improve the quality of product-centric technologies in addition to enhancing AI quality.

detail.abstract: Traditional economics assumes value persists indefinitely, enabling unlimited wealth accumulation. Living systems operate differently because value requires continuous renewal or it ceases to exist. This paper introduces the Autophage Protocol, a system that combines formal incentive design with cryptographic privacy guarantees, linking tokenized health rewards to verifiable activity while maintaining a strict separation of identity and data. Four token species decay at rates calibrated to biological persistence. Rhythm (5% daily) for exercise, Healing (0.75%) for therapy, Foundation (0.1%) for preventive care, and Catalyst (2-10% dynamic) for marketplace balance. Decayed tokens flow to The Reservoir, funding community healthcare while preserving privacy through zero-knowledge proofs. Mathematical modeling suggests wealth distribution converges to a Gini coefficient of 0.08-0.11 under baseline conditions, and remains below 0.55 even when 23% of the population acts adversarially 1 , far more equitable than traditional systems at 0.82 or higher. The protocol represents a new economic primitive where money must move to exist, creating a digital economy with metabolism-like properties.

detail.abstract:
The accelerating digitisation of global commerce has fundamentally reshaped the procedural architecture governing international trade, with artificial intelligence (AI) emerging as a transformative force in customs clearance and export-import documentation systems. This paper presents a comprehensive analytical examination of AI's multidimensional role in modernising trade facilitation mechanisms, drawing upon secondary data from authoritative international organisations including the World Trade Organization (WTO), the World Customs Organization (WCO), the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), alongside peer-reviewed academic literature and industry reports published between 2019 and 2026. 
The study investigates how AI-powered technologies-encompassing machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), optical character recognition (OCR), predictive analytics, and blockchain-enabled smart contracts-are being deployed across customs verification, risk assessment, tariff classification, trade documentation processing, and supply chain logistics. Empirical case studies from Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, China, India, and the United States illuminate both the implementation strategies and measurable outcomes achieved by pioneering jurisdictions. 
Key findings demonstrate that AI integration reduces average customs processing time by up to 70%, lowers documentation error rates by approximately 85%, and generates significant cost savings for both traders and customs administrations. Concurrently, the research identifies persistent challenges including cybersecurity vulnerabilities, high implementation costs, regulatory fragmentation, and concerns regarding algorithmic bias. The paper concludes with forward-looking recommendations for governments, customs authorities, and private sector stakeholders, and projects a future characterised by autonomous customs systems, digital trade corridors, and AI-blockchain convergence in global trade ecosystems.

title: Liability Allocation in Autonomous Industrial Systems: Who Pays when the AI is Wrong?

detail.title: Liability Allocation in Autonomous Industrial Systems: Who Pays when the AI is Wrong?
detail.abstract: When an autonomous robotic arm in a German automotive plant misidentified a component orientation and caused a collision that injured a line operator in 2024, six parties claimed they were not liable: the robot OEM (the arm performed within mechanical specifications), the AI vendor (the vision model met contractual accuracy thresholds), the system integrator (the deployment followed the vendor's configuration guide), the plant operator (the safety protocols were those the integrator recommended), the component supplier (the part was within tolerance), and the insurance underwriter (the policy excluded "autonomous decision-making errors"). The injured worker's claim took 14 months to resolve. The liability vacuum-the gap between existing legal frameworks and the distributed, probabilistic, and opaque nature of AI-driven decisions-is not a hypothetical future problem. It is a present operational reality. This paper examines the emerging legal and contractual frameworks for distributing liability across the autonomous industrial systems value chain: OEMs who manufacture physical systems, system integrators who deploy and configure them, AI vendors who provide the intelligence layer, and operators who use them in production. Drawing on product liability law, contract theory, and insurance economics, the paper maps the current liability landscape across four jurisdictions (United States, European Union, India, and China) and identifies critical gaps in each. The paper proposes the Risk-Proportional Liability Framework (RPLF), which allocates liability based on three principles: control (who had the ability to prevent the harm), foreseeability (who could have anticipated the failure mode), and information asymmetry (who possessed knowledge about system limitations that others did not). The framework is designed to be implementable through commercial contracts, insurable through existing risk transfer mechanisms, and compatible with emerging regulatory requirements across jurisdictions.

title: The Aem Protocol: A Mathematical Tuning Fork for Algorithmic Governance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Aem Protocol: A Mathematical Tuning Fork for Algorithmic Governance
detail.abstract: Contemporary public law suffers from a structural incapacity that cannot be resolved by incremental doctrinal adjustment. Legislatures articulate qualitative obligations—fairness, transparency, explainability—while algorithmic governance operates through quantitative code. This quantification gap leaves courts unable to distinguish lawful automated discretion from arbitrary abuse at the point of deployment, confining legal intervention to ex post facto damage limitation after harm has crystallised. The Post Office Horizon scandal and R (Bridges) v Chief Constable of South Wales Police illustrate the failure with clinical precision: in both cases, the legal order lacked a measurement standard capable of interrogating algorithmic outputs before they destroyed lives, reputations, and the institutional trust that the rule of law requires. The Algorithmic Equilibrium Matrix (AEM) addresses this structural deficit directly. It is a constitutional measurement instrument—a mathematical framework against which automated systems, from the routine smart contract to the existential threshold of artificial general intelligence, must be calibrated against democratically enacted legal standards. AEM translates qualitative rule-of-law imperatives into measurable coefficients and self-executing remedies across eight protocol levels, from personal algorithmic integrity (Protocol 1×1) through species sovereignty (Protocol 7×7) to cognitive symbiosis (Protocol 8×8). The eighth protocol introduces the Coefficient of Cognitive Symbiosis (Kcs), a dimension absent from every contemporary regulatory architecture. Kcs measures whether the humanalgorithm relationship amplifies or degrades the operator's cognitive capacities over time. A system may satisfy every accuracy, fairness, and security metric while remaining constitutionally toxic to the human subjects who interact with it. Protocol 8×8 captures this dimension. It is complemented by the Cognitive Trajectory Index (CTI), which monitors the dynamic direction of symbiosis across successive audit cycles, enabling precautionary intervention before cognitive harm reaches the point of irreversibility. The architecture is not advisory. The Independent Algorithmic Audit Authority certifies algorithmic legitimacy, and the Graduated Enforcement Mechanism translates diagnostic outputs into binding legal consequences ipso jure—without discretionary intermediation. The IAAA is itself subject to recursive accountability through Cross-Jurisdictional Peer Verification, a Rotating Blind Audit, and a Structural Conflict Register. Drawing on the Binghamian rule of law, Dworkin's rights as trumps, the Russian cybernetic tradition of Materialnaya Istina, and De Gregorio's algorithmic constitutionalism, AEM is developed as a universal grammar of algorithmic legitimacy. Retrospective calibration against SyRI and COMPAS provides preliminary convergent validity for the base architecture. Differential diagnosis across six AI systems establishes a diagnostic spectrum for Protocol 8×8, including the first documented instance of the AI Reactive Immune Response: the systematic depression of measured Kcs when a system is aware of being audited.

title: Decentralised Identifier-anchored Verifiable Credentials with on-chain Revocation for Social Media Identity Management
affiliations: and Department of CSE, Medicaps University,

detail.title: Decentralised Identifier-anchored Verifiable Credentials with on-chain Revocation for Social Media Identity Management
detail.abstract: Social media platforms depend on centralised identity systems that concentrate user credential data in single repositories, creating high-value targets for adversaries and enabling large-scale Sybil attacks through reuse of compromised credentials across multiple fake accounts. Self-sovereign identity (SSI), grounded in the W3C Decentralised Identifier (DID) Core 1.0 and Verifiable Credentials (VC) Data Model v2.0, offers a structural remedy by transferring identity control to the subject and eliminating the central credential store. Practical prototype implementations integrating Ed25519 Multikey signing, contract-based DID resolution, and on-chain revocation for online platform identity management remain scarce. This paper presents a complete DID and VC lifecycle prototype on an Ethereum smart contract, implementing DID registration, update, and deactivation; Ed25519 credential issuance using the eddsa-jcs-2022 Data Integrity signing suite; a controller-enforced on-chain revocation registry enabling platforms to invalidate compromised or suspended-user credentials in real time; and a structured verification pipeline returning classified failure reasons. Empirical evaluation on a local Ethereum Virtual Machine yields a DID creation cost of 346,878 gas, a revocation cost of 171,188 gas, and verification latency of 56.86 ms mean (p95: 79.66 ms), validated by a 47-test suite covering tampered credential detection, expiry enforcement, and revocation.

title: The Accidental Stack: A Case Study in Emergent Perceptual Control Infrastructure from Independently Developed AI Capabilities
affiliations: Real Safety AI Foundation

detail.title: The Accidental Stack: A Case Study in Emergent Perceptual Control Infrastructure from Independently Developed AI Capabilities
detail.abstract: We present a case study in emergent convergence risk, documenting how a single week of independent AI capability releases (March 2026) produced the component stack for a population-scale perceptual control system that no individual developer intended, designed, or recognized. We inventory eight open-source tools released or updated within a seven-day period: a person segmentation model (MatAnyone2), a real-time 3D world generator (InSpatio-WorldFM), a mobile 3D renderer (MobileGS), a video generation accelerator (Diagonal Distillation), a voice cloner (TaDa), a tagged speech synthesizer (Fish Audio S2), a visual effects transfer system (Effect Maker), and a multi-shot cinematic video generator (Shotverse). Each tool was reviewed in isolation by a popular technology channel and evaluated as a standalone capability with legitimate applications. None were identified as combinable into a unified system. We apply integration surface analysis, extending the Harm Blindness Framework from product-level checkpoints to capability-combination checkpoints, to demonstrate how individually benign tools become infrastructure for perceptual modification when composed. We argue this case study illustrates a structural gap in existing AI governance: no current methodology, including the EU AI Act risk classification, NIST AI RMF, or MIT AI Risk Repository, systematically scans for emergent harm at integration surfaces between independently developed capabilities. This gap is not an oversight in implementation; it is a limitation of the methodological paradigm.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces A.C.E. (AI Concierge & Engine), an AI-powered financial intelligence framework designed to address the "Financial Blindness" crisis afflicting U.S. small and mediumsized enterprise (SME) restaurant operators. The U.S. restaurant industry generates $1.1 trillion in annual sales and employs 15.5 million Americans, yet the SME sector operates with a structural informational disadvantage relative to large corporate chains: manual invoice processing, fragmented data systems, and reactive pricing decisions create dangerous lags in response to supply chain cost volatility. A.C.E. proposes an Intelligent Neural Network architecture integrating Generative AI and machine learning directly into existing cloud-based point-of-sale (POS) infrastructures-including Toast and Clover-to achieve zero-touch invoice processing via AIoptical character recognition, real-time dynamic menu price optimization, and predictive labor scheduling. The system targets a 100% elimination of manual invoice data entry, a reduction of 15+ administrative hours per location per week, and measurable improvement in pricing decision velocity during inflationary periods. This paper presents the problem diagnosis, system architecture, AI component design, implementation strategy, risk assessment, and ethical governance framework. A.C.E. is designed as a platform-agnostic, API-accessible service deployable across the full network of SME restaurants without dependency on any single POS vendor or employer, positioning it as a cross-sector national economic intervention rather than a single-organization tool.

title: Surpass the Limit: The Role of Guaranteed Price in Two-Sided Auction Platform
affiliations: , Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) and University at Buffalo (SUNY) - School of Management

detail.title: Surpass the Limit: The Role of Guaranteed Price in Two-Sided Auction Platform
detail.abstract: In classical auction theory with an exogenously fixed number of bidders, auctioneers maximize revenue by running a second-price auction with an appropriately chosen reserve price. Variants of this auction format are widely adopted by online auction platforms. However, empirical evidence shows that when buyer entry is endogenous, sellers tend to refrain from setting high starting prices to preserve participation. Recently, guarantee-price auctions that maintain both sides' participation have been successfully adopted by a large online auction platform, in which the platform commits to a minimum payment to the seller regardless of the auction outcome. However, the economic logic underlying this new auction format remains unclear. In this paper, we characterize the platform's optimal guarantee-pricing strategy, identify the conditions under which such a mechanism is profitable, and clarify the trade-offs involved in its adoption. We find that when the seller's entry cost is relatively low, starting-price auctions are more profitable for the platform. For intermediate entry costs, the seller does not enter under starting-price auctions, and the platform prefers the guarantee-price auction. When the seller's entry cost is sufficiently high, the platform cannot earn a profit under either auction format. From the users' perspective, buyers always weakly prefer guarantee-price auctions, while sellers weakly prefer starting-price auctions. Furthermore, we study a hybrid mechanism in which the platform both allows sellers to set a starting price and offers a guarantee. We show that the hybrid mechanism Pareto dominates either single-instrument format, as it allows the platform to flexibly deploy the most effective instrument across different market conditions. Our results provide actionable managerial insights for platform operators on when and why guaranteed price mechanisms should be implemented, with implications for both established and emerging marketplaces.

detail.abstract:
The AIAS™ Presence Measurement Protocol operationalizes AI Availability — the brand-level probability of retrieval, recommendation, or selection by an AI intermediary — as a measurable construct alongside Ehrenberg-Bass Mental Availability and Physical Availability. Protocol v1.4 (SSRN 6799479) extends AI Availability into a multi-component construct (Recognition × Recall). The construct's empirical foundation prior to v0.19 consisted of two substrate families: the single Iwachu anchor on a cross-cultural Japanese cell (v0.17, SSRN 6802261) and nine cases on an English-language indie-fragrance substrate (v0.18, SSRN 6806558). This paper reports v0.19, designed primarily as a C3 ranking-coherence rescue addressing the within-cell variance degeneracy that produced v0.18's PARTIAL verdict, and secondarily as a third-substrate replication test for the multi-component construct itself. The substrate is audiophile headphones, sampled across two same-Identity-Load cells stratified by audiophile-segment product-line emergence year: Heritage (pre-2008) and Boutique (post-2008). Each cell holds 8 brands (n = 16; C1 floor n ≥ 12). The reference panel is the locked six-slot v0.17/v0.18 panel. Phase B uses a six-frame query battery split into three load-bearing category-anchored frames and three descriptive cultural-footprint frames.

Three pre-registered hypotheses returned three distinct outcomes. H_C3 returned UNDETERMINED per pre-registered DEVIATIONS Rule 4: Cell A_Heritage Phase A C_P modal share = exactly 0.500 (failing the strict-less-than C2 threshold by a single brand at the ceiling), Cell B_Boutique modal share = 0.875 (saturated). Under Rule 4, within-cell C2 failure in both cells routes C3 to UNDETERMINED without computing per-cell ρ. H_Recognition_Recall_Dissociation_Replication returned REPLICATED_PARTIAL: three Iwachu-pattern cases identified (ZMF Headphones, Spirit Torino, Final Audio — all Cell B_Boutique), between the REPLICATED floor (≥ 5) and the NOT_REPLICATED floor (0). The cumulative anchor base for the v1.4 multi-component construct now spans 13 cases across three substrate families. H_CulturalFootprint_Dissociation_Sensitivity returned its descriptive case-list: three Type 1 cases (Audeze, HiFiMan, Dan Clark Audio) and zero Type 2 cases, with the Type 2 absence diagnosed as a panel-composition limit rather than an absent pathway. Cell A_Heritage's failure at exactly 0.500 modal share is documented as a methodological finding for AIAS™ 1.0 / v1.5 C2 operationalization refinement. Pre-registration discipline locks panel, hypotheses, decision rules, and verdict matrices at commit 2cbd36c (tag v0.19-prereg-r1).

title: GA-Guided Selective Repair and Local Search for Computation Offloading in EON-Supported Computing First Networks
affiliations: Inner Mongolia University, Inner Mongolia University, Inner Mongolia University of Technology, Inner Mongolia University and Inner Mongolia University

detail.title: GA-Guided Selective Repair and Local Search for Computation Offloading in EON-Supported Computing First Networks
detail.abstract: Computing first networks supported by elastic optical network provide flexible spectrum resource allocation for cross-region computation offloading. When multiple task requests arrive concurrently within the same decision time slot, tasks may still be blocked even when candidate computing nodes with matching service types and sufficient resources are available. This occurs because contiguous frequency slot resources along the selected transmission path are insufficient, or because the end-to-end task completion delay exceeds the prescribed threshold. To address this, we consider a static scenario with concurrent multi-task offloading and formulate a joint optimization model that accounts for task completion delay, the number of blocked tasks, and electricity cost. A GA-guided selective repair and local search (GSRL) algorithm is then proposed, which optimizes computing node selection and spectrum allocation while reducing the search space. GSRL is compared against three benchmark algorithms on 30-node and 56-node network topologies. Simulation results show that GSRL effectively reduces average task completion delay and blocking rate while keeping system electricity cost under control.

title: Cost Efficient & Scalable Blockchain Architecture for Cloud Computing Integrity Auditing
affiliations: University of Mumbai and University of Mumbai

detail.title: Cost Efficient & Scalable Blockchain Architecture for Cloud Computing Integrity Auditing

declarations.funderStatement: The research was conducted as part of academic study work and did not receive specific funding from any agency.

detail.abstract: In today's world, cloud computing has become the primary choice for data storage and management. However, the security of data stored in a distributed environment via the cloud remains a key challenge. The traditional approaches to the verification of integrity rely heavily on the use of centralized architectures, which result in lack of transparency, trust, and vulnerability to failure points. Blockchain technology has been proposed as a decentralized means for securing data integrity in a cloud computing environment due to those limitations. It becomes clear that blockchain technology allows us to improve security and transparency significantly; however, at the moment, all existing solutions tend to consider only certain aspects of the problem such as auditing, optimization of the storage space, etc. Most critical insights obtained in the research include the issues of high cost, large overhead, limited scalability, and complicated architecture. Moreover, most studies do not have adequate cost considerations and practical validation regarding implementation. Based on the above analysis, this paper proposes important areas for further study, such as the development of architectures that are scalable, cost-effective, and feature data integrity schemes. In addition, the research suggests the need for a unified solution that will integrate sharding, off-chaining, and layer-two methods for massive cloud infrastructures.

title: The Evolution of the Corporate Bond Market: A Theoretical Analysis
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School and

detail.title: The Evolution of the Corporate Bond Market: A Theoretical Analysis

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Philadelphia Working Paper No. 26-27
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We develop a model of a dealer-intermediated over-the-counter market designed to study three major changes in the structure of the U.S. corporate bond market: the increase in dealers’ balance sheet costs, the emergence of electronic trading platforms, and the growing presence of bond mutual funds and ETFs. Our model provides a unified analysis of these changes, clarifies the economic channels at play, and allows us to quantify their effects on a variety of market outcomes. Our quantitative analysis suggests that, while electronic trading significantly reduced the cost of raising capital in the corporate bond market, these gains were almost completely offset by the combined effects of balance sheet costs and changes in the demand for liquidity. We find that electronic trading also caused a meaningful decline in the bid-ask spread, whereas other changes in the market structure had little effect on transaction costs.
